bill_summary: This bill establishes the Gambling Prevention Technology Pilot Program within the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to address and mitigate problem gambling on the campuses of Bowie State University and Morgan State University. It requires the implementation of geofencing technology to prevent access to online sports wagering platforms within designated campus 'no gambling zones' and mandates a report on the program's effectiveness by 2031.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: Students at Bowie State University and Morgan State University, online sports wagering operators, and the Maryland Center of Excellence on Problem Gambling.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $90,600 in FY 2027, with annual expenditures between $59,700 and $114,500 through FY 2031 to support a contractual program manager. Revenues from sports wagering are not expected to be materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Gambling Prevention Technology Pilot Program within the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission (SLGCC), which is part of this agency. The agency is responsible for implementing the program, collaborating with universities, monitoring online sports wagering, and reporting findings to the Governor.

Morgan State University is explicitly named as a mandatory participant in the Pilot Program. It must collaborate with the SLGCC to designate 'no gambling zones' on campus, develop signage, and implement technology to monitor and prevent online gambling.

Bowie State University, a member of the University System of Maryland, is a named mandatory participant in the Pilot Program. Additionally, the Maryland Center of Excellence on Problem Gambling, which is a mandated collaborator, is housed within the University of Maryland School of Medicine, also a member of USM.

The Department of Health funds the Maryland Center of Excellence on Problem Gambling (a required collaborator for the pilot) through the Problem Gambling Fund, which it administers. The pilot's goal of mitigating problem gambling directly aligns with MDH's mission to manage behavioral health and substance use disorders.

The fiscal note indicates a need for general fund expenditures to hire a contractual program manager at SLGCA to oversee the pilot program. DBM oversees the state’s personnel system and annual operating budget, including these types of personnel and funding requests.

The SLGCC is required to submit a report on the pilot program's findings and the effectiveness of geofencing technology to the Governor by January 1, 2031. The office also oversees the SLGCA as an executive agency.

As the state's coordinating board for higher education, MHEC establishes statewide policies and long-range planning for colleges and universities. The implementation of a gambling prevention pilot program on campuses impacts student welfare and campus policy, which falls under MHEC's broad regulatory oversight.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission on State and Local Government Real Property Bearing Confederate Names to develop and implement a framework to identify real property owned by the State or a political subdivision that bears a Confederate name; and requiring the Commission to make recommendations regarding the real property that should be renamed and report its findings to the Governor, the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City, the governing body of each county, and the General Assembly by October 1, 2033.
Title: Commission on State and Local Government Real Property Bearing Confederate Names - Establishment
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Commission on State and Local Government Real Property Bearing Confederate Names as an independent unit of the State's executive branch. The commission is tasked with identifying real property owned by the State or local governments, such as streets and parks, that bear names associated with the Confederacy and providing recommendations for their renaming by October 1, 2033.
responsible_party: Commission on State and Local Government Real Property Bearing Confederate Names
stakeholders: Maryland residents, local government entities including counties and municipalities, school districts, and the Maryland State Archives.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will increase State expenditures to provide travel reimbursement for the 24 commission members and to hire a dedicated archivist at the Maryland State Archives. The commission is authorized to seek and accept external funding from federal, private, or foundation sources, which could impact State revenues. While the commission makes recommendations, it does not have the authority to mandate or fund the actual renaming of property, which would be at the discretion and cost of the owning entity.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is responsible for appointing all 24 members of the Commission, with the advice and consent of the Senate, and is one of the recipients of the Commission's final report.
The bill mandates that the Commission hire an archivist who must be an employee of the Maryland State Archives to assist with the Commission's research and identification tasks.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new independent commission within the executive branch, which falls under this category of government entities.
This office is responsible for vetting and recruiting candidates for the 24 member positions (one from each county) that the Governor must appoint.
The bill explicitly subjects the Commission's funds, including gifts and private donations, to audit by the Legislative Auditor.

As the agency responsible for the maintenance and management of state-owned facilities and real estate, DGS records will be central to the Commission's task of identifying property with Confederate names.
The Commission is tasked with identifying Confederate names on state parks and public lands, which are managed and inventoried by the DNR.
The bill's definition of real property includes streets, many of which are managed by MDOT business units, requiring coordination to identify relevant naming data.
DBM will oversee the fiscal and personnel aspects of establishing the new commission, including the archivist's employment and member travel reimbursements.
Through the Maryland Historical Trust, the Department of Planning provides expertise in the state's historical sites and names, which is relevant to the Commission's research.
The OAG will serve as the legal advisor to the new Commission regarding its framework for identifying property and the legal implications of its renaming recommendations.
The Comptroller's office will manage the payroll for the Commission's archivist and provide general fiscal oversight for the new unit.
The Treasurer would act as the custodian for any private funds, gifts, or grants the Commission receives and manages.
The Commission's scope includes identifying property owned by school districts, which are supervised by the State Department of Education.
USM institutions own and manage significant state real property, including buildings and streets, which the Commission is mandated to review.

Synopsis: Repealing a provision that authorizes a local department of social services to ask the juvenile court to find that reasonable efforts to reunify a child with the child's parent or guardian are not required if the local department concludes that a parent or guardian has involuntarily lost parental rights to a sibling of the child; and repealing the authorization for a juvenile court to waive a local department's obligation to provide certain services if a parent has involuntarily lost certain parental rights.
Title: Family Law - Children in Need of Assistance and Termination of Parental Rights (Right to Fight Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/29 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: The Right to Fight Act repeals provisions that allow a local department of social services to request that a juvenile court waive the requirement for reasonable reunification efforts if a parent or guardian has involuntarily lost parental rights to a sibling of the child. It also removes the juvenile court's authority to waive the local department's obligation to provide services in such cases.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services and the Juvenile Court
stakeholders: Children in Need of Assistance (CINA), parents or guardians who have previously lost parental rights to a sibling, and local departments of social services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by approximately $300,000 annually as the Department of Human Services (DHS) will provide services and reunification efforts in cases previously eligible for waivers. This may result in longer case resolutions and increased costs for case management, care stipends, and specific treatments (e.g., parenting classes, therapy). Local government operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Human Services (DHS) as it regulates the 'local department of social services,' which are under DHS jurisdiction. It repeals their authority to request that juvenile courts waive reunification efforts for children whose parents previously lost rights to a sibling. The fiscal note explicitly identifies DHS as having a potential $300,000 annual expenditure increase due to this change.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, changing the standards for juvenile court findings and the authorization for judges to waive service obligations. The AOC supports the judiciary in managing the infrastructure and policies impacted by these procedural changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent residents in parental rights and juvenile delinquency proceedings. By requiring 'reasonable efforts' for reunification in more cases, the agency will see an increased workload in providing effective counsel throughout longer and more complex family law proceedings.

The Governor's Office for Children leads a 'whole-of-government' approach to child well-being and family poverty. This bill represents a significant shift in family law policy regarding child welfare and reunification, which falls under the office's mandate for policy coordination.

The OAG serves as the primary legal advisor and representative for state agencies, including the Department of Human Services. This bill changes the legal standards OAG attorneys must navigate when representing local departments in juvenile court hearings.

The fiscal note identifies a notable increase in general fund expenditures ($300,000 annually) for DHS. DBM is responsible for the formulation and oversight of the state's budget and would be involved in allocating these additional resources.

Synopsis: Requiring that an abortion be performed by a physician, rather than a qualified provider; repealing certain provisions of law related to State interference with an abortion, regulations related to abortion, and liability or criminal punishment for qualified providers who perform an abortion; prohibiting a physician from knowingly performing, inducing, or attempting to perform or induce an abortion under certain circumstances and subject to certain exceptions; etc.
Title: Public Health - Abortion (Heartbeat Bill)
Status: In the House - First Reading Health

bill_summary: The bill, known as the 'Heartbeat Bill,' prohibits physicians from performing abortions if a fetal heartbeat is detected, except in cases of medical emergency. It requires physicians to perform a sonogram, offer the patient the chance to view the images and hear the heartbeat, and provide specific medical and support information at least 24 hours before a procedure. Enforcement is handled exclusively through private civil actions, allowing individuals to sue those who perform or assist in a prohibited abortion for statutory damages of at least $10,000 per violation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland State Judiciary
stakeholders: Pregnant women, physicians, healthcare providers, insurance companies, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's heartbeat requirements are enforced exclusively through private civil actions, preventing direct state or local enforcement expenditures. However, the state court system may see an increased caseload due to these private lawsuits. The Maryland Department of Health will incur administrative costs to develop and distribute required printed materials and maintain a website for alternative pregnancy services. The bill also establishes joint and several liability for costs and attorney's fees for parties unsuccessfully challenging abortion restrictions in court.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health - General Article and defines the Maryland Department of Health as the 'Department' responsible for creating and providing printed materials and maintaining a website regarding abortion alternatives and medical risks. It also changes the definition of who may perform abortions in the state, which falls under MDH's regulatory scope.

The bill creates extensive legal frameworks regarding sovereign, governmental, and official immunity for the state, and establishes fee-shifting rules for constitutional challenges. The OAG, as the state's chief legal advisor and representative in court, would be responsible for defending these provisions and the state's interests in anticipated litigation.

The bill mandates that enforcement occur 'exclusively through private civil actions,' creating a new class of litigation. It specifies venue requirements, limits transfers between counties, mandates statutory damages of at least $10,000, and prohibits courts from awarding attorney's fees to defendants, all of which directly impact judicial administration and court operations.

As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and other agencies affected by this major policy change. The Governor is also responsible for signing or vetoing this landmark legislation which significantly alters reproductive health laws in Maryland.

The bill defines 'aiding and abetting' to include paying for or reimbursing the costs of an abortion through insurance. This creates potential civil liability for insurers regulated by the MIA and could lead to significant changes in insurance policy forms and rate filings in the state.

The bill requires the Department of Health to produce physical and digital materials and maintain a specialized website. DBM would oversee the fiscal allocation and personnel resources required for the executive branch to implement these new mandates.

The bill contains provisions aimed at limiting taxpayer funding for individuals or entities that perform or promote abortions. The BPW, which approves significant state contracts and expenditures, would be relevant to ensuring state procurement and funding align with these restrictions.

As the state's fiscal watchdog and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is relevant to the bill's provisions regarding the restriction of taxpayer funds and the monitoring of state revenues and expenditures related to the new mandates.

Synopsis: Proposing a Constitutional Amendment requiring that a special election be held at the same time as the regular statewide primary and general elections that are held in the second year of a term to fill a vacancy in the office of Delegate or Senator in the General Assembly if the vacancy occurs on or before the date that is 55 days before the deadline for filing certificates of candidacy for the regular statewide election that is held in the second year of the term.
Title: General Assembly - Special Election to Fill a Vacancy in Office
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This proposed constitutional amendment requires a special election to be held to fill a vacancy in the office of State Senator or Delegate in the General Assembly if the vacancy occurs on or before a specific date (55 days before the candidacy filing deadline for the regular statewide election in the second year of the term). The special election is to be held concurrently with the regular statewide primary and general elections in that second year. Until a successor is elected, the Governor fills the vacancy via appointment. If the vacancy occurs after the specified deadline, the gubernatorial appointee serves the remainder of the four-year term.
responsible_party: Governor of Maryland and the Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Voters in Maryland, candidates for the General Assembly, and political party central committees.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures may increase minimally to cover costs related to additional ballot styles, printing, and programming for special elections held at the same time as regular elections. However, the Department of Legislative Services estimates these costs can be absorbed within existing resources. There is no effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the independent agency responsible for managing and supervising all elections in Maryland, the State Board of Elections is the primary entity that will implement the special election requirements for General Assembly vacancies as mandated by this constitutional amendment.

The bill directly involves the Governor’s constitutional duties to appoint individuals to fill vacancies and issue proclamations declaring special primary and general elections for the General Assembly.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the legal advisor to the Governor and the General Assembly. They would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the proposed constitutional amendment and drafting the ballot language for the 2026 general election.

The Secretary of State performs administrative and certification duties for official state documents, including amendments to the Maryland Constitution and certain official acts related to state records.

As the central depository for government records, the Archives is responsible for preserving permanent records of legislative and executive actions, including the formal records of this constitutional amendment and the resulting special election proclamations.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Digital Asset Reserve Fund to serve as a reserve asset for the State through the investment of cryptocurrency; and authorizing the State Treasurer to invest the funds obtained by the State through the enforcement of certain gambling violations into cryptocurrency.
Title: Strategic Digital Asset Reserve Act of Maryland
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 1:30 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill creates the Maryland Digital Asset Reserve Fund, a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the State Treasurer. The fund is designed to serve as a reserve asset for the State by investing in cryptocurrency, specifically decentralized digital assets with a market capitalization of at least $500 billion. The fund's primary revenue source is money seized and forfeited to the State from specific gambling violations, though it may also receive budget appropriations and interest earnings.
stakeholders: The State of Maryland, the Maryland State Treasurer's Office, and individuals subject to asset seizure for illegal gambling violations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances because the primary intended funding source—proceeds from illegal gambling seizures—is typically handled by federal authorities rather than the State. No funding is provided in the fiscal 2027 budget. If the fund is utilized, the State Treasurer may incur a one-time cost of approximately $10,000 for a specialized custodian and annual management fees of 3% to 5% of assets. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer is the primary administrator of the Maryland Digital Asset Reserve Fund, responsible for investing the fund in cryptocurrency, maintaining a secure storage platform, and selecting qualified custodians for the state's digital assets.

The Comptroller is explicitly tasked by the bill to account for the Maryland Digital Asset Reserve Fund and ensure that interest earnings are properly credited to the special fund rather than the General Fund.

As the state's primary law enforcement authority, the Maryland State Police are responsible for the investigation and seizure of money from gambling violations that provide the initial revenue source for the new reserve fund.
The Office of the Attorney General serves as the legal advisor to the State Treasurer and would handle the legal processes surrounding the forfeiture of seized gambling funds to the State.

The bill requires that all expenditures from the Maryland Digital Asset Reserve Fund be made in accordance with the state budget, which is overseen and managed by the Department of Budget and Management.

The Office of Legislative Audits is responsible for auditing all executive branch agencies and would be required to review the fiscal compliance and management of the newly created cryptocurrency fund and its related assets.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch's fiscal policy and the drafting of the annual budget, which must include any proposed expenditures or transfers from this new special fund.

The Board of Public Works, which includes the Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer, oversees major state expenditures and would likely review and approve the procurement of the specialized custodial services needed to safeguard digital assets.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections to provide a toll-free voter hotline for incarcerated individuals to receive information about voting, request election-related materials, and report voting rights violations; and altering the circumstances under which an individual is not qualified to be a registered voter for the purpose of allowing individuals convicted of a felony and serving a court-ordered sentence of imprisonment for the conviction to register to vote.
Title: Election Law - Incarcerated Individuals - Voter Hotline and Voting Eligibility (Voting Rights for All Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: The Voting Rights for All Act restores voting rights to individuals serving court-ordered sentences of imprisonment for felony convictions. The bill requires the State Board of Elections to establish a toll-free hotline for incarcerated individuals to access voting information and materials and report violations. Additionally, it removes the mandate for court clerks to report felony convictions to election officials and repeals criminal penalties associated with voting while serving a felony sentence.
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals serving sentences for felony convictions, State Board of Elections, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The provided text does not include the official Fiscal Note. However, implementation of the bill's requirements, specifically the creation of a toll-free voter hotline and the management of registration and voting for incarcerated individuals, would likely increase state expenditures for the State Board of Elections and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the State Board of Elections as the primary agency responsible for providing a toll-free voter hotline for incarcerated individuals, adopting regulations for its administration, and managing the registration of individuals previously ineligible due to felony convictions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Board of Elections to collaborate with the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to adopt regulations for the voter hotline. Furthermore, the agency oversees the correctional facilities and the population impacted by the change in voting eligibility.

The bill repeals existing requirements for the clerks of the circuit court and district court to report felony convictions and commitment papers to the State Administrator, which directly alters the administrative reporting duties of the Judiciary's support infrastructure.

As the legal advisor to both the State Board of Elections and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, the OAG would be responsible for interpreting the legal changes to voting eligibility and assisting in the drafting of new regulations required by the bill.

The bill requires the establishment of a new toll-free voter hotline and the processing of new voter registrations, which will have a fiscal impact on the state budget that must be overseen and managed by DBM.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the agencies implementing this bill and is responsible for the overall policy direction regarding voting rights and criminal justice reform in Maryland.

Synopsis: Altering an exception to the prohibition against the possession of certain nondomesticated animals in the State by reducing from 10 days to 48 hours the amount of time a nonresident may travel through the State with an otherwise prohibited animal; repealing the exception to the prohibition against the possession by a person with certain disabilities of certain nondomesticated animals for a certain purpose; etc.
Title: Criminal Law – Nondomesticated Animal Prohibitions – Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk

bill_summary: This bill expands the list of prohibited nondomesticated animals in Maryland to include zebras, kangaroos, wallaroos, and wallabies, banning their import, sale, possession, and breeding. It shortens the period a nonresident traveling through the state can possess such animals from 10 days to 48 hours and repeals the exception that allowed individuals with severe mobility-limiting disabilities to use nondomesticated animals as assistance animals. A grandfather clause allows current owners of the newly listed animals to keep them if they notify local animal control by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Local animal control authorities and State and local law enforcement officers
stakeholders: Current and prospective owners of zebras, kangaroos, wallaroos, and wallabies; nonresidents traveling through Maryland with prohibited animals; and individuals with severe mobility disabilities who use assistance animals.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. Enforcement is handled by existing law enforcement and animal control structures. Violations are misdemeanors carrying fines of up to $1,000 for individuals and $10,000 for entities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically references the Department of Natural Resources as the authority for issuing licenses or permits that provide an exception to the prohibitions on importing, selling, or possessing the listed nondomesticated animals.

The bill repeals an existing exception that allows individuals with disabilities that severely limit mobility to possess certain nondomesticated animals as assistance animals, which directly impacts the rights and services for the department's constituency.
The Maryland State Police, as the primary statewide law enforcement agency, has the authority to enforce the criminal prohibitions and misdemeanor penalties established or altered by this bill.
The bill alters criminal law and creates new misdemeanor conditions related to the possession and trade of animals, which will impact judicial caseloads and court administration.
The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor for state agencies and manages criminal appeals; it would be involved in interpreting the revised criminal statute and supporting enforcement efforts.

The Department of Agriculture is responsible for animal health and monitoring animal diseases in Maryland. Prohibiting the importation and possession of kangaroos, zebras, and other species relates to their regulatory interest in animal health and the state's agricultural environment.
The Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation passed by the General Assembly, including changes to the state's criminal code regarding animal welfare.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Restructuring Maryland's Electric Utility Industry to study and make recommendations on restructuring the State's electric utility industry; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly on or before November 1, 2027.
Title: Task Force to Study Restructuring Maryland's Electric Utility Industry
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Task Force to Study Restructuring Maryland's Electric Utility Industry. The task force is charged with studying various options for restructuring the state's electric utility industry, including publicly owned utilities and cooperatives, evaluating electricity rates, analyzing the legal implications of public ownership of utility assets, and examining options for energy market participation such as withdrawing from PJM Interconnection, LLC.
stakeholders: Maryland electric utility companies (investor-owned, cooperative, and municipal), Maryland electricity ratepayers, PJM Interconnection, LLC, independent electricity generation companies, and state agencies including the Department of the Environment and the Maryland Energy Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission (PSC) increase by approximately $667,000 in FY 2027 and $333,000 in FY 2028 to hire consultants to support the task force. These expenditures are offset by a corresponding increase in special fund revenues from assessments imposed on public service companies. The bill is expected to have no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The PSC is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. The Chair of the PSC must designate the Task Force chair, the PSC must provide administrative staff for the Task Force, and the commission is a named member of the body. Furthermore, the fiscal note indicates a $1 million special fund impact on the PSC to hire consultants to support the study.

The People's Counsel is a named member of the Task Force. The bill’s core mandate—evaluating electricity rates and strategies for ratepayer responsiveness—directly aligns with the OPC's mission to advocate for residential utility consumers.

The Director of MEA is a named member of the Task Force and is specifically responsible for designating an independent electricity generation company representative. The restructuring study directly impacts state energy policy and efficiency goals managed by the MEA.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a specialized Task Force to conduct an in-depth inquiry into electric utility policy and provide formal recommendations to the General Assembly, which is the primary function of this governmental designation.

The Secretary of the Environment is a named member of the Task Force. Restructuring the electric utility industry has significant implications for environmental quality, carbon emission goals, and the state's climate change initiatives overseen by MDE.

The Secretary of Transportation is a named member of the Task Force. Utility infrastructure and restructuring models can affect transportation logistics and the state's broader infrastructure planning missions.

The Task Force is mandated to analyze the legal implications of transferring privately owned electric company assets to public ownership, including the use of eminent domain. The OAG serves as the state’s primary legal advisor for such constitutional and regulatory analyses.

The Governor is responsible for appointing a public representative with industry expertise to the Task Force and the office oversees the executive agencies (PSC, MEA, MDE, MDOT) involved in the study.

The Office of Appointments would be tasked with recruiting and vetting the public expert appointed by the Governor to ensure the candidate reflects the necessary industry expertise and diverse representation required.

DBM is responsible for state fiscal oversight and the budget process. The bill has a notable fiscal impact on special funds and requires travel expense reimbursements to be provided in the state budget.

Synopsis: Applying statewide certain provisions of law authorizing the use of speed monitoring systems in certain residential districts.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Speed Monitoring Systems - Residential Districts
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: This bill expands the authorization to use speed monitoring systems (speed cameras) on highways in residential districts with a maximum posted speed limit of 35 miles per hour to all local jurisdictions in Maryland. Previously, this authority was limited to Anne Arundel, Montgomery, and Prince George’s counties.
responsible_party: Local jurisdictions and their governing bodies
stakeholders: Maryland motorists, local governments, and the District Court of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues from contested District Court cases may increase minimally starting in FY 2027. Local jurisdictions (excluding Anne Arundel, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties) will experience an increase in revenues from speed camera citations and an increase in expenditures related to the installation, administration, and operation of the systems, with net revenues used for authorized safety purposes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Highway Administration is responsible for establishing the traffic engineering practices used to set the speed limits that determine where speed monitoring systems may be placed. The bill also amends sections of law where SHA is specifically authorized to use such systems on certain interstates.

MDOT is the parent agency for the State Highway Administration, Motor Vehicle Administration, and Maryland Transportation Authority, all of which are directly involved in the implementation, regulation, or data support of speed monitoring systems.

The bill expands speed monitoring authority statewide, which is expected to increase the volume of contested citations. The AOC manages the District Court infrastructure and budget impacted by this increased caseload and the resulting general fund revenue.

The MDTA is specifically authorized within the statute amended by this bill to use speed monitoring systems on the Intercounty Connector and other facilities, making it a primary stakeholder in state-level automated enforcement.
The MVA provides the vehicle registration records used by state and local agencies to identify vehicle owners and mail citations for violations recorded by automated speed monitoring systems.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are involved in traffic safety policy and provide support for the administration and oversight of speed monitoring programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the central hub for public safety policy and funding in Maryland, coordinating statewide initiatives to reduce traffic-related fatalities and advising on public safety legislation.
DBM manages the state's revenue estimation and the general fund, which is expected to receive increased revenue from the civil penalties paid in contested District Court cases.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state transportation agencies regarding the enforcement of vehicle laws and would represent the state in any legal challenges related to the expanded use of monitoring systems.

The bill expands automated speed enforcement authority to all local jurisdictions, providing the 18 rural counties represented by the Council with new tools for traffic management and revenue generation.

Synopsis: Requiring that each legislative district established for the purpose of electing members of the House of Delegates consist of three single-member delegate districts; requiring the General Assembly to enact a law establishing and governing a Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention to establish legislative and congressional districts and establishing certain requirements regarding the Redistricting Convention; establishing the Redistricting Convention; etc.
Title: Districting - Single-Member Districts and Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention
Status: In the House - First Reading House Rules and Executive Nominations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to require that Maryland's legislative districts be divided into three single-member delegate districts for House of Delegates elections. It also establishes a 188-member Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention, elected by voters every ten years following the decennial census, to draw state legislative and congressional boundaries. Plans certified by the Convention become law unless they are successfully challenged by the General Assembly and rejected by the Supreme Court of Maryland.
responsible_party: Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention
stakeholders: Maryland voters, candidates for the House of Delegates, the General Assembly, and the Supreme Court of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures will increase to conduct elections for Convention members every ten years and to reimburse those members for travel and standard expenses. The Office of the Attorney General and the Department of Legislative Services will incur costs to staff the Convention, and the Supreme Court of Maryland may face increased expenditures related to judicial reviews and potential special master appointments for redistricting challenges.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill fundamentally alters the Governor's constitutional role by removing the requirement for the Governor to prepare and present legislative redistricting plans to the General Assembly, shifting this authority to a newly established convention.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Office of the Attorney General, jointly with the Department of Legislative Services, shall serve as the staff for the new Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention.

The Board is responsible for determining the election date for the 188 members of the Redistricting Convention and is specifically tasked with apportioning the number of seats for the convention among counties based on census data.

The bill grants the Supreme Court of Maryland original jurisdiction to review districting plans or establish them if the convention fails. As the central support agency for the Judiciary, the AOC would manage the administrative and fiscal impacts of these new legal proceedings and tight judicial timelines.

The Department of Planning is responsible for demographic research used for state initiatives like redistricting; the Redistricting Convention would rely on the data and research managed by this agency to draw legislative and congressional maps.

The bill establishes a new 188-member elected body and entitles members to expense reimbursement, which will require DBM to coordinate funding for the convention's operations and staffing within the state budget.

The bill sets rigorous eligibility standards and prohibitions for convention members (e.g., excluding lobbyists, political party employees, and relatives of officials) to ensure the integrity of the process, falling under the Commission's broad interest in government impartiality and integrity.

As the agency responsible for certifying official state documents and managing the administrative process of constitutional amendments, the Secretary of State is involved in the proclamation of the ratified amendment if approved by voters.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Civic Excellence Program in the State Department of Education; authorizing a local school system to participate in the Program to recognize students who meet criteria related to student proficiency in civics and civic literacy; and requiring the Department, no later than the 2027-2028 school year, to develop guidelines to assist participating local school systems.
Title: Public Schools - Maryland Civic Excellence Program - Established
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/29 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Awards, Medals, and Prizes -see also- Gaming&Gambl; Lottery
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Civic Excellence Program within the Maryland State Department of Education to recognize students and public schools that promote civic readiness and engagement. Local school systems can voluntarily participate in the program by using state-developed guidelines to award a 'Seal of Civic Excellence' to students who demonstrate proficiency in civics and civic literacy.
stakeholders: Public school students, local school systems, and the Maryland State Department of Education.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can develop the required guidelines using existing resources. While local school systems that choose to participate may experience increased expenditures for program administration and awards (such as medals or diploma insignia), these costs are discretionary. The bill has no impact on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Civic Excellence Program within MSDE, tasking the department with its administration, the development of proficiency guidelines for civics and civic literacy, and the oversight of annual reports from participating local school systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is responsible for promoting service and civic innovation to strengthen communities. As the bill focuses on student civic readiness and engagement, this department is a primary stakeholder for consultation on program guidelines and potential collaboration on civic initiatives.

The MLDS Center collects and analyzes student-level records to track educational and workforce outcomes. Attainment of the Seal of Civic Excellence would be a significant educational data point to be incorporated into the longitudinal repository to evaluate student achievement.

The bill explicitly allows for collaboration between local school systems and institutions of higher education. As the state’s coordinating board for colleges and universities, MHEC would likely facilitate these partnerships and oversee how the seal is recognized for postsecondary success.

The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor to MSDE and would be responsible for providing legal counsel during the development of program guidelines and ensuring the implementation of the Maryland Civic Excellence Program adheres to state education laws.

Synopsis: Requiring a county that submits an application to the Secretary of Transportation for funding for certain transportation services for elderly and disabled persons to identify interjurisdictional paratransit service routes between facilities within certain networks of providers in the application; requiring the Secretary to adopt procedures to ensure counties cooperate in establishing interjurisdictional paratransit service routes between facilities within certain networks of providers; etc.
Title: Transportation - Paratransit Services - Interjurisdictional Routes
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland counties applying for state funding for paratransit services to identify and establish interjurisdictional routes connecting counties to specific healthcare provider networks, including Adventist Healthcare, Johns Hopkins Medicine, LifeBridge Health, Luminis Health Maryland, MedStar Health, and the University of Maryland Medical System. The bill mandates that the Secretary of Transportation develop procedures to ensure county cooperation in establishing these routes to better serve the transportation needs of elderly and handicapped residents.
stakeholders: Elderly and handicapped residents of Maryland, Maryland county governments (including Baltimore City), and major healthcare provider networks (Adventist Healthcare, Johns Hopkins Medicine, LifeBridge Health, Luminis Health Maryland, MedStar Health, and University of Maryland Medical System).
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires counties to establish specific interjurisdictional paratransit routes to healthcare networks as a condition for receiving state transportation funding. While specific new funding amounts are not provided, the bill mandates that the Secretary of Transportation identify and allocate existing funds for elderly and handicapped transportation (60 percent distributed equally among counties and 40 percent based on population), and counties must use these funds for equipment or operating costs of the transportation service.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Transportation Article and tasks the Secretary of Transportation with identifying funds, managing the application process for county paratransit grants, and adopting procedures to ensure interjurisdictional cooperation.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Transportation to consult with the Department of Aging regarding fund distribution and enforcement. Additionally, local Area Agencies on Aging (which are overseen by this department) must certify and approve all project applications.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Transportation to consult with the Department of Disabilities on the distribution of funds, the development of application criteria, and the enforcement of paratransit service requirements.

As a division of MDOT, the MTA is responsible for paratransit systems and connecting residents to healthcare. It would likely be the primary unit tasked with overseeing the technical and operational aspects of establishing these interjurisdictional routes.

Synopsis: Requiring certain expedited proceedings in a wrongful detainer action if the property that is the subject of the action is, at the time of the complaint, advertised or listed for sale or lease by the complainant and requiring that notice of a hearing or appeal be served in person or, under certain circumstances, posted conspicuously on the property; requiring the District Court or the circuit court to issue a warrant within 24 hours if the court rules in favor of the complainant in an expedited wrongful detainer action; etc.
Title: Real Property - Expedited Wrongful Detainer Proceedings - Property for Sale or Lease
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m. (Economic Matters)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill establishes expedited legal proceedings for wrongful detainer actions when the property in question is advertised or listed for sale or lease at the time of the complaint. It mandates significantly shorter timeframes for court summons, hearings, judicial rulings, and the issuance and execution of warrants for restitution of possession, and modifies notice and service requirements for such cases.
responsible_party: The Maryland District Court, Maryland circuit courts, and local sheriffs' offices
stakeholders: Property owners and sellers, individuals in possession of real property without legal right (unauthorized occupants), the Maryland Judiciary, and local law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates expedited requirements for the judiciary and local law enforcement, which is expected to increase the administrative and operational workload for the District Court, circuit courts, and sheriffs' offices. While no specific funding amount or mandated appropriation is identified in the bill text, the shortened timelines for hearings, rulings, and warrant executions may result in increased state general fund expenditures and local expenditures to ensure compliance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly impacts the judicial system by establishing specific, expedited timelines for District and Circuit Court hearings, rulings, and the issuance of warrants in wrongful detainer cases. The AOC is responsible for the administrative and financial infrastructure of the court system and would need to manage these new operational requirements.

The OAG serves as the primary legal advisor to the Judiciary and the General Assembly. They would likely review this bill for legal sufficiency and advise on its implications for real property law and consumer protection, especially regarding the expedited removal of occupants from listed properties.

As the agency dedicated to expanding access to affordable housing and fostering neighborhood revitalization, the DHCD has a policy interest in laws that alter the process for recovering possession of real property, particularly those intended for sale or lease.

The Department of Labor oversees professional licensing, including the State Real Estate Commission. Since the bill's expedited proceedings are triggered by a property being advertised or listed for sale or lease, the department has an interest in how these procedural changes affect the real estate professionals they regulate.
The Governor’s Office is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation and overseeing the operations of all state departments. This bill would require executive review before being enacted into law.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an institution of higher education from denying access or services to a student based on the student's diagnosis of sickle cell disease; requiring an institution of higher education to provide reasonable accommodations for students with sickle cell disease; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to develop an education and awareness campaign for institutions of higher education in the State regarding students with sickle cell disease; etc.
Title: Sickle Cell Disease - Institutions of Higher Education - Policies, Procedures, and Educational Campaigns
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland institutions of higher education from denying access or services to students based on a sickle cell disease diagnosis and requires the provision of reasonable accommodations for such students. It mandates that the Maryland Department of Health, in collaboration with the Maryland Higher Education Commission and other stakeholders, develop an educational awareness campaign, clinical procedures, and a framework for supporting and treating students with sickle cell disease at these institutions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Students with sickle cell disease attending Maryland institutions of higher education, as well as the faculty, staff, and health personnel employed by those institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in a state general fund expenditure increase of $139,400 in FY 2027 and $157,900 in FY 2028. This funding is primarily for contractual personnel at the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Higher Education Commission to develop educational materials, clinical procedures, and provide technical assistance. These positions are assumed to terminate in 2028. Public and private institutions of higher education and local community colleges are expected to implement the requirements using existing resources. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the chief executive office, it oversees the operations of all state departments and will be responsible for ensuring that MDH and MHEC successfully implement the new statewide policies and awareness campaigns mandated by the bill.

The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor for state agencies and higher education institutions; it would likely be involved in reviewing the new framework, procedures, and non-discrimination policies for legal compliance.

The bill explicitly prohibits institutions of higher education from denying access or services based on a student's medical diagnosis, which aligns with the commission's mandate to enforce anti-discrimination laws in public accommodations.

DBM is responsible for the state's personnel and budget oversight; the fiscal note indicates a need for new contractual positions at MDH and MHEC to implement the bill, requiring DBM approval for funding and position creation.

MDH is a primary implementing agency responsible for developing the education and awareness campaign, creating the framework and procedures for institutions, providing technical assistance, and compiling educational materials for staff.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Statewide Steering Committee on Sickle Cell Disease to be consulted in the development of the framework, procedures, and educational materials, and to jointly provide technical assistance to institutions.

MHEC is a primary implementing agency tasked with consulting on the development of procedures, providing technical assistance to institutions, and monitoring institutional compliance with the new policies.
MHEC is specifically mandated by the bill to consult on the sickle cell framework and procedures, provide technical assistance to colleges, and monitor the implementation of these policies statewide.

As a public institution of higher education, the university must comply with the bill's requirements to provide reasonable accommodations, establish reporting procedures for discrimination, and publicize these services.

As the state's public honors college, it is directly impacted as it must implement the required non-discrimination policies, provide accommodations for students with sickle cell disease, and establish reporting mechanisms.

As the umbrella organization for 12 public universities, USM is responsible for ensuring its member institutions implement the mandated sickle cell disease policies, accommodations, and reporting procedures.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "student financing company" to exclude an institution of postsecondary education for purposes of certain registration and reporting requirements.
Title: Financial Institutions – Definition of Student Financing Companies – Alteration
Status: In the House - Hearing canceled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of a student financing company to exclude institutions of postsecondary education. This change exempts these institutions from existing registration and annual reporting requirements administered by the Office of Financial Regulation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Office of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Institutions of postsecondary education and students who utilize student financing products.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland state or local government operations or finances. There are no significant estimated changes to state revenues or expenditures as a result of exempting these institutions from registration and reporting requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Labor's Office of Financial Regulation (OFR), which is the primary state entity responsible for the registration and oversight of student financing companies. By excluding institutions of postsecondary education from this definition, the bill removes these institutions from the OFR's regulatory and reporting requirements.

As the governing body for 12 public universities, the University System of Maryland is highly relevant because its member institutions are 'institutions of postsecondary education.' The bill would exempt these institutions from the registration and annual reporting requirements currently imposed on student financing companies.

As a public urban research university and state agency, Morgan State is an institution of postsecondary education. The bill would exempt the university from being classified as a student financing company, thereby removing registration and reporting obligations for any student financing products it offers.

As the state's public honors college, Saint Mary's is an institution of postsecondary education that may offer student financing. This bill would exempt the college from the regulatory oversight, registration, and reporting requirements administered by the Office of Financial Regulation for student financing companies.

The Higher Education Commission coordinates policies for the institutions affected by this bill. The legislation's change to the definition of 'student financing company' specifically targets the educational institutions within the Commission's scope of policy coordination and academic oversight.

This agency oversees the state's postsecondary education system and administers financial aid standards. The bill's exclusion of postsecondary institutions from student financing company regulations directly impacts the regulatory and administrative framework for the colleges and universities under this agency's jurisdiction.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the Office of Financial Regulation and the Higher Education Commission. They would be responsible for interpreting the change in law and advising these agencies on the legal interpretation of the changed definitions and the resulting shift in regulatory enforcement responsibilities.

The Governor's Office oversees all executive agencies, including the Department of Labor. As the bill involves the regulation of financial institutions and higher education, the office would be responsible for reviewing the policy implications and signing or vetoing the legislation.

Synopsis: Requiring the District Court for Anne Arundel County to issue its summons for a trial to repossess for failure to pay rent to any constable or sheriff's designee; providing that a sheriff's designee in Anne Arundel County has the same authority and responsibility as a constable or sheriff in an action to repossess for a failure to pay rent; requiring a sheriff's designee to post a notice of a trial at a certain property or address; etc.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Summons for Actions to Repossess for Failure to Pay Rent - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill modifies the legal procedures for failure-to-pay-rent repossession actions specifically in Anne Arundel County. It authorizes the District Court to issue summons to a sheriff's designee, who is granted the same authority and responsibilities as a constable or sheriff. The bill extends the trial timeline from 5 days to 30 days after a complaint is filed, requires a 7-day advance notice of trial to be posted at the property, and limits the District Court to hearing no more than 100 such cases per day. It also mandates that service fees be paid directly to the Sheriff's Office.
responsible_party: District Court for Anne Arundel County and the Anne Arundel County Sheriff's Office
stakeholders: Landlords and tenants in Anne Arundel County, the Anne Arundel County Sheriff's Office, and the Maryland District Court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires that service fees for summons be paid directly to the Anne Arundel County Sheriff's Office when service is directed to a constable or sheriff's designee. The provision capping the number of repossession cases at 100 per day may impact court scheduling and administrative workload. A full fiscal note with specific revenue and expenditure estimates was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly impacts the operations of the District Court in Anne Arundel County by altering trial timelines for repossession cases from 5 to 30 days, establishing a daily cap of 100 cases, and expanding the authority of process servers to include a sheriff's designee.
The bill modifies the legal procedure for rent-related repossessions, which is a core component of housing policy and community stability managed by the DHCD.

The OAG acts as the legal advisor to state agencies and the Judiciary; they would be responsible for ensuring that the implementation of new service procedures and the delegation of authority to sheriff's designees adhere to state law.

The underlying statute (Real Property 8-401) modified by this bill requires landlords to certify compliance with the MDE's lead paint registration and inspection requirements to file a repossession complaint.
As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office reviews and signs legislation that affects judicial procedures and housing policy in major jurisdictions like Anne Arundel County.

Synopsis: Requiring certain interscholastic and intramural junior varsity and varsity athletic teams or sports sponsored by certain schools and certain locker rooms to be expressly designated based on biological sex; prohibiting certain entities from taking certain adverse actions against a school for maintaining separate interscholastic and intramural junior varsity and varsity athletic teams or sports or locker rooms for students of the female sex; etc.
Title: Education - Interscholastic and Intramural Junior Varsity and Varsity Teams and Locker Rooms - Designation Based on Sex (Fairness in Girls' Sports Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: The Fairness in Girls’ Sports Act requires Maryland public high schools and certain nonpublic high schools to designate junior varsity and varsity athletic teams and locker rooms based on biological sex. It prohibits students of the male sex from participating on teams or using locker rooms specifically designated for girls, females, or women. The bill also establishes a civil cause of action for students or schools that suffer harm or retaliation due to violations, allowing them to seek monetary damages and attorney's fees.
responsible_party: Maryland public high schools, participating nonpublic high schools, and local school systems.
stakeholders: High school student athletes, public and nonpublic high schools, local boards of education, and athletic associations or organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: While a separate Fiscal Note was not provided in the text, the bill creates significant potential fiscal impacts by authorizing civil actions against schools and athletic organizations. Prevailing plaintiffs can recover monetary damages for psychological, emotional, and physical harm, as well as reasonable attorney’s fees and costs, which would increase expenditures for local school systems and the State.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly regulates athletic teams and locker rooms in public high schools and certain nonpublic high schools. As the primary agency overseeing the K-12 system and host of the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association (MPSSAA), MSDE is responsible for implementing these requirements and ensuring school compliance.

The bill establishes new legal requirements based on biological sex and creates a private right of action for civil suits against schools and organizations. The OAG would be responsible for providing legal counsel to the Department of Education and defending the state in potential litigation concerning the act's constitutionality or implementation.

The bill explicitly provides students and schools the right to bring civil actions for monetary damages, attorney's fees, and injunctive relief in response to violations or retaliation. This creates a new category of litigation that will directly impact court workloads and judicial administration.

The MCCR enforces anti-discrimination laws in public accommodations and education. This bill mandates sex-based separation in athletics and facilities, which directly interacts with state civil rights frameworks regarding sex and gender identity discrimination.

As the chief executive, the Governor oversees the state agencies responsible for enforcing this legislation. The bill addresses significant state policy regarding education and social issues, aligning with the Governor’s role in overseeing department operations and statewide initiatives.

The MCSS, which operates within MSDE, is tasked with supporting the emotional well-being and physical environment of schools. The bill's requirements for locker room designation and the potential for lawsuits based on 'psychological, emotional, and physical harm' fall within their scope of monitoring school environments.

The GOC leads a whole-of-government approach to child well-being. Policies dictating student participation in sports and access to school facilities significantly impact the social and educational environment for Maryland youth.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth to analyze the challenges related to the delay in student enrollment counts and its effect on school funding and the connection between growing student populations and the provision of school funding; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 15, 2026.
Title: Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth to analyze challenges related to student enrollment counts, population growth, and their effects on school funding, and to make recommendations for improvements to funding provision.
stakeholders: Public school students, local boards of education, the Maryland State Department of Education, public school personnel, and county governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services assumes the task force can be staffed using existing resources, although the Office of the Governor estimated a fiscal 2027 need of $254,000 for contractual support and an executive assistant. State expenditures may increase minimally for travel reimbursements for task force members. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires a representative from the Office of the Comptroller to serve as a member of the Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth. As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller provides fiscal expertise relevant to analyzing education funding formulas and student population growth impacts.

The Task Force's focus on analyzing and recommending improvements to state education funding formulas directly impacts the state’s annual operating budget, which DBM is responsible for formulating and overseeing. Additionally, DBM has a role in managing potential fiscal impacts related to staffing and reimbursement for task force members.

MSDE is a primary implementing agency for this bill. A representative of the department is a mandated member of the Task Force, and the agency is the primary source of the student enrollment and funding data the Task Force is charged with analyzing.

The Department of Planning is responsible for projecting school enrollment, which is a critical data component of the Task Force's mandate to analyze challenges related to student population growth and enrollment counts.
The bill explicitly requires the Office of the Governor to provide staffing for the Task Force, and the Governor is responsible for appointing the majority of the members and designating the chair.

The Office of Appointments is responsible for the recruitment and vetting of candidates for boards and task forces. They will manage the administrative process for the nine appointments to the Task Force made by the Governor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill creates a new executive task force, which falls directly into this functional category. The Task Force will conduct inquiries and provide formal recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.

Synopsis: Clarifying that a communication between an attorney and a client that acts as a fiduciary is subject to the attorney-client privilege even if fiduciary funds are used to compensate the attorney for services rendered to the client.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Fiduciaries - Attorney-Client Privilege
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/28 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill clarifies that communications between an attorney and a client acting as a fiduciary are protected by attorney-client privilege, even if the attorney's fees are paid using fiduciary funds. It further provides that the existence of a fiduciary relationship between a fiduciary and a beneficiary does not waive this privilege.
stakeholders: Fiduciaries (including trustees, executors, administrators, and agents under a power of attorney), beneficiaries of estates and trusts, and attorneys.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances. The impact on small businesses is estimated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts judicial proceedings and the rules of evidence by clarifying the scope of attorney-client privilege for fiduciaries, which is a primary matter handled by the Maryland Judiciary and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Register of Wills is responsible for overseeing the administrative probate of estates, where fiduciaries (such as personal representatives) are appointed and frequently interact with legal counsel and beneficiaries.
As the state's chief legal office, the OAG upholds the rule of law and advises the General Assembly and state agencies on the legal standards for privilege and fiduciary responsibilities.
The Department of Aging manages public guardianship services and advocates for older adults, who are major users of fiduciary arrangements like powers of attorney and trusts addressed in the bill.
DHS oversees adult protective services and welfare programs that often involve court-appointed guardians acting as fiduciaries for vulnerable individuals.

bill_summary: The bill, titled the Restoring Energy Freedom Act, requires the Governor to withdraw Maryland from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI). It repeals the statutory mandate for the State's participation in RGGI and removes provisions requiring that proceeds from the sale of carbon dioxide allowances be deposited into the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund.
stakeholders: Maryland electricity customers, particularly low- and moderate-income households receiving energy assistance; manufacturers; the Maryland Department of the Environment; and the Maryland Energy Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in a significant loss of special fund revenue for the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) by eliminating proceeds from the sale of carbon dioxide allowances under RGGI. This loss of revenue will reduce funding available for the Electric Universal Service Program, energy efficiency and conservation programs, and renewable energy initiatives. Additionally, the bill removes specific allocation requirements for these proceeds and adjusts the administration of other compliance fees within the SEIF.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Governor to withdraw the State from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) and mandates a report to the General Assembly regarding the withdrawal plan.
The bill repeals various environmental statutes related to RGGI, which the department is currently responsible for implementing and overseeing as the primary environmental regulator.

The MEA administers the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is currently funded by RGGI auction proceeds. This bill removes those proceeds as a revenue source, fundamentally altering the fund's capacity.

A major portion of RGGI proceeds in the SEIF is allocated to the Electric Universal Service Program and other low-income energy assistance programs managed by DHS. The bill eliminates this specific funding stream.
The withdrawal from RGGI would have a significant fiscal impact on the state budget, as the proceeds from the initiative currently fund various state energy and environmental programs.
The bill removes provisions in the Natural Resources Article that utilize the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund to help achieve RGGI offset opportunities in urban areas.
The bill impacts the funding structure of the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, which specifically provides funding to the Maryland Clean Energy Center.
The bill involves oversight of electricity rates, legislative energy relief refunds, and the reallocation of compliance fees within the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.

The bill mentions funding for the Climate Technology Founder’s Fund, which is an initiative TEDCO is involved with, and relates to the broader energy innovation funding landscape affected by the bill.
As the chief legal office, the OAG would be involved in the legal and administrative process of withdrawing the State from the multi-state Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative agreement.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain Ten Commandments Monument to be placed on the grounds of the Maryland State House; requiring the Commission on Artistic Property to oversee the care and maintenance of the monument; and establishing the Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument.
Title: State Government - State House Trust - Ten Commandments Monument Display Act
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.
