bill_summary: The Ten Commandments Monument Display Act requires a monument of the Ten Commandments to be placed on the grounds of the Maryland State House. It establishes a seven-member Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument to oversee the design, construction, and placement of the monument, which must be funded by a private entity. The Commission on Artistic Property is designated to manage the long-term care and maintenance of the monument once it is installed.
responsible_party: The Commission on Artistic Property, the Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument, and the Division of Historical and Cultural Programs in the Department of Planning
stakeholders: The citizens of Maryland, visitors to the Maryland State House, the Governor, the Maryland General Assembly, and the Maryland Attorney General
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires the design, construction, and placement of the monument to be completed by a private entity at no cost to the State. State expenditures may increase to cover travel reimbursements for members of the Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument and potential legal costs incurred by the Attorney General in the event of a constitutional challenge.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill assigns the Commission on Artistic Property (which is managed by the Maryland State Archives) the responsibility for overseeing the care and maintenance of the monument. The State Archives also maintains the state's historical records and artistic property.

The State House Trust oversees and preserves the Maryland State House and its grounds. The bill requires the monument to be placed on these grounds and explicitly requires the new Commission to consult with the Trust on site selection and placement.
The bill mandates that the Division of Historical and Cultural Programs within the Department of Planning provide the staff support for the newly created Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new specialized body, the Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument, to manage the design, construction, and placement of the monument.

The Governor is responsible for appointing three members to the new Commission and designating its chair. The office also oversees the State House Trust and the operations of the executive branch agencies involved.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to prepare and present a legal defense of the monument should its legality or constitutionality be challenged in court.
DGS is responsible for the maintenance and logistics of state-owned facilities, including the State House. The bill requires the new Commission to consult with DGS regarding the monument's placement.
The bill requires the new Commission to consult with the Maryland State Arts Council, which is a component of the Department of Commerce, regarding the monument's design and placement.

Synopsis: Requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration to develop and make available an Old Line Plate with a certain numeric-only registration number for certain motor vehicles.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Special Registration Plates - Old Line Plates (Old Line Plate Program Act of 2026)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to develop and offer 'Old Line Plates,' which are numeric-only registration plates (one to five digits) designed to resemble Maryland's 1911 license plates with white characters on a black background. The MVA is required to establish a public auction program to award the rights to these numbers, set regulations for their transfer, and use the collected fees to recover costs and credit the Transportation Trust Fund.
stakeholders: Maryland owners of Class A (passenger), Class E (truck), and Class M (multipurpose) vehicles, and the Motor Vehicle Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues increase from auction and registration fees, while TTF expenditures increase for plate production (approximately $10 per set) and auction operation costs (approximately $27,500 per auction). The MVA is authorized to recover its costs from the fees collected. There is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MVA is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation, including developing the Old Line Plate, managing the inventory of registration numbers, establishing the public auction program, and adopting the necessary regulations.

As the parent agency of the MVA, MDOT oversees the administration of the new registration program, and all auction fees and transfer fees collected under the bill will be credited to the Transportation Trust Fund which MDOT manages.

As the primary agency for enforcing motor vehicle and traffic laws, MSP must be prepared to identify and verify the validity of these new non-standard registration plates (white characters on a black background) in the field.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees Maryland Correctional Enterprises (MCE), which is the primary manufacturer of vehicle registration plates for the state and will likely be responsible for the production of the new Old Line Plates.
The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor to the MVA and will be involved in drafting and reviewing the regulations and auction protocols required by the bill to ensure they meet legal standards.
The bill authorizes the MVA to deny, suspend, or revoke registration rights for fraud or misuse; such administrative actions are typically subject to appeal and adjudication before the OAH.

The Board of Public Works may be required to review and approve significant procurement contracts if the MVA utilizes third-party vendors for the online auction platform or specialized manufacturing materials.
The Comptroller acts as the state's fiscal watchdog and sits on the Board of Public Works, overseeing the flow of new revenues into the Transportation Trust Fund.
DBM is responsible for overseeing the state's annual budget and will monitor the fiscal impact of the new revenues and administrative costs associated with the MVA's Old Line Plate program.
The Treasurer serves as a member of the Board of Public Works and manages the state's financial assets, including the investment of funds within the Transportation Trust Fund.

Synopsis: Altering the exemption from overtime pay for individuals who are employed to work in an administrative, executive, or professional capacity.
Title: Labor and Employment - Exemptions From Overtime Pay - Administrative, Executive, or Professional Capacity
Status: In the House - First Reading Government, Labor, and Elections

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill alters the criteria for overtime pay exemptions for individuals employed in administrative, executive, or professional capacities. It establishes a multi-year phase-in of minimum salary thresholds required to qualify for these exemptions, starting at $769.23 per week in 2027 and increasing to $961.54 per week by 2031, or the federal threshold if higher. The bill also codifies specific duties tests for each exempt category, aligning state law with federal regulations.
stakeholders: Maryland employers and employees working in administrative, executive, or professional capacities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government expenditures are expected to increase to provide overtime pay to employees whose salaries fall below the new thresholds. General fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Labor will increase for enforcement and administrative staffing. State revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties collected from employers found in violation of the overtime provisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for enforcing wage and hour laws and protecting the economic welfare of workers. This bill directly amends the Labor and Employment Article, specifically the thresholds and criteria for overtime exemptions, which falls under the department's regulatory and enforcement mandate.

DBM manages the statewide personnel system and the executive branch budget. By increasing the salary thresholds for overtime exemptions, the bill will likely increase personnel costs for the state government as more employees become eligible for overtime pay.

The Comptroller manages the central payroll for over 100,000 state employees. Any change to overtime eligibility criteria requires the Comptroller to update payroll systems and processing protocols to ensure state workers are compensated correctly under the new law.

As the agency focused on economic development and supporting small businesses, the Department of Commerce is impacted by changes to labor laws that increase the cost of doing business in Maryland. The higher overtime thresholds will affect private sector employers across various industries.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the Department of Labor and other state agencies. They would be responsible for providing legal interpretations of the revised administrative, executive, and professional duty tests and defending the state against any legal challenges.

The Governor's Office oversees all state departments and is responsible for drafting the annual budget. The fiscal impact of increased overtime pay for state employees would need to be reflected in the state's financial planning and executive initiatives.

The University System of Maryland is a major state employer with a significant number of administrative and professional staff whose exempt status may be affected by the new salary thresholds, leading to notable fiscal and operational impacts.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Highway Administration to study and make recommendations on the implementation of a consistent statewide policy for the use of traffic calming devices on highways in the State; and requiring the Administration to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2026.
Title: State Highway Administration - Traffic Calming Devices - Study
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: The bill requires the State Highway Administration to study and recommend a statewide policy for traffic calming devices, such as speed bumps and traffic circles, to ensure consistency and safety across Maryland highways.
stakeholders: Bicyclists, motorists, pedestrians, and local governments (counties and municipalities)
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by an estimated total of $75,000 ($12,500 in FY 2026 and $62,500 in FY 2027) for consultant services to conduct the study. There is no impact on State revenues or direct fiscal effect on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Highway Administration to lead the study, research best practices, and report findings on traffic calming policies.

As the parent agency of the SHA, MDOT is responsible for the overall transportation network and manages the Transportation Trust Fund, which the fiscal note identifies as the funding source for this study.
The SHA is required to report its findings and recommendations directly to the Governor, and the office oversees the executive departments involved.

The study must include recommendations for technical support to counties and municipalities, which aligns with the Department of Planning's role in supporting local governments with urban design and infrastructure management.

The MSP is responsible for highway safety and crash prevention; traffic calming devices are physical measures intended to impact driver behavior and reduce speeds, affecting MSP's enforcement and safety mission.
The bill has a notable fiscal impact of $75,000 in Special Fund expenditures, which falls under DBM's oversight of the state's annual operating budget and fiscal accountability.
The bill requires a list of academic entities that could assist in the development of the policy; USM institutions often partner with state agencies for such research and technical expertise.

As a preeminent public urban research university, Morgan State's engineering and urban planning expertise makes it a potential academic partner for researching traffic calming devices as required by the study.
Traffic calming devices, such as raised crosswalks and narrowed roads, directly impact accessible transportation and the safety of individuals with disabilities in community environments.
Traffic calming devices are a primary tool for enhancing student safety in school zones, which is a core interest of the MCSS.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to reimburse a psychiatric rehabilitation program for a minimum of 6 and a maximum of 30 psychiatric rehabilitation community psychiatric support services delivered to certain individuals each month.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Psychiatric Rehabilitation Program Services - Reimbursement (Youth Psychiatric Rehabilitation Parity Act of 2026)

bill_summary: The Youth Psychiatric Rehabilitation Parity Act of 2026 requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to reimburse psychiatric rehabilitation programs for a minimum of 6 and a maximum of 30 community psychiatric support services per month for eligible individuals. The mandate applies to individuals with serious emotional disturbances or persistent mental disorders who are severely impaired and living with a parent, guardian, or relative.
stakeholders: Individuals with serious emotional disturbances or persistent mental disorders, their legal guardians or family members, and psychiatric rehabilitation program providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase State expenditures for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program by establishing a mandatory reimbursement range for psychiatric rehabilitation services. These costs will likely be shared between State general funds and federal matching funds. Specific expenditure estimates and revenue impacts were not included in the provided text as the Fiscal Note was not present.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) to reimburse psychiatric rehabilitation program services at specific rates.

As the state’s central fiscal authority, DBM is responsible for the oversight of the Maryland Medical Assistance Program's budget, which will be impacted by changes in reimbursement minimums and maximums.

The bill specifically addresses services for individuals with serious emotional disturbances who live with a parent or guardian, aligning with the office's mission to coordinate mental health services and support child well-being.
The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the Department of Health and will be involved in the review and drafting of the mandatory regulations required by this legislation.
The department coordinates policy for residents with disabilities, including those with serious and persistent mental disorders, and advocates for community-based services and independence.

The Governor’s Office oversees all state departments, including the Department of Health, and is responsible for signing the legislation and coordinating statewide initiatives related to health and economic opportunity.

Synopsis: Establishing an Edible Forests and Foraging Program within the Department of Natural Resources; requiring individuals who forage in designated foraging areas to obtain a foraging permit; requiring the Department to charge a permit application fee and establish a fee waiver process for individuals who demonstrate financial need; requiring the Department to establish and maintain edible forests on State land, subject to available funding; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Edible Forests and Foraging Program - Establishment

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Edible Forests and Foraging Program within the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to manage and regulate foraging on state-owned land. It requires the DNR to designate foraging areas where individuals must obtain a permit to harvest plants for personal consumption, while also establishing 'edible forests' that are open for foraging without a permit. The bill creates a special fund, the Edible Forests and Foraging Fund, to support the cultivation of noninvasive plants and the administration of the program.
stakeholders: Foragers, Maryland residents, and the Department of Natural Resources
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a special nonlapsing fund, the Edible Forests and Foraging Fund, which will be funded through permit fees, interest earnings, and potential state budget appropriations. Expenditures from the fund will be used to designate, plant, and maintain foraging areas and edible forests, as well as for administrative costs. The requirement to establish edible forests is subject to the availability of funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of Natural Resources as the primary agency responsible for establishing, administering, and regulating the Edible Forests and Foraging Program, including the issuance of permits and management of the associated special fund.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the Edible Forests and Foraging Fund separately and invest its money in the same manner as other State money.
The bill mandates that the Comptroller account for the Edible Forests and Foraging Fund, which is established as a special, nonlapsing fund.

The bill requires the establishment and maintenance of edible forests on 'State-owned land'. As the agency responsible for managing the state's real estate and infrastructure, DGS may be involved in the implementation or maintenance of these forests on lands outside of DNR's direct jurisdiction.

The OAG will be responsible for providing legal counsel to the Department of Natural Resources regarding the establishment of the program, the drafting of new regulations, and the enforcement of the foraging permit requirements.
The bill establishes a new special fund that includes money appropriated in the State budget, requiring DBM to oversee the fiscal allocation for the program and its administrative expenses.

The program coordinates land use and sustainable growth via edible forests, which aligns with the Department's role in providing technical assistance and policy guidance for the state's cultural and natural resource assets.
The bill creates a new statewide program and fund within the executive branch, impacting the Governor's environmental and budget priorities.
As the fiscal watchdog for state agencies, the OLA will be responsible for auditing the financial controls and compliance of the newly established Edible Forests and Foraging Fund.
This multi-agency initiative focuses on sustainable growth and environmental stewardship, which are central themes of establishing edible forests and regulated foraging on state lands.

The council advocates for rural interests and community health; foraging and the cultivation of edible forests are highly relevant to food access and natural resource management in rural Maryland counties.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Education to develop, by July 1, 2027, curriculum content for an elective course in water safety and swimming for public school students in kindergarten through grade 8; requiring, beginning in the 2027-2028 school year, county boards of education to implement the water safety and swimming curriculum content for students in kindergarten through grade 8 in public schools in the county; etc.
Title: Public Schools - Water Safety and Swimming Course - Established

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland State Board of Education to develop curriculum content standards for a water safety and swimming course for public school students in kindergarten through grade 8 by July 1, 2027. Beginning in the 2027-2028 school year, county boards of education must implement the course in all applicable schools, ensure reasonable accommodations for students with disabilities, and may partner with local parks and recreation agencies for facility access.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education and county boards of education
stakeholders: Public school students in kindergarten through grade 8, students with disabilities, county boards of education, and local parks and recreation agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The provided text does not include the associated Fiscal and Policy Note; however, the bill mandates the State Board of Education to develop standards and requires local county boards to implement swimming courses starting in the 2027-2028 school year. These requirements will result in state costs for curriculum development and significant local expenditures related to instructional staff, facility access, and student transportation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the State Board of Education (within MSDE) to develop curriculum content standards and regulations for the water safety and swimming course. It also oversees the implementation by county boards.

The bill explicitly requires county boards to provide reasonable accommodations for students with disabilities to ensure equal opportunity to participate in the swimming course, aligning with the Department's mission to coordinate accessible services.

The mandate to implement a swimming course in all public schools for grades K-8 will have a significant fiscal impact on state and local education budgets, requiring facility access, transportation, and staffing.
The OAG acts as the legal advisor to the State Board of Education and would likely provide counsel on the development of curriculum standards and compliance with disability and liability laws.

If the implementation of the mandated swimming course requires modifications to school facilities or the construction of new aquatic infrastructure, the IAC would be responsible for oversight and funding allocation.

Synopsis: Requiring a procurement contract for 3 years or more in duration and valued at greater than $2,000,000 for construction or security services to include a clause requiring contract modification for increased costs for compensation and benefits as a result of statutory changes increasing required compensation or benefits; and requiring a certain contract that is modified to be contingent on approval by the Chief Procurement Officer.
Title: State Procurement - Construction and Services - Contract Modification
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill requires State procurement contracts for construction and security services that are valued at more than $2 million and have a duration of at least three years to include a clause for contract modification. This clause allows for equitable adjustments to the contract price when costs for compensation and benefits increase due to statutory changes. For security service contracts, modifications are also required if cost increases result from collective bargaining. All such modifications are contingent upon the approval of the Chief Procurement Officer.
stakeholders: State procurement units, construction and security service contractors, and small businesses in the construction and security industries.
fiscal_impact_summary: State procurement costs across all funds may increase significantly starting in FY 2027 as the State assumes the risk for higher labor costs resulting from legislative changes or collective bargaining. A precise estimate of these costs is not feasible. Additionally, State procurement units such as the Department of General Services and the Maryland Department of Transportation may require extra staff to manage the increased volume of contract modifications. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is a primary procurement unit and houses the Chief Procurement Officer (CPO), who must approve all contract modifications under the bill. The agency also manages significant state construction and security service contracts.

MDOT manages the largest volume of state construction projects through SHA, MTA, and MAA. The fiscal note explicitly identifies MDOT as an agency that may require additional staff to process the resulting contract modifications.

The BPW is the highest administrative authority for state procurement and must approve contract modifications exceeding $50,000. This bill directly impacts the modification process and liability for state funds.

DBM oversees state personnel costs and the annual operating budget. Statutory changes to compensation or benefits—which trigger the bill's modification requirements—directly fall under DBM's policy and fiscal purview.
USM handles its own procurement for significant construction and security service projects across its 12 universities, making it directly subject to the bill's contract clause requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages correctional facilities which require extensive security service contracts and ongoing construction/renovation, making the agency highly sensitive to contract adjustments for labor costs.
The MSA plans and manages major construction projects, including stadiums and the 'Built to Learn' school program. Many of its projects meet the bill's $2 million and 3-year threshold.

As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller reviews and approves significant state contract modifications. The agency is also involved in the state's fiscal reporting and payroll oversight.
The Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works and advises on major state procurements and capital projects impacted by the bill.

The OAG provides legal counsel for state agencies and will be responsible for drafting and reviewing the mandatory contract clauses required by the bill to ensure compliance with State Finance and Procurement law.
As a primary procurement unit and a major urban research institution with significant construction projects, Morgan State will need to include these modification clauses in its qualifying contracts.

The IAC funds and oversees public school construction projects. While many projects are local, the IAC manages the state's capital investment policies which align with the bill's focus on construction contract modifications.
MDH operates numerous healthcare and behavioral health facilities requiring security services and construction, often under long-term contracts that meet the bill's thresholds.
DJS manages secure detention facilities that utilize long-term security service contracts and facility construction, both of which are impacted by the bill's requirements.

The Governor signs legislation affecting state procurement and serves on the Board of Public Works. The Chief Procurement Officer, who must approve the modifications, operates within the executive structure overseen by this office.
The bill's triggers include statutory changes to compensation and benefits, which are often administered or influenced by the Department of Labor's workforce and regulatory policies.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition on applicants for and holders of video lottery operation licenses and persons who own an interest in video lottery facility operations in the State from directly or indirectly making contributions to certain campaign finance entities.
Title: Video Lottery Operations - Prohibitions on Campaign Contributions - Parity Act
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/29 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill repeals the existing prohibition that prevents applicants for video lottery operation licenses, license holders, and individuals or entities with an ownership interest in video lottery facilities from making campaign contributions to nonfederal candidates or campaign finance entities in Maryland.
stakeholders: Applicants for and holders of video lottery operation licenses, owners of video lottery facilities, and candidates for nonfederal public office in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Maryland State or local government finances, as it primarily changes campaign finance eligibility for specific entities rather than creating new state expenditures or revenue streams.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for administering and supervising campaign finance in the state. This bill repeals a specific prohibition on campaign contributions from video lottery entities, which falls directly under the board's oversight of the Fair Election Practices Act.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency regulates the video lottery license holders and applicants who are currently prohibited from making campaign contributions. The agency coordinates with the Board of Elections to identify entities subject to these restrictions, and the bill directly impacts the permitted activities of its licensees.

The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes violations of state election laws. This bill repeals a specific category of campaign finance violations, thereby altering the office's investigative and prosecutorial mandate regarding political contributions from the gaming industry.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal advisor to the Maryland State Board of Elections. It would be responsible for providing guidance on the legal implications of repealing these restrictions and representing the state in any related litigation.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the reallocation of school safety grants to local school systems that have fully expended their initial grant allocation and can demonstrate additional unmet needs within the same fiscal year. bill_summary: The Ticket Resale Consumer Protection and Transparency Act regulates the ticket resale market in Maryland. The bill limits resale prices and service fees to a maximum of 10% above the original ticket price, prohibits the sale of speculative tickets (tickets not currently in the seller's possession), and mandates refunds for counterfeit tickets or canceled events. It also requires ticket platforms to implement technology to prevent the use of bots to bypass purchase limits.

stakeholders: Ticket purchasers (consumers), ticket resellers, secondary ticket exchanges and marketplaces, and ticket issuers including musicians, sports teams, and venue operators.

bill_summary: This bill reclassifies several motor vehicle offenses, including certain registration, equipment, and window tinting violations, as secondary offenses, meaning they can only be enforced if a driver has been detained for a different primary violation. It requires police officers to document all reasons for a stop on citations or police reports and allows the failure of an officer to provide required identification or the reason for a stop to serve as a basis for excluding evidence. Additionally, it prohibits stops for expired registrations until the fourth month following the expiration date.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Maryland Department of Transportation (Motor Vehicle Administration), and Maryland law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Maryland motorists, law enforcement officers, and the state court system
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are expected to decrease, potentially significantly, due to a reduction in fine collections from traffic stops for offenses reclassified as secondary. Transportation Trust Fund revenues will also decrease due to fewer referrals to the MVA for registration noncompliance. State general fund expenditures increase by $4,200 in FY 2027 for Judiciary computer programming. Local government finances and operations are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are directly impacted by the new requirements for documenting traffic stops, the shift of several traffic offenses to secondary enforcement, and the legal implications of the expanded exclusionary rule regarding evidence obtained during stops.

The SHA maintains state highways and is responsible for road safety and infrastructure. The bill changes the enforcement of laws regarding littering and placing injurious substances on highways, which are within the SHA's maintenance and safety purview.

The DBM is responsible for state revenue estimation and fiscal oversight. The fiscal note indicates a potentially significant decrease in general fund revenue due to foregone fines, requiring DBM's attention to state fiscal health.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is concerned with significant shifts in general fund revenue, such as the foregone traffic fine revenues projected by the fiscal note.

The MDE is responsible for protecting Maryland's water and land. The bill's provisions regarding the discharge of refuse or injurious substances into public waters and highways overlap with MDE's environmental protection mission.

bill_summary: This bill expands existing exemptions from the recordation tax and the State and county transfer taxes to include transfers of real property between related business entities involving common law trusts. bill_summary: This bill designates the megalodon (Otodus megalodon) as the official State shark of Maryland, acknowledging its historical significance as a major predator that lived in the region and is represented extensively in the state's fossil record.
stakeholders: The residents of Maryland, scientific researchers, paleontology enthusiasts, and cultural institutions such as the Calvert Marine Museum.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances. There is no impact on small businesses, and no expenditures or revenues are projected as a result of designating the State shark.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Archives is the central depository for historical records and manages the Maryland Manual On-Line, which serves as the official record-keeper for Maryland's state symbols and designations.
The Secretary of State maintains the Great Seal of Maryland and is responsible for certifying official state documents and the state's symbolic identity.
The Governor's Office is responsible for signing the legislation into law and traditionally facilitates the ceremonial recognition of new state symbols.
The designation of a State Shark provides new opportunities for marketing Maryland's unique natural history and fossil-rich locations, such as Calvert Cliffs, to domestic and international travelers.
The Department of Education oversees the state's K-12 academic standards, and official state symbols are traditionally incorporated into the curriculum for Maryland history and science.

The Department of Natural Resources manages Maryland's land and water resources; the megalodon’s role in prehistoric ecosystems and the state's current shark populations connect to its mission of environmental stewardship.
Through its Historical and Cultural Programs, the Department of Planning coordinates the preservation of the state's archaeological and paleontological heritage.

Synopsis: Requiring a register of wills to allow an installment payment plan for the inheritance tax to be paid by a certain beneficiary of limited means under certain circumstances and subject to certain limitations; and applying the Act to all decedents dying on or after July 1, 2026.
Title: Inheritance Tax - Beneficiaries of Limited Means - Installment Payments
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/20 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires a register of wills to provide an installment payment plan for inheritance taxes for beneficiaries of limited means if the tax liability would otherwise necessitate the sale of the inherited real property. Eligible property includes the beneficiary's primary residence or agricultural land that remains in agricultural use.
stakeholders: Beneficiaries of limited means inheriting primary residences or agricultural land
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect total inheritance tax revenues, but it will likely delay collections beginning in FY 2027, reducing general fund revenues in the near term. Additionally, the registers of wills will incur indeterminate one-time programming costs in FY 2027 to implement the installment systems, which will further reduce general fund revenues by a corresponding amount.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the register of wills allow inheritance tax installment payment plans for certain beneficiaries and gives the registers the authority to specify payment schedules and application requirements.

As the state's chief tax collector and fiscal officer, the Comptroller is responsible for revenue oversight; the bill modifies the collection timing for inheritance taxes which contribute to the General Fund.

The Register of Wills functions as the clerk to the orphans' court and utilizes the administrative and technological infrastructure managed by this agency, which may require system programming for installment plans.

The bill defines eligible real property to include agricultural land, supporting the agency's mission of resource conservation and farm economic viability by allowing heirs to retain farmland through installment tax payments.

The agency oversees the state's revenue estimations and fiscal accountability; the bill has a notable fiscal impact by delaying General Fund revenue collections and necessitating one-time administrative programming costs.

Synopsis: Altering the restrictions on a municipality, for a period following an annexation of land, to authorize the development of certain annexed land for certain land uses or certain densities without obtaining the express approval of the county in which the municipality is located; and altering the authority of a municipality to authorize certain land uses or certain densities for certain annexed land with the express approval of the county in which the municipality is located.
Title: Municipalities - Annexed Land - Land Use and Density
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Smart Growth -see also- Zoning and Planning

bill_summary: This bill modifies the criteria used to determine if a municipality may develop annexed land for different land uses or higher densities without county approval. For five years following an annexation, a municipality is restricted from allowing development that is substantially different in use or density from existing standards unless it receives express approval from the county. The bill changes the benchmark for this comparison from the county's zoning classification to the land use recommendations in the comprehensive plan of the county or municipality applicable at the time of annexation.
responsible_party: Maryland municipalities and county governments with planning and zoning authority
stakeholders: Municipal and county governments, land developers, and owners of property in areas subject to annexation
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill modifies the administrative benchmarks for planning and zoning determinations post-annexation. While the bill text does not specify direct state or local fiscal mandates, it affects local government zoning procedures and could indirectly influence the local property tax base by altering the density and usage of developed annexed land.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Planning is the primary state agency responsible for land use coordination and providing technical assistance to local governments. This bill directly modifies the legal standards for municipal annexation and how density and land use changes are evaluated against local comprehensive plans, which is central to the department's mission.

This multi-agency initiative focuses on implementing 'Smart Growth' land-use policies and reducing urban sprawl. Legislative changes to the density and land-use restrictions following municipal annexation directly impact the initiative's coordination of sustainable development across Maryland communities.

As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation and overseeing state policy on local government relations and land use infrastructure, which are affected by this bill.

The OAG serves as the chief legal advisor to the General Assembly and state agencies. It would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the interpretation of jurisdictional changes between counties and municipalities under the Local Government Article.

Synopsis: Expanding the eligibility for the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program to an applicant who is or was eligible for the Chapter 35 Survivors' Dependents' Educational Assistance benefit as determined by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs; and authorizing certain methods for verifying eligibility of these individuals for the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program.
Title: Higher Education - Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program - Eligibility
Status: In the House - Hearing canceled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program to include individuals who are or were eligible for the federal Chapter 35 Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance benefit from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. It also establishes methods for verifying eligibility, allowing applicants to submit a Certificate of Eligibility or providing for verification by a school certifying official or institutional liaison.
responsible_party: Maryland postsecondary institutions and the Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Surviving spouses and children of veterans, members of the uniformed services, and certain public safety employees who qualify for federal Chapter 35 benefits; Maryland postsecondary institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: Expanding the eligibility criteria for the scholarship program is expected to increase the number of eligible recipients. This likely results in an increase in state expenditures from the General Fund to support additional scholarship awards, although the exact impact depends on the number of new applicants and the total funding appropriated for the program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the state's primary regulatory and coordinating board for higher education and administers over $100 million in financial aid. The bill directly modifies eligibility for the Conroy Memorial Scholarship, a state-funded program overseen by MHEC.

This agency advocates for veterans and helps them secure benefits. The scholarship is specifically for veterans and their dependents, and the bill links eligibility to federal Chapter 35 Survivors’ and Dependents’ Educational Assistance benefits, making the department a key resource hub for this policy.

USM is the strategic leadership body for 12 public universities. The bill requires postsecondary institutions to determine the eligibility of applicants, meaning USM member institutions will be responsible for implementing the new verification procedures.

As a public state agency and independent university, Morgan State will be responsible for processing and verifying the eligibility of applicants for the Conroy Scholarship based on the new criteria established by this bill.

Saint Mary's College is a public liberal arts college and state agency. It is directly impacted by the bill's requirement that postsecondary institutions handle the eligibility determination and verification for scholarship applicants.

DBM oversees the state's budget and fiscal accountability. Expanding scholarship eligibility is likely to have a notable fiscal impact on state expenditures, requiring DBM to manage and allocate the necessary funds.

The Governor's Office enforces state laws and drafts the annual budget. The office is responsible for funding the scholarship program and would be involved in signing the eligibility expansion into law.

Synopsis: Requiring a public broadcaster that holds a debate between candidates for statewide office to invite all candidates who are certified to the ballot in the general election subject to certain requirements; prohibiting a public broadcaster from using or receiving State funds for the remainder of the fiscal year under certain circumstances; requiring the Governor to approve an amended appropriation to reappropriate State funds from a public broadcaster under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Public Broadcasters - Debate for Candidates for Statewide Office - Required Participants
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 2:00 p.m. (Government, Labor, and Elections)
bill_summary: This emergency bill requires any public broadcaster receiving Maryland state funding that hosts a debate for statewide office candidates to invite all candidates certified to the ballot for the general election. Broadcasters are prohibited from using party affiliation, polling thresholds, or fundraising metrics to determine eligibility. If a broadcaster violates these requirements, they are prohibited from using or receiving state funds for the remainder of that fiscal year, and the Maryland Public Broadcasting Commission must request that those funds be reappropriated to another program.
stakeholders: Public broadcasters receiving state funding, candidates for statewide office, and Maryland voters.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances or have any local fiscal impact. While a violation of the bill's requirements would result in a loss of funding for the specific public broadcaster, the bill requires the Maryland Public Broadcasting Commission and the Governor to reappropriate those remaining funds to another program for the current fiscal year.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Public Broadcasting Commission (MPBC) is the primary agency impacted as it operates Maryland Public Television. The bill establishes mandatory requirements for its candidate debates and creates a mechanism where the MPBC must request to reappropriate its own funds to other programs if it violates these requirements.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor approve amended appropriations to reappropriate State funds away from a public broadcaster found in violation of the participation requirements. The Governor also oversees the executive agencies affected by the funding prohibition.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is the designated recipient for proposed amended appropriations if a broadcaster violates the bill's provisions. DBM would be responsible for processing the reappropriation of those State funds to other programs.

The bill's core requirement is that broadcasters must invite all candidates 'certified to the ballot' for statewide office. SBE is the agency responsible for the certification of these candidates, making its records the definitive source for compliance.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor for the Governor and State agencies. It would likely be required to provide legal guidance on the enforcement of the funding penalties and the bill's interaction with federal law and First Amendment protections mentioned in the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Requiring a county superintendent of schools to allow a certain dependent child of an active service member to advance enroll in a school in the county in a certain manner; requiring the remote registration process to provide an opportunity for the service member or other parent or guardian of a dependent child with a disability to note whether the child has an individualized education program or a 504 plan in the sending state; and requiring the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families to publish information on advance enrollment.
Title: Education - Dependent Children of Active Service Members - Advance Enrollment Procedures
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/29 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

Veterans and Military Families, Department of

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland local school systems to establish remote registration and advance enrollment procedures for dependent children of active service members relocating to the state on official orders. It prohibits charging fees or requiring physical appearance for advance enrollment and ensures that children with disabilities who have Individualized Education Programs (IEP) or 504 plans receive appropriate education services without undue delay. The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families is also required to publish and maintain information regarding these enrollment procedures and available services.
responsible_party: Maryland county superintendents of schools, local boards of education, and the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Dependent children of active service members, their parents or guardians, and Maryland local school systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland state or local government operations or finances. State agencies and local school systems can implement the bill's requirements with existing resources. No effect on revenues is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families to publish and maintain information regarding advance enrollment procedures and related services for active service members and their dependent children.

MSDE oversees the K-12 public education system and sets the standards for school enrollment and special education. This bill directly amends the Education Article regarding enrollment procedures and the continuity of Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and 504 plans for students with disabilities.

The bill requires the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families to consult with the Office of Military and Federal Affairs and the Maryland Military Installation Council, both of which are administrative units within the Department of Commerce.

The bill contains specific provisions requiring local school boards to ensure that dependent children of service members who have disabilities continue to receive an appropriate education (IEP or 504 plan) without undue delay.

As an independent state agency providing public K-21 education, the Maryland School for the Deaf is impacted by statewide enrollment and special education notification standards for dependent children of military families.

The Adjutant General oversees the Maryland National Guard and advises on military matters; the bill impacts the families of National Guard members serving on active duty orders who relocate and need to enroll their children in Maryland schools.

Synopsis: Repealing certain exemptions relating to a prohibition on a consumer contract that sets a shorter time to bring an action under or on the consumer contract under certain circumstances; prohibiting a consumer contract from waiving, limiting, impairing, or disclaiming any right conferred or created or a manner of enforcement established by federal or State law; establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to enforcement and certain civil penalties; etc.
Title: Consumer Protection - Consumer Contracts - Prohibited Waiver
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill prohibits consumer contracts from including provisions that waive, limit, or disclaim rights or enforcement methods granted by federal or Maryland law, such as shortening the statute of limitations. It repeals existing exemptions for certain regulated industries, including utilities and security services. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices, allowing the state to seek civil penalties and providing consumers the right to sue for damages, declaratory relief, or injunctions. Waivers of these protections are prohibited except as part of a dispute settlement.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Maryland consumers and businesses providing goods or services for personal, family, or household use.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill classifies violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act, which subjects violators to existing civil penalty and enforcement provisions. While a specific Fiscal Note summary was not included in the provided text, the bill allows for civil penalties and private legal actions for damages.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division is the primary entity responsible for enforcing the Consumer Protection Act. This bill defines violations of consumer contract waiver prohibitions as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under Title 13, directly expanding the OAG's enforcement mandate and authority over civil penalties.

The bill repeals a specific exemption for services regulated by the Maryland Public Service Commission. This change directly affects the regulatory framework for utilities and companies under the Commission's jurisdiction, as their consumer contracts will now be subject to these state consumer protection prohibitions.

As the independent advocate for residential utility consumers, the OPC is highly relevant because the bill removes the consumer contract exemption for utility services. This change empowers the OPC to better protect utility customers from predatory contract terms that waive or limit their legal rights.

The bill repeals an exemption for security system services licensed under Title 18 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article, which is overseen by the Department of Labor. Additionally, the broad repeal of exemptions for any business licensed by a State agency impacts numerous professional trades and financial services regulated by this department.

The bill establishes new legal standards for how courts must handle illegal provisions in consumer contracts (voiding them while enforcing the remainder) and creates specific causes of action for declaratory relief and injunctions, directly affecting judicial proceedings and court administration.

The bill's inclusion of violations under the Consumer Protection Act may lead to an increase in administrative contested cases. The OAH would be responsible for providing the impartial forum and Administrative Law Judges to hear enforcement actions brought by state agencies against businesses violating these contract standards.

Synopsis: Providing that all unhoused individuals have certain rights; establishing an affirmative defense of necessity to certain criminal charges relating to trespass or disturbing the peace; and repealing the authority of a municipality to prohibit vagrancy.
Title: Unhoused Individuals - Rights and Affirmative Defense
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill establishes legal rights for unhoused individuals to engage in life-sustaining activities in public places, such as sleeping, sitting, or taking shelter, provided these activities do not obstruct traffic or business. It prohibits state and local government entities from imposing criminal or civil penalties for these activities unless adequate alternative indoor space is provided. Additionally, it creates an affirmative defense of necessity for criminal prosecutions related to trespass or disturbing the peace and repeals the authority of municipalities to prohibit vagrancy.
responsible_party: Maryland State and local government entities, including law enforcement agencies, social service departments, and the Judiciary.
stakeholders: Unhoused individuals, law enforcement officers, state and local government agencies, and small businesses located in affected public areas.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase across multiple funds, including the State Insurance Trust Fund and the Transportation Trust Fund, to address potential legal claims and operational changes such as law enforcement training and facility maintenance. Local government expenditures are expected to increase significantly due to increased costs for social services, shelter provision, public order management, and litigation risks under the Local Government Tort Claims Act. Revenues are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new affirmative defense of necessity for criminal prosecutions and requires the Judiciary to liberally construe the subtitle, impacting court proceedings and judicial administration.

The bill establishes rights for unhoused individuals to use public places without discrimination based on housing status, which aligns with the Commission's role in enforcing anti-discrimination laws.
The fiscal note indicates a likely increase in expenditures across multiple fund types, which DBM would need to manage as the state’s central fiscal authority.

As the manager of state-owned facilities and public buildings, DGS is affected by the rights established for unhoused individuals to take shelter and engage in life-sustaining activities in these locations.
The bill explicitly mentions public health agencies as entities that may offer interventions, and the fiscal note highlights potential public health challenges resulting from the bill.
The bill directly relates to DHCD's mission of homelessness prevention and managing affordable housing, particularly as it relates to the definition of adequate alternative indoor space.

DHS is the primary provider of social services for vulnerable individuals; the bill references local human and social services agencies regarding interventions and shelter availability for unhoused individuals.
DNR manages state parks, which are explicitly defined as public places where unhoused individuals would have a right to engage in life-sustaining activities under this bill.

MDOT is identified in the fiscal note as having significant operational and legal impacts, particularly regarding BWI Marshall Airport, the Maryland Transit Administration, and the State Highway Administration.
As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office oversees all state departments and signs or vetoes legislation affecting statewide civil and criminal policy.

The bill's definition of unhoused individuals includes abandoned minors and those awaiting foster care placement, which falls under GOC's mandate to coordinate services for families and vulnerable youth.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency advises on public safety policy and manages grants; the bill's changes to criminal penalties for unhoused individuals and the affirmative defense for trespass directly impact criminal justice strategies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent individuals and will be the primary agency responsible for asserting the new affirmative defense of necessity for clients charged with trespass or disorderly conduct.
MSP is the primary statewide law enforcement agency and would be prohibited from penalizing unhoused individuals for protected life-sustaining activities in public places.

The STO manages the State Insurance Trust Fund; the fiscal note explicitly states the bill may significantly increase SITF expenditures due to potential tort claims regarding the infringement of rights.
OAG serves as the chief legal office and will handle appeals and provide legal counsel to state agencies regarding the bill's constitutional and civil penalty restrictions.

Synopsis: Requiring restaurants to make available to each customer a written disclosure of each main food allergen, if any, that is an ingredient in each menu item; and excluding a violation of the Act from certain criminal penalties.
Title: Public Health - Restaurants - Disclosure of Main Food Allergens
Status: In the House - Hearing canceled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

bill_summary: House Bill 105 requires Maryland restaurants to provide customers with a written disclosure identifying any main food allergens used as ingredients in menu items. This disclosure can be provided on the menu, as a separate handout, or in a digital format. The bill specifies that while violations are subject to civil penalties, they are not subject to certain criminal penalties.
stakeholders: Maryland restaurants, restaurant owners and operators, and customers with food allergies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill provides that any person who violates the allergen disclosure requirement is liable for a civil penalty not exceeding $5,000 per day per violation. However, the bill specifically exempts these violations from existing criminal penalties (misdemeanor fines and imprisonment). No specific funding is allocated or mandated for implementation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of public health and food service facilities under the Health – General Article, the Department of Health (and local health departments) will be responsible for implementing and enforcing the new allergen disclosure requirements for restaurants.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and represents the state in civil actions to collect penalties for violations of the Health – General Article as specified in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates a cross-reference in Section 13-517 of the Education Article, which MIEMSS administers as part of the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program, to ensure the definition of a 'Facility' remains accurate following the renumbering of sections.

The bill specifies that civil penalties for violations of the allergen disclosure requirement are to be collected via civil actions in the District Court, directly impacting the judiciary's caseload and administrative processes.

The OAH may be required to adjudicate contested administrative actions, such as license suspensions, resulting from a restaurant's failure to comply with the health and food safety regulations established by this bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and is responsible for signing the legislation into law.

Synopsis: Providing collective bargaining rights to nontenure track faculty at State system institutions, Morgan State University, or St. Mary's College of Maryland; defining "nontenure track faculty" as full-time, part-time, or adjunct nontenure track employees whose assignments involve academic responsibilities, including teachers, researchers, and department heads and those in comparable positions; and establishing a separate collective bargaining unit for nontenure track faculty.
Title: State Personnel - Collective Bargaining - Nontenure Track Faculty
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill grants collective bargaining rights to nontenure track faculty members, including full-time, part-time, and adjunct employees, at the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, and St. Mary’s College of Maryland. It requires each of these institutions to establish separate collective bargaining units specifically for nontenure track faculty.
stakeholders: Nontenure track faculty (full-time, part-time, and adjunct) at the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, and St. Mary’s College of Maryland; administrators at these institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase for higher education institutions to reimburse the Public Employee Relations Board for administrative and election expenses. PERB's reimbursable revenues and expenditures will increase minimally. Administrative and personnel costs (including salaries and fringe benefits) at these institutions may increase significantly, depending on the outcome of collective bargaining negotiations. There is no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: PERB is the primary regulatory body tasked with overseeing the collective bargaining process, conducting elections, and managing the newly established faculty bargaining units.
USM is the largest employer impacted by the bill, which extends collective bargaining rights to nontenure track faculty across its constituent institutions.
MSU is explicitly named as one of the state institutions of higher education whose nontenure track faculty are granted collective bargaining rights under the bill.
SMCM is specifically named as one of the state institutions of higher education whose nontenure track faculty are granted collective bargaining rights under the bill.
DBM is the central personnel and budget authority for the state; any fiscal changes resulting from faculty contract negotiations will impact the state budget formulated by this agency.
This commission serves as the state's coordinating board for higher education policy and planning for the institutions impacted by the bill.
This agency is the regulatory and coordinating board for Maryland's public colleges and universities, responsible for statewide policies affecting the faculty at these institutions.
The fiscal note indicates that OAH will need to train its administrative law judges on the bill's provisions and may experience an increase in personnel-related hearings.
The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor for the Public Employee Relations Board and the various state institutions of higher education involved.
The Governor's Office oversees all state departments and institutions, manages the budget process, and is responsible for signing or vetoing the legislation.
The Comptroller manages the state's central payroll system and acts as a fiscal watchdog for revenue impacts related to state employee compensation.
The bill's impact on faculty compensation and status may have long-term fiscal implications for the retirement and pension systems managed by this agency.
The bill references state ethics laws in relation to employee participation in labor organizations.
The bill includes definitions for faculty at the Maryland School for the Deaf as part of the existing statute being amended, though the primary policy change affects higher education faculty.

Synopsis: Establishing the Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program; requiring individuals whose driver's licenses are subject to certain suspension or revocation to participate in the Program; requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue to participants a restricted license requiring the use of an intelligent speed assistance system; and prohibiting a participant from operating a motor vehicle in violation of the requirements of the Program.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program - Establishment
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Technology -see also- AeroT; BioT; EnergyT; InfoT; MedT; etc

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program in Maryland. It requires drivers who have accumulated enough points for license suspension or revocation due to speeding violations to use an intelligent speed assistance system for one year. The Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) will issue restrictive licenses to these participants, certify service providers to install and monitor the systems, and establish fees to cover the program's costs.
stakeholders: Maryland drivers facing license suspension for speeding, manufacturers of intelligent speed assistance systems, and automotive service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to establish a participation fee sufficient to cover the administrative costs of the program, although this fee must be waived for indigent individuals. While a separate Fiscal Note was not provided in the text, the legislation is designed to be self-funded through these fees. The MVA is required to report on the program's implementation and fiscal status by December 2029.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary agency responsible for establishing and managing the Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program, adopting regulations, certifying service providers, issuing restrictive licenses, and monitoring participant compliance.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, the Department of Transportation is responsible for the overall planning and operation of Maryland's multi-modal transportation network and the safety solutions implemented by its business units.

The Governor's Office oversees all state departments and the Motor Vehicle Administration is required to report the implementation and results of the pilot program directly to the Governor by December 2029.

The Office of Administrative Hearings provides the impartial forum for residents to challenge administrative decisions made by the Motor Vehicle Administration, including license suspensions, program removals, or disputes regarding restrictive license requirements.

The Maryland State Police is responsible for highway safety and traffic law enforcement; the pilot program directly impacts the management and monitoring of high-risk speeding offenders whom the MSP identifies through enforcement.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the fiscal accountability of state agencies and will manage the budgetary aspects of the new program, including the establishment of a fee structure intended to cover implementation costs.

The Office of the Attorney General acts as the primary legal advisor to the Motor Vehicle Administration and will be involved in drafting the necessary regulations and providing legal counsel for the enforcement of the pilot program.

The pilot program requires the technical monitoring of vehicle-installed systems and data reporting every 30 days, which aligns with the Department of Information Technology's role in overseeing state IT infrastructure and data security policies.

The Maryland Transportation Authority operates major toll bridges, tunnels, and highways where speeding is a significant safety concern; they will be affected by the restrictive licensing and behavior modification of offenders utilizing their facilities.

Synopsis: Establishing the Release Preparation Program in the Division of Correction for the purpose of providing access to formerly incarcerated individuals to State correctional facilities to assist incarcerated individuals with release preparation; and altering the purposes of the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund to include providing funds to cover the costs of supporting the Release Preparation Program.
Title: Division of Correction - Release Preparation Program
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 2:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill establishes the Release Preparation Program within the Division of Correction to allow formerly incarcerated individuals to access State correctional facilities to assist currently incarcerated individuals with release preparation. The program is funded through the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund.
responsible_party: Division of Correction, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals and formerly incarcerated individuals
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund (CREF) may increase starting in FY 2027 to cover program costs, such as a program coordinator estimated at $90,008. If the CREF balance is insufficient, cannabis tax revenues used to backfill the fund will reduce distributions to the State general fund, other special funds, and local governments. Consequently, local government revenues and expenditures may decrease beginning in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing the Division of Correction, it is responsible for establishing and implementing the Release Preparation Program and managing access to its facilities.
The bill specifically requires the Division of Correction to submit its registration protocol for the Release Preparation Program to the Attorney General for approval.
The bill alters the purpose and allowable uses of the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund, which is administered by this agency, to support the new program.
The Comptroller is tasked with accounting for the program's funding source and managing tax revenue distributions that may be impacted by the bill's fiscal requirements.
The Treasurer is mandated to hold the program's funding source separately and invest its money in the same manner as other State funds.
The bill explicitly subjects the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund, which now supports this program, to audit by this agency.

bill_summary: This bill requires the governing board of each institution of higher education in Maryland and each local school system to designate a Title VI Coordinator to ensure compliance with Title VI of the federal Civil Rights Act of 1964. These coordinators are responsible for overseeing compliance with laws prohibiting discrimination based on race, color, or national origin, promoting equal access to programs, providing training, investigating complaints, and maintaining relevant records.
responsible_party: The governing body of each institution of higher education and each local school system
stakeholders: Students, parents, guardians, and staff at Maryland institutions of higher education and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: The associated Fiscal and Policy Note was not provided in the text. However, the bill mandates the designation of Title VI Coordinators and the performance of specific oversight and investigative duties, which likely results in administrative expenditures for local school systems and institutions of higher education.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), as it oversees the local school systems required to designate Title VI Coordinators. Furthermore, the bill explicitly authorizes individuals to file discrimination complaints with the State Superintendent, who heads the MSDE.

The bill requires the governing board of each institution of higher education in the State to designate a Title VI Coordinator. MHEC is the primary regulatory and coordinating board for these institutions and will be responsible for overseeing statewide compliance and policy alignment.

This agency, identical to MHEC in scope, is the regulatory body for Maryland’s public and private colleges and universities, all of which must comply with the bill's requirement to appoint a Title VI Coordinator and manage discrimination complaints.

As the umbrella organization for 12 public universities, the USM is a primary implementing entity. Its member institutions' governing boards must comply with the mandate to designate coordinators, oversee Title VI compliance, and investigate complaints.

As an independent public university and state agency, Morgan State University's governing board is directly required by the bill to designate a Title VI Coordinator to manage compliance, training, and investigations on its campus.

As Maryland's public honors college, the institution's governing board must designate a Title VI Coordinator and ensure the college meets the administrative and reporting requirements mandated by the bill.

As an independent state agency that provides public K-21 education, the Maryland School for the Deaf operates similarly to a local school system and would be required to ensure Title VI compliance and complaint documentation through a designated coordinator.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to MSDE, MHEC, and the state universities. It will be responsible for providing legal guidance on the implementation of the Title VI Coordinator roles and defending agencies in cases of alleged discrimination.

The bill focuses on Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (non-discrimination in federally funded programs). This aligns with the MCCR's mission to enforce anti-discrimination laws and ensure equal opportunity in public accommodations and employment across the state.

DBM oversees the state's personnel system and budget. It may be impacted if state-run educational institutions or agencies require additional funding or the creation of new staff positions to fulfill the Title VI Coordinator requirements.

The MCSS is dedicated to fostering 'safe and inclusive learning environments' for K-12 students. The requirement for Title VI Coordinators to oversee non-discrimination compliance is directly relevant to the 'inclusive' aspect of the Center’s mission.
