Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill changes the compensation structure for the elected members and the president of the Montgomery County Board of Education. Instead of fixed annual salaries of $25,000 for members and $29,000 for the president, their compensation will be tied to the salary of a member of the Maryland General Assembly. Elected board members will receive the same annual compensation as a General Assembly member, and the board president will receive that amount plus an additional $10,000.
stakeholders: Elected members of the Montgomery County Board of Education and Montgomery County taxpayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in a local expenditure increase for Montgomery County to provide higher salaries for members of the Board of Education. Salaries for the seven elected members will increase from their current levels ($25,000 for members and $29,000 for the president) to match the salaries of the Maryland General Assembly (currently $50,330) plus an additional $10,000 for the president. There is no impact on state revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing Maryland's public K-12 education system and local boards of education, the department is relevant to legislation that alters the governance and compensation structures of its constituent local boards.

The agency manages retirement plans for local school board members and employees; changes to annual compensation directly impact earnable compensation levels, pension benefit calculations, and the system's actuarial liabilities.

The OAG reviews legislation for legal and constitutional sufficiency; this bill specifically addresses Article III, Section 35 of the Maryland Constitution regarding the restriction on altering the compensation of public officials during their term of office.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person with the intent to defraud another from creating, aiding in the creation of, or possessing a counterfeit lease or rental agreement.
Title: Criminal Law - Counterfeiting and Possession of Counterfeit Lease - Penalty
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill prohibits a person from creating, assisting in the creation of, or possessing a counterfeit lease or rental agreement with the intent to defraud. Violations involving counterfeiting are classified as a felony subject to up to 10 years imprisonment and/or a fine of $1,000, while possession of a counterfeit lease is a misdemeanor subject to up to 3 years imprisonment and/or a fine of $1,000.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Landlords, tenants, property owners, and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's creation of new criminal penalties may lead to a minimal increase in state and local expenditures for incarceration and a minimal increase in state revenues from fines collected in criminal cases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General serves as the state's primary legal advisor and manages criminal appeals. This bill creates new criminal offenses for counterfeiting and possessing leases, which impacts the OAG's role in upholding criminal law and public interest.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender provides legal representation to indigent residents facing potential loss of liberty. The creation of new felony and misdemeanor charges for counterfeit leases will directly impact their caseload and defense responsibilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages the state's adult correctional system. The bill establishes specific prison terms for new counterfeiting offenses, which will impact the management of incarcerated individuals and community supervision services.

The Maryland State Police is the primary statewide law enforcement agency responsible for investigating major crimes, including fraud. They would lead investigations into organized counterfeiting or fraudulent activities involving leases and rental agreements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the state's central hub for public safety policy and funding. This legislation amends the criminal code and establishes new penalties, which aligns with their mission to advise the Governor on criminal justice strategies.

The AOC provides the infrastructure for the state's court system. The bill specifically mentions jurisdiction related to filings with the clerk of the circuit court and creates new criminal proceedings that will be handled by the judiciary.

The bill explicitly includes instances where a counterfeit instrument is filed with the Register of Wills as a criterion for determining the jurisdiction for prosecution, involving the agency in the legal verification of documents.

The DHCD is responsible for housing accessibility and neighborhood revitalization. The use of counterfeit leases is a significant form of housing fraud that can undermine the programs and markets the agency manages.
As the state's fiscal watchdog, the Comptroller's office may encounter counterfeit leases used in fraudulent attempts to claim tax credits or during revenue collection audits.
The Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation and overseeing the agencies tasked with enforcing these new criminal laws and penalties.

Synopsis: Establishing a Class C-PCL (premium cigar lounge) alcoholic beverages license for use in conjunction with a certain tobacco products retailer license; authorizing a local licensing board to issue the license; prohibiting a county clerk from issuing a certain tobacco products retailer license if the location is adjacent to a health care facility or a child care facility; exempting a holder of a certain tobacco products retailer license from the Clean Indoor Air Act; providing an annual license fee of $100; etc.

bill_summary: The Maryland Premium Cigar Lounge Act of 2026 establishes a Class C–PCL (premium cigar lounge) alcoholic beverages license for retail tobacco businesses (tobacconists). The license allows customers to consume their own alcoholic beverages on-site provided they purchase a product from the establishment. The bill exempts these lounges from the Clean Indoor Air Act if they meet specific air filtration, signage, and revenue standards, while also prohibiting new tobacconist licenses for locations adjacent to health care or child care facilities.
responsible_party: Local alcoholic beverages licensing boards, the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission, and the Clerks of the Circuit Court.
stakeholders: Retail tobacco business owners (tobacconists), cigar lounge patrons, employees of premium cigar lounges, and state/local tobacco and alcohol regulators.
fiscal_impact_summary: Local government revenues will increase through a $100 annual fee for each Class C–PCL license, though issuance is limited by county population. State administrative expenditures for the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission will increase minimally to manage a registry of exempt businesses and process annual sales ratio reports. No specific state funding is mandated or allocated by the bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill prohibits County Clerks (who are part of the Maryland Judiciary and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts) from issuing certain tobacco products retailer licenses if the location is adjacent to a health care or child care facility.

The bill amends the Clean Indoor Air Act, which the Department of Health oversees, and restricts license issuance near 'licensed health care facilities,' which are licensed and regulated by the Department.

The bill requires employees of cigar lounges to sign acknowledgments regarding exposure to secondhand smoke, which involves occupational safety and health standards (MOSH) managed by the Department of Labor.
The bill prohibits the issuance of certain tobacco retailer licenses adjacent to 'licensed child care facilities,' which are regulated and certified by the Maryland State Department of Education.
As the state's chief financial officer and fiscal watchdog, the Comptroller oversees various business licenses and revenue collection related to tobacco and alcoholic beverages.
The bill requires reporting to the Executive Director of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission, an executive branch body overseen by the Governor's Office.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies and local licensing boards regarding the implementation and enforcement of new licensing categories and regulatory exemptions.

Synopsis: Requiring a court to notify the United States Postmaster General of a certain conviction involving the theft, taking, or opening of mail or packages, under certain circumstances.
Title: Criminal Law - Theft and Opening of Mail and Packages
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill establishes the theft of mail or packages as a felony punishable by up to five years in prison and prohibits the unauthorized opening of letters. It requires Maryland courts to notify the U.S. Postmaster General of convictions involving items delivered by the U.S. Postal Service and mandates that convicted individuals pay the associated administrative costs.
stakeholders: Maryland residents who receive mail and packages, delivery service companies, the United States Postal Service, and individuals prosecuted for mail or package theft.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires defendants to pay administrative costs associated with court-mandated notifications to the U.S. Postmaster General. The establishment of a new felony for mail theft may increase state expenditures related to incarceration. No specific revenue or expenditure estimates from a Fiscal Note were provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the court system notify the United States Postmaster General of specific convictions and requires defendants to pay administrative costs associated with those notifications. The AOC manages the administrative, technological, and financial infrastructure for the Maryland Judiciary, including record-keeping and fiscal management of court-ordered costs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation establishes a new felony for mail or package theft carrying a penalty of up to 5 years of imprisonment. This directly impacts the department's responsibility for managing adult correctional facilities, pretrial detention, and the Division of Parole and Probation for those convicted under the new statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The creation of a new felony and the modification of misdemeanor penalties will directly impact the caseload of the OPD, which provides legal representation to indigent residents facing criminal charges and potential incarceration in Maryland.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the MSP is responsible for investigating criminal violations. The establishment of new felony crimes related to mail and package theft falls under their enforcement jurisdiction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The GOCPP serves as the central hub for public safety policy and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies. This bill introduces a significant policy change regarding theft crimes and judicial reporting requirements.

The OAG manages all criminal appeals in both state and federal courts. The establishment of new criminal offenses and felony penalties is likely to result in litigation and appeals that the OAG must handle on behalf of the state.
The bill defines new criminal offenses for which youth may be referred to the juvenile justice system. DJS is responsible for the supervision and rehabilitation of youth involved in such cases.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions relating to the responsibilities of the Department of Human Services as representative payee and fiduciary for certain children committed to the custody of the Department; requiring the Department to use certain benefits in a manner that is in the best interest of the child for the child's current unmet needs; etc.
Title: Department of Human Services - Benefits for Children in Custody - Alterations
Status: In the House - First Reading Appropriations
bill_summary: This bill modifies the Department of Human Services' (DHS) responsibilities regarding federal benefits for children in its custody, such as Social Security and Veterans Affairs benefits. It prohibits the state from using these benefits to reimburse itself for the cost of foster care, requires DHS to seek alternative representative payees before acting as one, and mandates that these funds be used for the child's unmet needs—including education, technology, and housing—or conserved for their future. The bill also requires DHS to screen all children for benefit eligibility within 60 days of entering care and provides for enhanced financial counseling.
stakeholders: Children in Maryland's foster care system, the Maryland Department of Human Services, and attorneys or guardians ad litem representing children in custody.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will likely cause a decrease in State general fund revenue because the Department of Human Services can no longer use federal benefits to offset the cost of providing foster care. Additionally, the State may see an increase in administrative expenditures to implement mandatory annual benefit eligibility screenings for all children in custody and to comply with expanded notification and financial literacy requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Family Law Article to alter the responsibilities of the Department of Human Services as a representative payee and fiduciary for children in its custody, including benefit screening, management, and notification requirements.
The bill specifically identifies the establishment of a 529A plan (Maryland ABLE) as a mandated option for conserving a child's benefits in a manner that avoids federal asset limits.
The State Treasurer's Office oversees Maryland 529 and the Maryland ABLE program, which the bill requires the Department of Human Services to use for the conservation of children's benefits.

The bill creates a new judicial process requiring the court to grant requests from beneficiaries who are at least 18 years old to use their benefits for unmet needs, if determined to be in their best interest.

The bill requires the state to seek coverage for benefit eligibility screenings through the Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) benefit, which is a component of the Medicaid program administered by the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill aligns with the mission of the Governor's Office for Children to coordinate agency efforts to improve the well-being of children and families and to eliminate childhood poverty for vulnerable youth.
The bill prohibits the use of a child's benefits to reimburse the state for costs of care, which has a notable fiscal impact on the state's general fund and budget management.

The bill regulates the management of U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs benefits for children in state custody; the DVMF serves as the state's resource hub for residents navigating these federal benefits.

The bill addresses needs related to a child's disability, transition services for youth leaving state care, and the establishment of special needs trusts, which are core policy areas for the Department of Disabilities.

As the primary legal advisor for state agencies, the OAG will be responsible for advising the Department of Human Services on its altered fiduciary duties and the legal requirements for appealing benefit denials.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Department of Human Services to coordinate and consult with a child's attorney regarding benefit applications, appeals, and financial accounting; the OPD often provides legal representation for children in juvenile court proceedings.

bill_summary: This emergency bill requires the State Board of Social Work Examiners to issue conditional licenses to applicants for bachelor or master social work licenses who have met education and experience requirements but have not yet passed the required examination. It establishes an alternative pathway to full licensure through the completion of 1,500 hours of supervised practice as an alternative to passing the exam. bill_summary: The bill increases the minimum age requirement for a vehicle to be registered as a historic motor vehicle or a street rod. Additionally, a street rod must be at least 40 years old, an increase from the previous requirement of 25 years. It mandates that local governments allow these housing types by right on certain vacant single-family lots and in a portion of new residential subdivisions. stakeholders: Maryland residents, local governments, residential developers, and property owners

As the principal executive agency responsible for overseeing all state departments and signing or vetoing legislation, the Governor's Office will manage the broad policy shift toward increased housing density and the inter-agency coordination required by the bill.

They coordinate statewide initiatives to reduce crime and advise the Governor on criminal justice strategies, making this specific criminal law legislation highly relevant to their mission.

The OAG manages all criminal appeals and provides expert legal counsel to the state. They would be involved in defending convictions under this new law during the appeals process and providing legal guidance on the statute's implementation.

If juveniles are involved in the theft of mail or packages, DJS would be responsible for the intake, supervision, and rehabilitation of those youth under the new criminal guidelines established by the Act.

DBM oversees the state budget and estimates fiscal impacts. Because this bill creates a new felony that could increase incarceration costs and impact the judiciary's fiscal operations regarding restitution interest, DBM would need to account for these changes in the state's financial planning.

Synopsis: Requiring the prosecuting attorney of thefts of property or services with a value of less than $1,500 to notify the victim or the victim's representative about each court proceeding, the right of the victim to submit a victim impact statement, any posttrial court proceedings, any appeal, and any sentence review related to the case.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Theft - Notification of Victims and Victims' Representatives
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill requires prosecuting attorneys to provide specific notifications to victims or their representatives in theft cases involving property or services valued at less than $1,500. Notifications must cover court proceedings, the victim's right to submit impact statements, post-trial proceedings, appeals, and sentence reviews.
stakeholders: Victims of theft crimes involving property or services valued under $1,500 and State's Attorney's Offices.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected. Local expenditures may increase minimally for State's Attorneys' Offices to provide the required notifications for these additional cases.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's central hub for public safety policy and victim services, GOCPP is responsible for coordinating statewide initiatives and administering grants to support victim services, making the mandate for victim notification in theft cases directly relevant to their oversight of criminal justice policy and victim advocacy.

The OAG is responsible for managing all criminal appeals in the state. Since the bill specifically requires that victims be notified of any appeal and posttrial court proceedings, the OAG's appellate division would be directly involved in the stages of litigation where these notifications are required.

The AOC provides the administrative and technological infrastructure for the Maryland Judiciary. While the duty to notify falls on the prosecutor, the AOC manages the court systems, calendars, and records for the proceedings that victims must be notified about.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS provides support services to victims of crime and manages community supervision. The requirements regarding victim impact statements and sentence reviews intersect with the agency's role in managing post-conviction processes and victim advocacy.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to prohibit police officers from affiliating with, supporting, or advocating for White supremacist groups, ideologies, or causes or participating in or actively promoting a certain extremist group.
Title: Public Safety - Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission - Prohibition Against Certain Affiliation or Support by Police Officers
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to adopt regulations that prohibit police officers from affiliating with, supporting, or advocating for White supremacist groups, ideologies, or causes, or from participating in or actively promoting extremist groups.
responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
stakeholders: Maryland police officers and the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services increase by a minimal amount in fiscal 2025 to update the commission's database. The bill does not affect state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC) is an independent body housed within this department. The department provides administrative and logistical support for the commission that is tasked with establishing and enforcing these standards.

As the state’s primary law enforcement agency, all Maryland State Police officers are directly subject to the training and conduct standards established by the MPTSC, making this bill highly relevant to their personnel policy and professional standards.

The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor to the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission and would be responsible for providing legal counsel regarding the implementation and defense of these new prohibitions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office is the state’s central hub for public safety policy and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies, directly overlapping with the policy implications of regulating police officer conduct and affiliations.

The MDTA operates a dedicated police force whose officers must comply with all standards set by the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, meaning these prohibitions will impact their internal regulations.
The MTA operates its own police force to secure transit systems, and its officers are subject to the conduct and certification requirements mandated by the state commission.
The DNR manages the Natural Resources Police, a statewide law enforcement agency whose officers are certified and trained under the standards set by the Commission.
DGS manages the Maryland Capitol Police, a law enforcement unit that must follow the professional standards and prohibitions established for police officers in the state.
USM member institutions employ campus police officers who are regulated by the state’s police training and standards, requiring the system to ensure their officers comply with the new prohibitions.
Morgan State University maintains its own police department whose officers are subject to state training and standards commission requirements.
As a state agency with a campus police presence, the college must ensure its officers adhere to the conduct standards set by the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission.

The bill's focus on prohibiting white supremacist and extremist affiliations aligns with the MCCR's mission to enforce anti-discrimination laws and protect civil rights within the state government and its agencies.

This center is involved in the training and coordination of School Resource Officers (SROs), who are sworn police officers subject to the standards of the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission.
The Judiciary employs bailiffs and other security personnel who may be sworn police officers subject to these state standards.

Synopsis: Requiring that a carrier's internal grievance process provide for human review of grievances resulting from adverse decisions made using artificial intelligence, algorithm, or other software tools; requiring carriers to report certain information on grievances resulting from adverse decisions made using artificial intelligence, algorithm, or other software tools; requiring a carrier to provide a model review process under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Artificial Intelligence - Grievance Process and Reporting (AI Health Insurance Accountability Act of 2026)
Status: In the House - First Reading Health

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: The AI Health Insurance Accountability Act of 2026 requires health insurance carriers to provide human review for grievances when an adverse decision was originally made using artificial intelligence, algorithms, or other software tools. It also mandates that carriers report specific information regarding these grievances and provide a model review process under certain circumstances.
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, Maryland consumers/policyholders, and the Maryland Insurance Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will likely increase administrative and operational expenditures for the Maryland Insurance Administration to monitor compliance and manage new reporting requirements. Health insurance carriers will incur costs related to implementing human review protocols and reporting AI-specific grievance data.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of the state's insurance industry, the MIA is responsible for enforcing the bill's requirements regarding internal grievance processes, AI-driven adverse decisions, and mandatory reporting by carriers.

The OAG's Consumer Protection Division, specifically the Health Education and Advocacy Unit, manages health insurance complaints and would be directly involved in the legal and consumer advocacy implications of AI-driven medical denials.
The MHBE oversees the health plans offered through Maryland Health Connection; the new requirements for AI human review and reporting would apply to the carriers participating in the exchange.
The MDH oversees the state's Medicaid program and Managed Care Organizations (MCOs), which function similarly to carriers and may utilize AI tools for clinical and coverage decisions.

The MHCC is responsible for health system planning and quality reporting; tracking grievances related to AI technology aligns with their mission to provide transparency and evaluate the performance of the healthcare system.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies, including the Maryland Insurance Administration; disputes over AI-driven adverse decisions and grievance procedural compliance may result in hearings before Administrative Law Judges.

The DBM manages the health benefit plans for Maryland's state workforce; regulatory changes affecting how carriers handle grievances for AI-driven decisions will impact the administration of these employee benefits.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of recycling to exclude certain chemical conversion processes, pyrolysis, hydropyrolysis, methanolysis, gasification, enzymatic breakdown, or similar processes as determined by the Department of the Environment; and prohibiting a person from building in the State a facility that converts plastic to fuel or feedstock through a chemical conversion process.
Title: Recycling - Prohibition on the Chemical Conversion of Plastic
Status: In the House - First Reading Environment and Transportation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: This bill modifies the legal definition of recycling to exclude various chemical conversion processes, including pyrolysis, gasification, and enzymatic breakdown. It also prohibits the construction of any facility in Maryland that converts plastic into fuel or feedstock using these chemical conversion methods.
stakeholders: Plastic recycling and waste management industries, facility developers, environmental advocacy groups, and the Maryland Department of the Environment.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's prohibition on the construction of chemical conversion facilities for plastic may prevent potential future capital investments and associated tax revenues. The Maryland Department of the Environment would be responsible for updating regulations and oversight, which is expected to be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator for environmental protection and waste management, MDE is directly responsible for implementing recycling laws. The bill explicitly grants MDE the authority to determine processes similar to those excluded and impacts their oversight of recycling targets and facility permitting.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the Department of the Environment and the Governor, and would be responsible for defending the state's new regulatory prohibitions and ensuring enforcement of the chemical conversion ban.

MES provides technical and operational services for solid waste management and recycling. A change in the definition of recycling and the prohibition on chemical conversion facilities directly affects their long-term project planning and operational strategies for waste reduction.

The bill's prohibition on building specific industrial facilities affects the state's industrial policy and business attraction efforts, particularly for companies in the advanced recycling and waste-to-value sectors.

The MCEC facilitates climate and clean energy technologies; a ban on plastic-to-fuel facilities limits the scope of energy recovery technologies and circular economy projects the center can support or finance.

MEDCO issues revenue bonds and facilitates large-scale industrial projects. This legislation removes certain chemical conversion facilities from the pool of potential infrastructure projects the agency could develop or finance.

The MEA manages grants and programs for renewable and reliable energy. The prohibition on converting plastic to fuel directly impacts potential energy production projects that utilize chemical conversion technologies.

The Department of Planning coordinates land use and sustainable growth. The bill implements specific land-use restrictions by prohibiting the construction of certain industrial facilities in the state.

This multi-agency initiative focuses on environmental stewardship and sustainable growth; the bill's focus on refining the definition of recycling aligns with the initiative's goals for resource conservation.

TEDCO supports early-stage technology companies. The prohibition on chemical conversion and enzymatic breakdown processes for plastics could impact startups and venture capital investments in the green technology sector.

The PSC regulates certain energy generation processes. If gasification facilities were intended for power generation, this prohibition would intersect with the commission's regulatory oversight of new generating stations.
The Governor's Office oversees executive departments including MDE and is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation that significantly impacts state environmental policy.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an employer from taking certain discriminatory employment actions against a fire and rescue public safety employee based on the employee's use of medical cannabis, subject to certain conditions; and requiring an employer to report an incident of a fire and rescue public safety employee reporting for work while impaired by cannabis to the State Emergency Medical Services Board.
Title: Employment Discrimination - Fire and Rescue Public Safety Employees - Use of Medical Cannabis
Status: In the House - First Reading Economic Matters
bill_summary: This bill prohibits employers from taking discriminatory employment actions against fire and rescue public safety employees based on their status as a medical cannabis patient or their use of medical cannabis, provided conditions are met. It also mandates that employers report any instance of such an employee reporting to work while impaired by cannabis to the State Emergency Medical Services Board.
stakeholders: Fire and rescue public safety employees, fire departments, and local government employers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal fiscal impact on state and local governments. Potential increases in expenditures relate to administrative reporting and the handling of any additional discrimination complaints by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires employers to report incidents of fire and rescue employees reporting for work while impaired to the State Emergency Medical Services Board, which is the governing body for the system coordinated by MIEMSS. Additionally, MIEMSS licenses and certifies the clinicians affected by this legislation.

The Commission is the primary agency responsible for enforcing anti-discrimination laws in Maryland. This bill creates a new protected category or condition (medical cannabis use) for fire and rescue employees, directly falling under the agency's mandate to investigate and resolve employment discrimination complaints.

Fire and rescue personnel are public employees who are often members of collective bargaining units. The board oversees labor relations and unfair labor practices, making it relevant to any legislation that changes employment terms or disciplinary standards for public safety workers.

The MCA regulates medical and adult-use cannabis in Maryland. Legislation defining the rights and protections of medical cannabis users, particularly in the workforce, intersects with the agency's role in public education and industry oversight.

The Department of Labor administers unemployment insurance and oversees workforce standards. The bill's provisions regarding employer disciplinary actions and impairment reporting impact general labor relations and employment law.

The OAG acts as the chief legal advisor for state agencies. It would be responsible for providing legal guidance to MIEMSS and the Commission on Civil Rights regarding the implementation and enforcement of the bill's non-discrimination and reporting requirements.

As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office oversees the departments involved in implementing this policy (MIEMSS, Labor, etc.) and is responsible for signing and enforcing laws related to public safety and civil rights.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Commerce to authorize an eligible fund manager to receive, use, and retain a certain management fee; and authorizing the Department to set an annual cap on the cumulative amount of certain management fees an eligible fund manager may receive.
Title: Economic Development - Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Accounts - Management Fees (Small Business Increased Access to Capital Act)
Status: In the House - First Reading Economic Matters

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: The bill authorizes the Maryland Department of Commerce to allow eligible fund managers for the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account to receive and retain management fees. It also grants the Department the authority to set an annual cap on the total amount of management fees a fund manager can collect.
stakeholders: Small, minority, and women-owned businesses in Maryland and eligible fund managers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no significant impact on state or local finances. It alters the accounting mechanism for management fees within the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account, allowing managers to retain fees directly. While this may change the specific flow of special funds, it does not change the total amount of funding available to the program or result in new state expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Department of Commerce as the authority responsible for authorizing fund managers to receive management fees and setting annual caps on those fees within the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office oversees procurement and participation programs for the target demographics of the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account, making them a primary stakeholder in policies affecting these funds.

As the custodian of state financial assets and the manager of public funds, the Treasurer's Office has a role in the oversight of accounts and investment mechanisms like those used for small business capital access.
The Comptroller serves as the state's fiscal watchdog and chief financial officer, providing oversight on state revenues and the distribution of funds from state-managed accounts.
DBM oversees the state's operating budget and ensures fiscal accountability, making them relevant to changes in how management fees are retained and capped within state-supported programs.

OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of executive agencies. Changes to how fund managers use and retain state-allocated fees would be subject to their auditing procedures to ensure compliance with the new law.

Synopsis: Requiring the Public Service Commission to adopt regulations related to the construction of a generating station that is co-located with a data center but is not interconnected with the electric transmission system or electric distribution system.
Title: Maryland Co-Location Energy Innovation and Reliability Act
Status: In the House - First Reading Environment and Transportation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: The Maryland Co-Location Energy Innovation and Reliability Act requires the Public Service Commission to develop and adopt regulations for the construction of electricity generating stations that are co-located with data centers but do not connect to the public electric transmission or distribution systems.
stakeholders: Data center developers and operators, electric generation companies, and the Maryland Public Service Commission

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary agency named in the bill, specifically tasked with adopting regulations for the construction of generating stations co-located with data centers.
The MEA is responsible for promoting reliable and innovative energy solutions; this bill directly involves energy technology and infrastructure innovation related to behind-the-meter generation.
The MDE regulates air quality and environmental permits for power plants; any new generating station, even if not interconnected to the grid, must comply with state environmental standards.
The DNR, through the Power Plant Research Program, is typically involved in the scientific and technical review of new power plant construction and its impact on the state's natural resources.
The OAG acts as the legal advisor to the Public Service Commission and will be responsible for reviewing the legality of the new regulations and defending the commission in case of litigation.

The Department of Commerce promotes economic development, and data centers are a significant sector of Maryland’s business attraction strategy; co-location energy solutions impact the state's competitiveness in this industry.

The OPC advocates for residential utility consumers; while the generating stations are not interconnected, the office has an interest in how such configurations affect the broader reliability and cost structure of the electric grid.
The MDP coordinates land use and sustainable growth; the construction of large generating stations and data centers requires significant land use planning and adherence to smart growth strategies.

DoIT manages state IT strategy and cybersecurity standards; as data centers are central to this bill and cybersecurity is a listed subject, the agency’s expertise is relevant to policy implementation.
As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office oversees the implementation of major energy and economic initiatives and manages the regulatory boards involved.

Synopsis: Updating certain provisions of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future that refer to "behavioral health" to be inclusive of "student well-being and human flourishing"; and amending the purposes, membership, and duties of the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports to include the furtherance of student well-being and human flourishing.
Title: Education - Behavioral Health and Student Well-Being and Human Flourishing (Maryland Student Well-Being and Flourishing Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/18 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: The Maryland Student Well-Being and Flourishing Act updates the Blueprint for Maryland's Future by broadening the definition of behavioral health to explicitly include student well-being and human flourishing. It further amends the membership, duties, and purposes of the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports to incorporate these concepts into their administrative and supportive functions for students.
responsible_party: Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports
stakeholders: Maryland primary and secondary students, local school systems, and the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is clarifying and descriptive in nature and does not directly affect state or local finances; it does not mandate specific new funding or change existing revenue structures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing the Maryland public K-12 education system and the implementation of the 'Blueprint for Maryland’s Future,' MSDE is the lead agency responsible for incorporating 'student well-being and human flourishing' into educational standards and practices.

The Maryland Department of Health manages behavioral health services and coordinates with the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports. Amending the Consortium's duties directly impacts health-related programming and policy within schools.

The Governor's Office oversees the operations of all state departments and spearheads statewide initiatives like the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future, which this bill proposes to amend regarding student well-being.

The GOC leads a 'whole-of-government' approach to child well-being. This bill's focus on student flourishing and well-being directly aligns with the agency's mission to address the needs and stability of children.

MCSS is dedicated to fostering safe and inclusive learning environments and coordinates work between schools and mental health professionals, making the shift to a 'flourishing' and 'well-being' framework highly relevant to their training and resources.

DBM oversees the Governor’s annual operating budget and evaluates the fiscal impact of modifications to the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future, ensuring resources are properly allocated for new state priorities.

Synopsis: Providing an addition modification under the Maryland income tax for the gain from the sale or exchange of certain small business stock excluded from federal gross income and a certain amount of fines, penalties, and trade or business expenses; providing certain modifications to the federal adjusted gross income of an individual or federal taxable income of a corporation for Maryland income tax purposes relating to certain deductions under the federal income tax for the depreciation of certain property; etc.
Title: Income Tax - Addition Modifications - Business Stock Gains, Fines, Penalties, and Bonus Depreciation
Status: In the House - First Reading Ways and Means

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill requires taxpayers to include certain income and expenses in their Maryland taxable income that are currently excluded or deducted from their federal adjusted gross income. Specifically, it establishes addition modifications for gains from the sale of small business stock, certain fines and penalties, and adjustments related to federal bonus depreciation deductions for both individuals and corporations.
stakeholders: Individual and corporate taxpayers in Maryland, specifically those who sell small business stock, pay business-related fines or penalties, or utilize federal bonus depreciation deductions.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase state income tax revenues by broadening the tax base through addition modifications. These modifications require taxpayers to add back certain federal deductions and exclusions to their Maryland taxable income. Specific fiscal estimates for revenues and expenditures were not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's independent tax collector and chief financial officer, the Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering income tax laws, processing the proposed addition modifications, and managing the resulting revenue collection from individuals and corporations.

DBM is responsible for estimating state revenues and formulating the annual operating budget; changes to income tax modifications for business stock, fines, and depreciation directly impact revenue projections and the state's fiscal planning.

The Governor's Office oversees the operations of all state departments, signs or vetoes legislation, and drafts the annual budget, making it directly responsible for the policy direction and final approval of major tax code changes.

The Department of Commerce is tasked with stimulating private investment and supporting small businesses; modifications to tax treatments of small business stock gains and bonus depreciation are significant factors in the state's economic development and business attraction strategy.

The Maryland Tax Court is the administrative agency that adjudicates disputes regarding state income tax assessments; it would be the forum for controversies arising from the application of these new addition modifications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advocates for and connects small business entrepreneurs to opportunities; the proposed addition modification for certain small business stock gains directly impacts the financial environment for their constituents.

TEDCO provides funding and resources to early-stage technology companies; tax policy changes regarding the sale or exchange of small business stock directly affect the investment landscape and exit strategies for the startups they support.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the Comptroller and the General Assembly, and would be responsible for defending the state's application of these income tax modifications in court or providing guidance on their implementation.

The Treasurer's Office manages the investment of the state's public funds and sits on the Board of Public Works; fluctuations in state income tax revenue resulting from these modifications affect the overall management of state financial assets.

OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of state agencies, including the Comptroller; they would be responsible for ensuring that the new tax modifications are applied correctly and that revenues are handled according to the updated state law.

Synopsis: Providing that the contents of a certain intercepted communication and evidence derived from the communication may be received in evidence in a certain proceeding under certain circumstances.
Title: Wiretapping and Electronic Surveillance - Intercepted Communications - Admissibility of Evidence
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill allows evidence from intercepted communications, such as wiretaps, to be admitted in Maryland court proceedings if the interception was conducted legally in another jurisdiction and was not done at the request of Maryland law enforcement.
stakeholders: Law enforcement, legal professionals, and individuals involved in criminal or civil litigation.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no fiscal impact on state or local government revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OAG acts as the state's chief legal advisor and handles criminal and civil appeals. This bill directly affects the rules of evidence admissibility for intercepted communications, which is critical to their prosecution and litigation duties.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the MSP uses electronic surveillance in investigations. Changes to the admissibility of wiretap evidence directly impact their investigative protocols and the success of their criminal cases.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD provides legal defense to indigent residents in criminal cases. Admissibility standards for intercepted communications are a primary concern for defense strategies and the protection of defendants' constitutional rights.

The OSP investigates and prosecutes multi-jurisdictional crimes and government corruption. These complex cases frequently rely on electronic surveillance, making the admissibility of such evidence highly relevant to their mission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The GOCPP is the central hub for public safety policy in Maryland. This bill proposes a significant change in criminal procedure policy, which the GOCPP monitors and coordinates to improve the state's justice system.

The AOC supports the Maryland Judiciary by managing court policies and providing training for judges and court staff. Changes to evidence admissibility require administrative coordination and educational updates for the judiciary.

The DJS oversees youth in the juvenile justice system. Rules regarding evidence admissibility in legal proceedings apply to juvenile delinquency cases, impacting the agency's legal and rehabilitative processes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for public safety and the state's adult correctional system. While not the primary legal actor, they are impacted by changes in the investigative and prosecutorial framework that lead to incarceration.
The Governor's Office oversees the enforcement of state laws and reviews all legislation passed by the General Assembly, particularly high-impact changes to the criminal and civil codes.

Synopsis: Altering certain requirements of the career ladder for educators to increase the required percentage of working time a teacher on level one, two, or three of the career ladder must spend teaching in the classroom from 60% to 80%.
Title: Public Schools - Career Ladder - Teacher Classroom Teaching Time
Status: In the House - First Reading Ways and Means

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases the minimum amount of time that public school teachers at levels one, two, or three of the educator career ladder must spend teaching in the classroom, raising the requirement from 60% to 80% of their working time.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and local boards of education
stakeholders: Maryland public school teachers on career ladder levels one, two, and three

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary agency responsible for overseeing public K-12 education and academic standards. This bill directly alters the 'career ladder' for educators, which is a core component of the MSDE-led implementation of the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future.

As the agency responsible for labor relations and collective bargaining for public school employees, the board is directly impacted by changes to teacher workload and mandated teaching time, which are fundamental conditions of employment.

The DBM oversees the state’s annual budget and educational funding. Adjustments to the educator career ladder and teaching time requirements may have significant fiscal implications for the state’s long-term Blueprint funding and local school system allocations.

The MLDS Center tracks student and workforce data, including teacher career pathways. This bill's changes to career ladder requirements provide critical data points for the MLDS to research the effectiveness of education policies on labor outcomes.

OLA conducts performance audits to evaluate the efficiency of state programs. They would likely monitor the implementation of these new career ladder teaching requirements to ensure fiscal and programmatic compliance within MSDE.

The Governor’s Office oversees the operations of all state departments and spearheads statewide initiatives focused on economic opportunity and child well-being, including the landmark Blueprint for Maryland’s Future policy changes.

Synopsis: Establishing the Aging Resilience Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund; requiring the Fund to be used to carry out the mission of the Department of Aging including personnel, partnership development, and any programs, services, or activities within the Department; and requiring interest earnings of the Fund to be credited to the Fund.
Title: Department of Aging - Aging Resilience Fund - Establishment
Status: In the House - First Reading Health

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Aging Resilience Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund within the Maryland Department of Aging. The fund is intended to support the department's mission, including personnel, partnership development, and various programs and services for older adults. Interest earnings of the fund are to be credited back to the fund.
stakeholders: Older adults in Maryland, Maryland Department of Aging personnel, and community partners providing senior services.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount starting in fiscal 2025. General fund interest revenue decreases by a negligible amount as interest is credited to the new fund. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill establishes the Aging Resilience Fund specifically for the Department of Aging to carry out its mission, including funding for personnel, programs, and activities.
As the state's central fiscal and personnel authority, DBM will be involved in the budgetary allocation of the special fund and the management of the personnel it supports.

The State Treasurer's Office is the custodian of state funds and is responsible for managing the investment of public funds, including the interest earnings that the bill requires be credited to the new fund.

The Comptroller serves as the state's chief financial officer and fiscal watchdog, overseeing the collection and management of state revenues and central payroll for employees funded by the new resilience fund.
The Governor's Office oversees all state departments, drafts the annual budget which includes special fund allocations, and signs or vetoes legislation establishing such funds.
The OLA is responsible for auditing executive branch agencies to ensure that public funds, including special nonlapsing funds like the one established here, are handled according to state law.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation to grant, by law, a tax credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on certain dwellings that are subject to a mortgage or deed of trust provided by a nonprofit entity and a certain covenant or agreement that ensures affordable pricing of the dwelling; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: The Building Homes Act
Status: In the House - First Reading Ways and Means

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: The Building Homes Act authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City and other local governing bodies in Maryland to provide a property tax credit for dwellings that are subject to a mortgage or deed of trust from a nonprofit organization and include a covenant to ensure the dwelling remains affordable.
