It also specifies that any scholarships or grants received by these students may be applied to cover these costs.
responsible_party: Maryland public institutions of higher education
stakeholders: Foster care recipients and homeless youth

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary regulatory and coordinating board for higher education, MHEC is responsible for administering the tuition waiver policies and student financial aid programs that this bill expands to include room, board, and materials.
USM governs 12 public universities that are the primary institutions mandated by this bill to provide free room, board, and required educational supplies to eligible foster care and homeless youth.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State is directly mandated by the bill to provide free room, board, and course materials to qualifying foster care and homeless students.
As a public institution of higher education, Saint Mary's College is directly mandated by the bill to provide free room, board, and course materials to qualifying foster care and homeless students.
DHS oversees the state's foster care system and is responsible for verifying the status of foster care recipients, which is a prerequisite for eligibility for the benefits described in the bill.

The Department of Education tracks the status of homeless youth through the K-12 system, which often serves as the basis for determining eligibility for the higher education tuition and benefit exemptions.

The GOC leads a whole-of-government approach to combat childhood poverty and youth homelessness, directly aligning with the bill's goals of supporting vulnerable youth through higher education stability.
DBM oversees state fiscal accountability and will manage the fiscal impact of increased expenditures on public institutions of higher education providing these additional free services.
DHCD is responsible for homelessness prevention and supportive housing; this bill addresses a specific housing need (on-campus room and board) for homeless youth.
The MLDS Center tracks student outcomes across education levels and would be involved in evaluating the long-term impact and success of providing these expanded benefits to vulnerable populations.
The Governor's Office oversees all state departments and leads major initiatives for economic opportunity and child well-being that encompass the target populations of this bill.

This team focuses on data-driven solutions to reduce childhood poverty and increase economic mobility, which is the primary objective of supporting the education and housing of foster and homeless youth.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission to Examine the Expungement Laws of Maryland for issues of efficiency and equity; and requiring the Commission to submit a certain report to the General Assembly on or before December 31, 2027.
Title: Commission to Examine the Expungement Laws of Maryland
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill establishes the Commission to Examine the Expungement Laws of Maryland to study the efficiency and equity of current expungement procedures. The Commission is tasked with identifying potential improvements and must submit a report of its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 31, 2027.
responsible_party: Commission to Examine the Expungement Laws of Maryland
stakeholders: Individuals with criminal records seeking expungement, legal advocacy groups, the Maryland Judiciary, and law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in a minimal increase in state general fund expenditures for the Department of Legislative Services to provide staffing and administrative support for the Commission through 2027. There is no impact on state or local revenues or local government expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Judiciary is responsible for receiving expungement petitions, issuing court orders, and managing the 'Case Search' portal, making them a primary stakeholder in the efficiency and legal execution of expungement laws.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency manages the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS), the central repository for criminal records where expungement orders must be processed and records removed or shielded.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents indigent individuals who are the primary beneficiaries of expungement laws and is a lead advocate for policy changes regarding the equity and accessibility of the expungement process.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's primary purpose is to establish a new commission under this functional category to study state policy and provide formal recommendations to the General Assembly.
The OAG serves as the legal advisor to state agencies and the General Assembly on criminal law procedures and would likely provide counsel or have a representative on the commission.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the MSP maintains criminal records and is directly impacted by changes to the legal requirements for record retention and expungement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the central hub for public safety and criminal justice policy; they would likely participate in or lead the commission's efforts to analyze the impact of expungement laws.
The Governor’s Office is responsible for appointing members to commissions and overseeing the implementation of legislative mandates related to criminal justice reform.
Since expungement laws frequently cover juvenile delinquency records, DJS is a relevant stakeholder in ensuring the process is efficient and equitable for youth transitions.
DBM oversees the fiscal and personnel needs for state-authorized commissions and would be responsible for assessing any fiscal impact related to the commission's reporting requirements.

Synopsis: Requiring that a handgun permit bear a certain endorsement showing that the permit holder has enhanced privileges to wear, carry, or transport a handgun in any location where a law enforcement official is authorized to wear, carry, or transport a handgun, notwithstanding any law or ordinance that prohibits the wearing, carrying, or transporting of a handgun at a place.
Title: Handgun Permits - Special Endorsement for Security Clearance Holders
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill requires handgun permits issued in Maryland to include a special endorsement for individuals holding specific security clearances. This endorsement allows the permit holder to wear, carry, or transport a handgun in any location where law enforcement officers are authorized to do so, regardless of any state or local laws or ordinances that would otherwise prohibit the carry of handguns in those locations.
stakeholders: Handgun permit holders with high-level security clearances and the Maryland Department of State Police
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $166,400 in fiscal 2025 for the Department of State Police to update licensing IT systems and permit formats. There is no estimated impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police is the primary agency responsible for the licensing and issuance of handgun permits in the state. This bill directly mandates changes to the handgun permit format and grants specific carry privileges that the MSP would be responsible for regulating and enforcing.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the Maryland State Police and state government. They would be responsible for interpreting the legal interaction between this bill's 'enhanced privileges' and existing local or state laws that prohibit firearms in specific locations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the state’s central hub for public safety policy. This bill represents a significant shift in handgun carry policy and would require coordination with this office regarding statewide safety strategies and data-driven crime prevention impacts.

DGS manages and maintains state-owned buildings. Because the bill allows certain permit holders to carry handguns in locations where law enforcement is authorized, it directly impacts the security protocols and access regulations for state facilities managed by DGS.

MDOT manages public transit systems (MTA) and airports (BWI). Since law enforcement is authorized to carry in these sensitive transportation hubs, the bill would expand carry privileges to civilian permit holders in these areas, impacting MDOT security policies.

MDTA manages toll facilities and bridges and maintains its own police force. The bill would impact the enforcement and security protocols for Maryland's critical transportation infrastructure by allowing specially endorsed permit holders the same carry rights as LEOs.

The AOC manages court security and policy. As the bill provides handgun carry privileges in any location where law enforcement is authorized (which includes many judicial facilities), this impacts the security management of the Maryland court system.

As the principal executive agency, the Governor’s Office oversees the MSP and public safety initiatives. The Governor would be responsible for signing this legislation into law and overseeing its implementation across executive departments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for broader public safety and correctional facility management. While MSP handles the permits, DPSCS-managed properties and policies regarding the transport of firearms by non-LEO personnel may be impacted.

Synopsis: Providing that a justice or judge removed or retired from office upon a recommendation of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities is not eligible for future judicial office.
Title: Judiciary Department - Judicial Removal - Disqualification From Future Judicial Office
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill provides that a justice or judge who is removed or retired from office following a recommendation by the Commission on Judicial Disabilities is ineligible for any future judicial office in Maryland.
responsible_party: Commission on Judicial Disabilities and the Supreme Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland justices and judges
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no fiscal impact on state or local government revenues or expenditures, as implementation requirements can be managed within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly concerns judicial personnel and court policies by establishing disqualification criteria for judges and justices, which falls under the AOC's responsibility for judicial infrastructure and policy oversight.
The Governor is responsible for appointing judges; this legislation imposes a legal restriction on the pool of qualified individuals eligible for appointment to judicial posts.

This office identifies and vets candidates for judgeships. It would be responsible for ensuring that any individual disqualified under this law is not recommended or recruited for future judicial office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically references recommendations from the Commission on Judicial Disabilities, which functions as a specialized body within the state's oversight structure.

Synopsis: Providing that the maximum annual salary of the clerks of the circuit courts and the registers of wills may not be more than the salary of a State employee at grade 26, step 20 of the State of Maryland Standard and Bargaining Salary Scale in effect on the day before the clerk or the register begins a new term of office; and repealing as obsolete a certain minimum salary requirement for the register of wills for Baltimore City.
Title: Circuit Court Clerks and Registers of Wills - Maximum Salary
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Works -see also- Brg&Tun; Hwys; PublBlgFac; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill establishes a new maximum annual salary for clerks of the circuit courts and registers of wills, tying the limit to the salary of a State employee at grade 26, step 20 of the State of Maryland Standard and Bargaining Salary Scale. It also repeals an obsolete minimum salary requirement for the Register of Wills for Baltimore City.
stakeholders: Clerks of the circuit courts and registers of wills
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases the maximum possible salary for 24 clerks of the circuit court and 24 registers of wills. While the bill does not mandate a specific increase, it allows the Board of Public Works to set salaries up to a higher ceiling tied to the State's salary scale. Increased expenditures for salaries and fringe benefits will likely occur beginning in fiscal 2027 to coincide with the start of the next term of office. These costs are primarily funded through fees collected by the offices, with the General Fund covering any deficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is a primary subject of the bill, which establishes a new maximum salary cap for these officials and repeals outdated salary requirements specifically for the Register of Wills for Baltimore City.

The bill regulates the maximum salary for Clerks of the Circuit Court; the Administrative Office of the Courts is the central support agency for the Maryland Judiciary, managing its budget and personnel policies.
The Board of Public Works is the administrative body responsible for setting the specific salaries of Clerks and Registers within the limits defined by the General Assembly, which this bill modifies.
The bill benchmarks the salary cap to the State of Maryland Standard and Bargaining Salary Scale, which is the central personnel and compensation system managed and maintained by this department.

As the manager of the state's central payroll and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is responsible for both approving and processing the adjusted salaries for these constitutional officers.
The Governor's Office leads the Board of Public Works and oversees state budget formulation, playing a key role in the final approval and funding of salaries for these state officials.
The State Treasurer serves on the Board of Public Works, which is the body tasked with setting the compensation levels for these officers within the new statutory maximums.
The Attorney General acts as the primary legal advisor to state agencies and constitutional officers, providing guidance on the implementation of statutory changes to official compensation.
The Office of Legislative Audits conducts fiscal compliance audits to ensure that state agencies and officials are compensated in accordance with the limits established by state law.
Adjustments to the maximum salaries of state officials affect the long-term pension liabilities and actuarial calculations managed by the Retirement Agency for the state's workforce.

Synopsis: Establishing the Blockchain-Based Real Property Title Pilot Program in the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to explore the use of blockchain technology for securely recording and verifying real property ownership and to assess its potential for use by law enforcement and courts in resolving real property disputes involving squatting.
Title: State Department of Assessments and Taxation - Blockchain-Based Real Property Title Pilot Program - Establishment
Status: In the House - First Reading Ways and Means
bill_summary: This bill establishes the Blockchain-Based Real Property Title Pilot Program within the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). The program is designed to explore the use of blockchain technology for the secure recording and verification of real property ownership and to evaluate its potential application for law enforcement and the court system in resolving disputes related to squatting.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Real property owners, law enforcement agencies, the Maryland judiciary, and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $101,154 in FY 2025, which accounts for the cost of hiring one contractual administrator to oversee the pilot program. Expenditures continue through FY 2026 until the program sunsets. There is no impact on local revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for the state's IT strategic direction and cybersecurity standards, DoIT would be essential in overseeing the technical implementation, security, and digital architecture of a blockchain-based title recording system.
The bill specifically tasks the pilot program with assessing how blockchain technology can assist the courts in resolving real property disputes and squatting cases.

The Archives is the central depository for land records and property titles; transitioning these permanent legal documents to a blockchain ledger directly impacts their preservation and access mission.
The bill aims to evaluate the potential of blockchain technology for use by law enforcement in verifying ownership and resolving criminal or civil squatting disputes.

The OAG would provide critical legal counsel on the transition of real property title laws to a digital format and ensure the pilot program complies with state property law and constitutional requirements.
The pilot's focus on title security and squatting is highly relevant to DHCD's mission of community revitalization and maintaining safe, sustainable housing environments.
As the executive authority overseeing state departments, the Governor's Office would be involved in directing this new policy initiative and potentially signing the pilot into law.

DBM would oversee the fiscal allocation for the pilot program and evaluate the personnel and administrative costs required to implement blockchain technology within the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises on public safety and criminal justice strategies; the pilot's attempt to use blockchain to combat squatting and property crime aligns with their policy objectives.
The Board adjudicates disputes regarding property assessments, which rely on the accurate and secure verification of real property ownership that the blockchain pilot aims to provide.

The Department of Planning coordinates land use and resource conservation; digital innovation in property title recording provides critical data for their planning services and historical preservation efforts.

Synopsis: Altering a certain list of felony convictions that are eligible for expungement to include distributing or dispensing a controlled dangerous substance.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Expungement - Conviction of Distribution of Controlled Dangerous Substance
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill expands the list of felony convictions eligible for expungement to include the distribution or dispensing of a controlled dangerous substance. It allows individuals convicted of these offenses to petition for expungement after a designated waiting period following the completion of their sentence, including all terms of parole or probation.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals with prior felony convictions for the distribution or dispensing of controlled dangerous substances, the Maryland Judiciary, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in an increase in general fund expenditures for the Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to process and verify additional expungement petitions. A minimal increase in general fund revenues is expected from petition filing fees, although many applicants may be eligible for fee waivers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the central support agency for the Maryland Judiciary, the AOC is responsible for managing court records and the 'Case Search' portal. Expanding expungement eligibility directly impacts the administrative workload of court staff and requires significant updates to judicial databases and records management systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS), the state's central repository for criminal history. This agency is primary in ensuring that records are properly shielded or removed from the state's central database upon receipt of an expungement order.

The MSP maintains investigation and arrest records statewide. Altering the list of crimes eligible for expungement requires the MSP to process additional requests to destroy or remove these law enforcement records from their internal systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD provides legal representation to indigent residents, which frequently includes assisting clients with the expungement process. This bill would likely lead to an increase in petition filings and legal consultations handled by the OPD.
The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor to state agencies and represents the State in criminal appeals and potentially contested expungement hearings where the State might object to a petition.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's hub for public safety policy, GOCPP is responsible for advising the Governor on criminal justice strategies. This bill reflects a shift in criminal procedure policy regarding the long-term impact of felony drug convictions.

DBM oversees the state's personnel and fiscal accountability. Expanding expungement eligibility may have a notable fiscal impact due to the administrative costs and potential need for additional personnel to process the increased volume of petitions across the Judiciary and law enforcement agencies.

The Archives serve as the central depository for permanent government records, including historical court documents. Expungement orders often extend to these archives, requiring staff to locate, remove, or redact records from the state's historical collections.

The Department of Labor manages workforce development and reentry initiatives. Expungement of criminal records is a critical component of their mission to remove barriers to employment for Maryland residents.
The Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation and overseeing the agencies (like DPSCS and MSP) that must implement the procedural changes mandated by the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor annually to proclaim the month of May to be Brain Health and Chronic Headache Awareness Month; requiring the proclamation to align with a certain national brain tumor awareness initiative; establishing the Maryland Brain Health Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund; requiring the Maryland Department of Health, in collaboration with certain entities, to develop guidelines on brain health screening; and requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill for fiscal 2028 an appropriation of $500,000 for the Fund.
Title: Brain Health - Guidelines, Grant Fund, and Commemorative Month (Tahjai's Law)
Status: In the House - First Reading Government, Labor, and Elections and Appropriations

bill_summary: Tahjai's Law requires the Governor to annually designate May as Brain Health and Chronic Headache Awareness Month, aligning with national brain tumor awareness initiatives. It establishes the Maryland Brain Health Grant Fund to provide grants for brain health research and treatment and mandates that the Maryland Department of Health collaborate with stakeholders to develop brain health screening guidelines. The bill also requires a $500,000 state appropriation for the grant fund in fiscal year 2028.
stakeholders: Marylanders suffering from brain tumors and chronic headaches, healthcare providers, medical researchers, and nonprofit organizations focused on brain health.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 in fiscal 2028 to satisfy a mandated appropriation to the Maryland Brain Health Grant Fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures will increase by $500,000 as funds are received and subsequently awarded as grants. Additionally, the Maryland Department of Health will incur administrative costs to develop screening guidelines and manage the grant program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Governor to annually proclaim May as Brain Health and Chronic Headache Awareness Month and mandates the inclusion of a $500,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for fiscal 2028.

The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for developing brain health screening guidelines in collaboration with other entities and likely overseeing the Maryland Brain Health Grant Fund established by the bill.
DBM oversees the state budget process and would be responsible for ensuring the mandated $500,000 appropriation for the Maryland Brain Health Grant Fund is included in the fiscal 2028 budget.
The State Treasurer's Office serves as the custodian of state funds and would be responsible for managing and safeguarding the newly established Maryland Brain Health Grant Fund.
As the state's chief financial officer and fiscal watchdog, the Comptroller is responsible for oversight of state revenues and special funds like the one created by this bill.

Brain health screening guidelines and awareness initiatives are highly relevant to the Department of Aging's mission to support the independence and wellness of Maryland's older adults, many of whom are impacted by cognitive health issues.

The department advocates for individuals with various disabilities, including those resulting from brain-related medical conditions, making the development of screening guidelines relevant to their policy work.

Synopsis: Prohibiting, for a taxable year beginning after June 30, 2026, but before July 1, 2029, an increase of the assessed value of residential real property in the State except under certain circumstances.
Title: Property Tax - Residential Real Property - Moratorium on Assessment Increases
Status: In the House - First Reading Ways and Means
bill_summary: This bill establishes a temporary moratorium on assessment increases for residential real property for three taxable years, beginning after June 30, 2026, and before July 1, 2029. During this period, the assessed value of residential property may not be increased except under specific conditions such as new construction or changes in the property's use.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Residential property owners and State and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in a significant decrease in property tax revenues for the State and local governments during the three-year moratorium (Fiscal 2027–2029) by preventing the typical growth of the residential property tax base.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is directly responsible for hearing appeals regarding property tax assessments. A moratorium on assessment increases would fundamentally alter the volume and nature of appeals brought before the board for residential properties.

As the highest administrative review body for tax controversies, including property assessments, the Tax Court would be the final arbiter of legal disputes arising from the application of the moratorium and its exceptions.

The Board of Public Works is responsible for setting the annual state property tax rate to ensure sufficient revenue for the Annuity Bond Fund. A moratorium on assessment increases directly impacts the state's property tax base, potentially requiring the Board to adjust tax rates to meet debt service obligations.

The Treasurer manages the state's debt and the Annuity Bond Fund, which is funded by state property taxes. Constraining the growth of the property tax base through a moratorium affects the revenue stream used to pay off general obligation bonds and could impact the state's fiscal forecasting and credit analysis.

DBM is responsible for estimating state revenues and formulating the budget. A multi-year moratorium on residential assessment increases would have a notable impact on revenue projections and fiscal planning.

DHCD is concerned with housing affordability. Property tax assessments are a significant component of the cost of homeownership and rental housing, making this policy highly relevant to their mission of fostering sustainable housing opportunities.

As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller monitors state revenue trends and fiscal health, both of which are impacted by changes to property tax assessment growth.
The Governor's Office oversees the drafting of the state budget and signs or vetoes legislation. This bill represents a major shift in state and local tax policy and fiscal management.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to state agencies, including the assessment authorities, regarding the interpretation and implementation of the moratorium and its specific exceptions.

Synopsis: Repealing a requirement that certain motor fuel tax rates be adjusted in future years based on growth in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers; prohibiting the State or a local jurisdiction from imposing or levying a vehicle-miles-traveled tax or certain other similar fees, tolls, or taxes; requiring that the Maryland Transit Administration achieve a certain farebox recovery requirement for certain transit services; etc.
Title: Repair the Transportation Trust Fund Act
Status: In the House - First Reading Ways and Means and Environment and Transportation

bill_summary: This bill repeals the requirement that motor fuel tax rates be adjusted annually based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI), prohibits state and local jurisdictions from implementing vehicle-miles-traveled taxes or similar fees, and mandates that the Maryland Transit Administration meet specific farebox recovery requirements for transit services.
responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) and Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT)
stakeholders: Maryland motorists, public transit riders, and state and local government agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to reduce future motor fuel tax revenue by repealing CPI-based adjustments and limits potential revenue by prohibiting vehicle-miles-traveled taxes. It also impacts transit service management through mandated farebox recovery requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary agency responsible for the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which this bill directly amends. The bill restricts the revenue sources for the TTF and imposes specific operational mandates on its business units.
The bill explicitly requires the MTA to achieve a certain farebox recovery requirement for its transit services, directly impacting its operational budget and service delivery.
The Comptroller is the state's tax collector and is responsible for administering and collecting motor fuel taxes. The bill alters the future rates of these taxes by repealing the CPI adjustment.

SHA is a primary beneficiary of the Transportation Trust Fund for highway maintenance and construction; changes to fuel tax revenue and the prohibition of vehicle-miles-traveled taxes directly impact its long-term funding and planning.

The Governor's Office oversees all state departments, drafts the annual budget including the TTF, and sets the state's transportation and fiscal policy priorities which this bill significantly modifies.

DBM oversees state revenue estimates and fiscal accountability. The repeal of the tax adjustment and prohibition of certain fees will have a notable impact on the state's long-term financial forecasting and the Maryland budget.
The MVA manages vehicle-related laws and is funded via the TTF. Prohibitions on vehicle-miles-traveled taxes and similar fees affect the scope of their regulatory and revenue-collection authority.
The MDTA manages toll facilities; the bill's prohibition on mileage-based taxes, fees, or tolls could restrict the authority's future ability to implement certain revenue-generating strategies.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDOT and the Comptroller and would be responsible for interpreting the bill's prohibitions on new taxes and tolls to ensure compliance by state and local jurisdictions.

The Board of Public Works approves major state contracts and expenditures; changes to the funding and operational requirements of the transit system and transportation fund impact their oversight duties.
The Treasurer manages the investment of state funds and the sale of general obligation bonds, which are influenced by the long-term solvency and revenue stability of the Transportation Trust Fund.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the State Board of Education to include an educational support member who is actively working in a public school as a noncertificated, nonsupervisory public school employee; and providing for the qualifications, term, powers, and election of the new member.
Title: State Board of Education - Membership - Educational Support Member
Status: In the House - First Reading Ways and Means

bill_summary: This bill adds an educational support member to the State Board of Education. This member must be a noncertificated, nonsupervisory employee currently working in a public school and is elected by their peers to serve a term on the board.
stakeholders: Noncertificated and nonsupervisory public school employees (educational support professionals), the Maryland State Board of Education, and the Maryland State Department of Education.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are expected to increase minimally to cover travel and expense reimbursements for the additional board member. There is no significant impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership of the Maryland State Board of Education, which is the governing and policy-making body for the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).
This office is responsible for the recruitment, vetting, and administrative oversight of members serving on state boards and commissions, including the State Board of Education.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the structure of state boards and signs legislation that alters their composition and selection processes.
The bill mandates a specific election process for the new educational support member, which may require coordination or oversight from the state’s election authority.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the State Board of Education and the Department of Education; they would be responsible for ensuring the new membership and election rules comply with state law.
DBM manages the state’s budget and personnel policies and would evaluate any fiscal impact related to the new board member's expenses, per diems, or administrative election costs.
The new member must be a noncertificated, nonsupervisory public school employee; these workers fall under the labor relations and collective bargaining oversight of the PERB.

Synopsis: Requiring an applicant for certain for-hire driver's licenses and transportation network operator's licenses to submit to the Public Service Commission documentation verifying that the applicant completed a certain human trafficking awareness training program; and prohibiting licensed taxicab drivers, for-hire drivers, or transportation network operators from being held civilly or criminally liable for reporting or responding to in good faith a suspected incident of human trafficking.
Title: Public Utilities - For-Hire Drivers and Transportation Network Operators - Human Trafficking Awareness and Prevention Training and Liability
Status: In the House - First Reading Environment and Transportation
bill_summary: The bill requires applicants for for-hire and transportation network operator licenses to complete human trafficking awareness training and submit verification to the Public Service Commission. It also provides immunity from civil and criminal liability to these drivers when reporting or responding to suspected human trafficking in good faith.
stakeholders: For-hire drivers, transportation network operators, and taxicab drivers
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal impact is expected to be minimal, primarily involving administrative costs for the Public Service Commission to verify applicant training documentation. No specific funding amount or significant revenue changes are noted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Public Service Commission with regulating for-hire and transportation network operators by requiring them to verify documentation of human trafficking awareness training as part of the licensing process.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency serves as the state’s hub for public safety policy and victim services; the bill's focus on human trafficking awareness and prevention aligns with their mission to coordinate statewide crime reduction initiatives and support victims.

The Maryland State Police are responsible for investigating major crimes, including human trafficking, and would likely be the agency receiving reports from drivers who observe suspected trafficking incidents in good faith.

Through the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), MDOT manages driver licensing; changes to requirements for for-hire driver's licenses and TNC operators may require coordination with existing MVA driver records or safety standards.
The OAG acts as the legal advisor to the Public Service Commission and would be responsible for interpreting the legal immunity and liability protections provided to drivers under this bill.

The Secretary of State manages the 'Safe at Home' program for victims of human trafficking, making the office relevant to state-level advocacy and protection for the population this training aims to identify.
The bill creates civil and criminal liability protections for drivers reporting trafficking, which impacts the adjudication of such cases within the state's court system managed by the AOC.

DHS oversees adult and child welfare services; they are a primary stakeholder in handling the protective services and support required for trafficking victims identified through the proposed awareness training.

The OAH resolves contested cases for state agencies, including the PSC and MVA; it may be required to adjudicate disputes if a driver's license is denied or suspended based on the new training verification requirements.
DBM oversees the fiscal accountability of state agencies; they would evaluate the personnel and budgetary impact on the Public Service Commission for managing the new training verification system.
DoIT may be involved if the Public Service Commission needs to modernize its digital licensing portals to accept and track training verification documentation from applicants.

bill_summary: This emergency bill prohibits local boards of elections from counting absentee ballots unless the return envelope is signed by both the voter and a witness. It also requires the local board to verify the voter's signature. Active duty uniformed services members serving overseas, along with their spouses and dependents, are exempt from the witness signature requirement.
stakeholders: Maryland voters using absentee ballots, local boards of elections, and overseas military members and their families.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill synopsis indicates that the legislation is an emergency bill and includes local government mandates, which suggests a potential impact on local administrative expenditures for signature verification processes, though specific fiscal estimates are not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing this legislation and overseeing the State Board of Elections' implementation of these new absentee ballot procedures.
The Comptroller acts as a fiscal watchdog and sits on the Board of Public Works; they may oversee the financial reporting aspects related to the fiscal impact on local election boards.

The OAG is the primary legal advisor for the State Board of Elections and would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the implementation of signature verification requirements and defending the state in any related litigation.
DBM oversees the state budget and estimates revenues; this bill has a notable fiscal impact on local government mandates for election administration and ballot processing.
The Department of Transportation, through the MVA, manages the driver's license database which contains the signatures typically used by election officials for voter verification.

The bill includes specific witness signature exceptions for active-duty uniformed service members serving overseas and their families, requiring this agency to act as a resource hub for affected residents.
The Adjutant General advises the Governor on matters concerning the Maryland National Guard, whose members serving overseas are directly affected by the bill's witness signature exemptions.
Guard members serving overseas are subject to the specific absentee ballot signature and witness requirements, including the provided exemptions for uniformed services.

This is the primary implementing agency responsible for managing election procedures, certifying ballots, and coordinating with local boards to ensure uniform compliance with new signature and verification mandates.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the MSP may be involved in investigating major instances of voter fraud or election-related criminal activity involving signature forgery.
The MVA maintains the digital signature records of Maryland drivers, which are the primary source data used by election boards to conduct the signature verification required by this bill.

The OLA conducts fiscal compliance and performance audits of executive agencies, including the State Board of Elections, to ensure they adhere to state laws regarding ballot counting and verification.
The OSP is responsible for investigating and prosecuting violations of state election laws, including fraudulent signatures on absentee ballot return envelopes.

bill_summary: This bill establishes collective bargaining rights for local government employees by applying the Maryland Public Employee Relations Act to county and municipal government employers and their staff. It defines management employee roles for collective bargaining purposes and implements impasse procedures that include binding arbitration to resolve labor disputes between local governments and employee organizations.
stakeholders: County and municipal government employees, local government employers, and labor unions.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase local government expenditures significantly due to the costs of collective bargaining processes and the potential for higher personnel costs resulting from binding arbitration awards. State expenditures will also increase to provide for additional staff and resources for the Maryland Public Employee Relations Board to oversee the expanded jurisdiction of local government labor relations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly expands the jurisdiction of the Maryland Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) to include county and municipal government employers and employees. PERB would be responsible for overseeing the newly established collective bargaining rights, conducting representation elections, and resolving labor disputes for local government entities.

As the state's central personnel authority, DBM manages the statewide personnel system and collective bargaining for state employees. The expansion of the Public Employee Relations Act to local governments will require DBM to coordinate on policy alignment and will have a significant fiscal impact regarding the resources and personnel needed for the state-run Board to manage a massive increase in local caseloads.

The OAG would be responsible for providing legal counsel to the Public Employee Relations Board regarding the implementation of the Act, especially concerning the complex legal and constitutional issues surrounding the establishment of binding arbitration for local governments.

The Governor's Office oversees the operations of all state departments, including the Public Employee Relations Board. This bill represents a major policy shift in labor relations across the state and requires executive approval and oversight for its implementation and fiscal funding.

Synopsis: Prohibiting State law enforcement agencies from hiring individuals who were hired as sworn officers by United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement after January 20, 2025.
Title: Public Safety - State Law Enforcement Agencies - Hiring Restriction (ICE Breaker Act)
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: The ICE Breaker Act prohibits Maryland State law enforcement agencies from hiring any individual who was employed as a sworn officer by United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on or after January 20, 2025.
stakeholders: Maryland State law enforcement agencies and individuals hired as sworn officers by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement after January 20, 2025.
fiscal_impact_summary: The provided text does not contain a fiscal note, but the legislation imposes a hiring restriction on certain individuals which is unlikely to have a direct impact on state revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary law enforcement agency, it is directly restricted by this bill's prohibition on hiring certain former federal officers.
The agency operates the Natural Resources Police, a state law enforcement body that would be subject to the bill's hiring restrictions.
This agency manages the Maryland Capitol Police and must comply with the bill's prohibition when hiring sworn personnel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency employs sworn correctional and parole officers, making it subject to the new hiring restrictions for law enforcement personnel.
This agency operates its own police force and is directly impacted by the prohibition on hiring specific former ICE employees.
The agency manages a transit police force that falls under the definition of a state law enforcement agency restricted by this bill.
The department employs personnel with law enforcement powers for youth supervision and detention, necessitating compliance with the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates statewide public safety policy and would oversee the implementation of these hiring restrictions across the state.
The university system oversees multiple institutions with sworn campus police departments that must follow this hiring prohibition.
The university operates a sworn campus police force that is classified as a state law enforcement agency under the bill's criteria.
The college maintains a sworn police department that is subject to the hiring restrictions established by the bill for state law enforcement.
This office has law enforcement and investigative functions that are directly impacted by the bill's personnel hiring restrictions.
The agency's Field Enforcement Division employs sworn officers who are subject to the bill's hiring prohibition for state agencies.
The OAG employs investigators and oversees legal standards for state law enforcement, making it relevant to the bill's restrictions.
The Adjutant General leads the National Guard, which can serve in law enforcement roles and may be impacted by these personnel rules.
As the central personnel authority, DBM must update statewide hiring systems to reflect this new statutory restriction on former ICE officers.
As the parent department for several agencies with police forces, MDOT is responsible for overarching policy compliance and oversight.
The Governor's Office oversees executive agencies and coordinates the administration's public safety and personnel policies statewide.

Synopsis: Reestablishing the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland with an altered membership and mandate; and requiring the Commission to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2027.
Title: Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland - Reestablishment
Status: In the House - First Reading Environment and Transportation
bill_summary: This bill reestablishes the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland with updated membership and mandates. The Commission is charged with studying lithium-ion battery safety and submitting a report with findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2027.
stakeholders: Lithium-ion battery manufacturers, retailers, emergency responders, fire safety officials, and Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's fiscal impact is expected to be minimal, as the Maryland Department of the Environment is tasked with providing staff support for the commission using existing departmental resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission is required to report its findings and recommendations directly to the Governor, and the office oversees the implementation of such statewide policy initiatives.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reestablishes a specific commission intended to study policy areas and provide recommendations, which is the core function of this governmental category.
Lithium-ion battery safety involves hazardous material management and environmental protection, which fall under MDE's regulatory and public health domain.
As the state agency managing energy policy and the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, MEA is central to battery technology and storage safety standards.
Lithium-ion battery fires represent a significant public safety and disaster response challenge, aligning with MDEM's mission of hazard mitigation and incident response.
The prevalence of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles and public transit systems makes MDOT a stakeholder in safety regulations and recommendations.
The State Fire Marshal’s Office, located within the MSP, is responsible for fire safety standards and investigations related to electrical and battery hazards.
MCEC facilitates the commercialization of climate technologies, including energy storage systems that rely on lithium-ion batteries.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state commissions and ensures that new safety regulations or mandates comply with state and federal law.
DBM oversees the fiscal impact and resource allocation for the operations and staffing of state commissions.
The bill alters the membership of the Commission, which may require the Governor’s Office of Appointments to vet and recruit new members.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of child neglect to include the failure or refusal to provide to a child the education required by law.
Title: Family Law - Child Neglect Definition - Alteration
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of child neglect in Maryland family law to include situations where a parent or guardian fails or refuses to provide a child with the education required by state law.
stakeholders: Parents, guardians, children, and the Maryland Department of Human Services

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state agency responsible for child welfare and protective services, DHS oversees the investigation of child neglect. Altering the definition of child neglect to include failure to provide legal education directly expands the scope of the agency's Child Protective Services (CPS) investigations and social service interventions.

MSDE oversees the public K-12 education system and sets the standards for compulsory education laws. This bill links the failure to meet these educational requirements directly to child neglect, necessitating coordination between schools and social services for enforcement.

Child neglect cases are adjudicated in the Maryland court system as Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) proceedings. The AOC manages the judicial infrastructure and court help centers that will process cases arising from this expanded definition.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD provides legal representation to indigent residents in neglect and parental rights proceedings. An expanded definition of neglect would increase the potential caseload for the agency and change the legal criteria used in their defense of clients.

The OAG acts as the legal advisor for both DHS and MSDE and represents the state in civil appeals involving child welfare. They would provide counsel on the implementation and legal defense of this new statutory definition.

The OAH conducts administrative hearings when individuals challenge findings of neglect made by local departments of social services. Expanding the definition of neglect may lead to more contested cases being appealed to and heard by Administrative Law Judges.

The GOC coordinates state efforts to improve child well-being and addresses childhood poverty and educational access. This bill aligns with their mission to ensure children have a stable environment and access to required education.

Synopsis: Repealing the authority for the issuance and execution of a no-knock search warrant; establishing that a warrant may not authorize an officer to enter a building, apartment, premises, or place without first announcing the officer's purpose and authority; specifying that a warrant may be executed only between 8:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m.; and requiring an officer executing a search warrant, before entering certain areas to be searched, to give reasonable notice to alert any occupants of the officer's authority and purpose.
Title: Criminal Procedure - No-Knock Search Warrants
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill repeals the authority for the issuance and execution of no-knock search warrants in Maryland. It establishes that a search warrant may not authorize an officer to enter a premises without first announcing their purpose and authority, and it mandates that such warrants be executed only between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m.
responsible_party: Maryland law enforcement agencies and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Law enforcement officers, criminal suspects, and Maryland residents
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to have a direct impact on state or local revenues. State and local law enforcement agencies may experience minimal operational impacts and training requirements to comply with the new warrant execution procedures, which can be absorbed within existing budget resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are directly responsible for the execution of search warrants. This bill significantly alters their operational procedures by repealing no-knock authority, imposing strict time limits on execution, and mandating announcement and notification requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent defendants in criminal cases. Changes to search warrant procedures are highly relevant to their work, as they frequently litigate the legality of searches and seizures and the admissibility of evidence obtained through warrants.

The Judiciary is responsible for the issuance of search warrants. This bill amends the standards and restrictions under which judges can authorize warrants, requiring the AOC to update judicial training, forms, and procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency serves as the central hub for public safety policy and manages grants for law enforcement. The bill impacts statewide criminal justice strategy and law enforcement standards, which are core components of GOCPP's advisory and policy mission.

The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor to state agencies, including law enforcement, and handles criminal appeals. Changes to criminal procedure regarding warrants affect their legal guidance and the prosecution of cases involving evidence obtained via search warrants.

The MDTA Police is a dedicated law enforcement force that protects transportation assets and the Port of Baltimore. Like other law enforcement agencies, they must comply with the bill's new restrictions on search warrant execution.

The Natural Resources Police (NRP) have statewide law enforcement authority for hunting, fishing, and boating safety. They execute search warrants as part of their investigative duties and would be subject to the bill's procedural changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: While primarily focused on corrections, the department manages community supervision (parole and probation) and certain law enforcement functions. Procedural changes in the criminal justice system regarding searches are relevant to their broad public safety mission.

The OSP investigates and prosecutes crimes related to the integrity of state government and elections. They utilize search warrants in their investigations and would be bound by the bill's new requirements.

As the chief executive, the Governor oversees the state's law enforcement agencies and policy initiatives regarding public safety. This bill would require executive review for signature and implementation oversight.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing Maryland's public K-12 system, MSDE is responsible for supervising county boards of education and implementing state-mandated educational policies, including those related to Advanced Placement (AP) curricula and academic standards.
The Governor's Office oversees state education policy and is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation that impacts local school board mandates and the state’s broader educational equity goals.
DBM monitors fiscal mandates on local governments and boards of education, and would analyze the potential impact of prohibiting fee collections on the local and state budgets.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Department of Education and the General Assembly regarding the implementation and enforcement of laws governing county boards of education.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary regulator for public K-12 education and establishes standards for school operations, including the requirements for students to participate in interscholastic sports.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) oversees public health and medical standards. This bill impacts healthcare provider practices and establishes new medical screening standards (cardiovascular prescreening) for students.

The MCSS provides technical assistance and coordination to ensure safe environments for K-12 students. New health-safety requirements for athletic participation fall within their mission to prevent and respond to student safety threats.

The DBM is responsible for the state's budget and personnel. It would be involved in assessing the fiscal impact of any state-funded outreach, regulatory updates, or potential staffing needs required by MSDE or MDH to implement this bill.
The OAG would provide legal advice and represent the state agencies (MSDE and MDH) in drafting the regulations and forms required to comply with the mandate for cardiovascular prescreening.

The GOC coordinates state agencies to improve child well-being and health access. A statewide mandate for heart screenings in schools aligns with their mission to improve childhood healthcare outcomes.

Synopsis: Repealing a requirement that authorized prescribers submit prescriber-pharmacist agreements to the health occupations board that regulates the authorized prescriber; authorizing pharmacists, under certain circumstances, to enter into prescriber-pharmacist agreements that authorize the pharmacist to treat an opioid use disorder using controlled dangerous substances drug therapy; etc.
Title: State Board of Pharmacy - Prescriber-Pharmacist Agreements
Status: In the House - First Reading Health
bill_summary: This bill allows pharmacists to enter into agreements with authorized prescribers to provide treatment for opioid use disorder using controlled dangerous substances. It also removes the previous requirement that prescribers submit these agreements to their own specific health occupation boards.
stakeholders: Pharmacists, authorized prescribers (such as physicians, podiatrists, and advanced practice nurses), and patients with opioid use disorder.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the State Board of Pharmacy increase by $34,845 in fiscal 2025 to hire one part-time investigator to handle the increased workload related to monitoring and investigating pharmacist-prescriber agreements. Future year expenditures reflect full-year salaries and benefits. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Pharmacy and other health occupations boards (such as the Board of Physicians and Board of Nursing) referenced in the bill. Additionally, the department manages behavioral health services and the state's response to substance use disorders, including opioid use disorder (OUD).

The OCSA is responsible for enforcing the state’s Controlled Dangerous Substances (CDS) Act. Since the bill authorizes pharmacists to treat opioid use disorder using CDS drug therapy, this agency will be responsible for monitoring the legal supply chain and ensuring compliance among participating pharmacists.

The Office of the Lieutenant Governor is specifically tasked with coordinating the state’s response to the opioid crisis. This bill directly relates to the expansion of treatment options for opioid use disorder.

The OAG serves as the primary legal advisor to the Maryland Department of Health and the various health occupations boards. It would be responsible for providing legal counsel regarding the changes to prescriber-pharmacist agreements and the expanded scope of practice.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates statewide initiatives to reduce substance abuse. As the bill aims to modify the delivery and oversight of opioid use disorder treatment, it aligns with GOCPP's public safety and substance abuse policy mandates.

The Governor’s Office oversees all state departments and agencies, including the Department of Health, and spearheads statewide initiatives focused on public safety and child well-being, which include addressing the opioid epidemic.

DBM oversees state agency personnel and budgets. The repeal of submission requirements for prescriber-pharmacist agreements may have administrative and fiscal impacts on the health occupations boards that DBM manages.

responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City and the governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) administers the Main Street Maryland program and leads neighborhood revitalization efforts. The Department of Commerce promotes the state's Arts and Entertainment districts and provides financial assistance and tax credits to small businesses. agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advocates for small business owners and helps them navigate economic opportunities. The bill creates a property tax credit specifically intended to support small businesses by incentivizing fair market value rents in designated revitalized districts.

The Comptroller acts as the state's fiscal watchdog and monitors revenue impacts. Although property tax is collected locally, the Comptroller oversees the state’s fiscal health and provides economic forecasting related to business-related tax credits.

This board has jurisdiction over appeals related to property tax assessments and credit programs. If a local jurisdiction grants this credit and a dispute arises regarding eligibility or the valuation of the building, this agency would be involved in the appeals process.

The Maryland Tax Court is the highest level of administrative review for tax controversies, including property tax disputes. It would be the final venue for legal challenges related to the application or denial of the property tax credit authorized by this bill.

The Department of Planning coordinates land use and sustainable growth strategies. Its role in supporting urban design and comprehensive planning for local municipalities makes it relevant to the designation and management of the districts mentioned in the bill.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no significant impact on state or local government finances or operations as it primarily concerns the internal governance and administration of private common ownership communities.

The AOC manages the judicial infrastructure and ensures judges are updated on changes to real property law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the surviving spouses of service members who died in the line of duty, a core constituency for which this agency provides advocacy and benefit navigation services.

The bill's timeframe for protected sign display is directly tied to the schedule of primary elections, general elections, and early voting periods, all of which are managed and certified by the State Board of Elections.

Alterations to the laws governing condominiums, homeowners associations, and housing cooperatives may lead to civil litigation or disputes within the Maryland court system. The AOC provides the administrative and technological infrastructure necessary to manage such cases and public records.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary agency responsible for overseeing the public K-12 system, establishing teacher certification standards, and is explicitly tasked by the bill to register local school systems with a national membership organization and oversee educator screening requirements.

As an agency dedicated to fostering safe learning environments and providing technical assistance to public schools, the MCSS is directly impacted by changes to personnel vetting and screening processes intended to improve school safety.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor for MSDE and the state government; they would be responsible for reviewing the legal implications of utilizing a national clearinghouse and ensuring compliance with state and federal laws regarding personnel records and licensure.

DBM oversees the state budget and personnel systems. The requirement for MSDE to pay for national organization memberships and the administrative oversight of a new screening process carries a fiscal impact that falls under DBM’s purview.

This bill involves Maryland's participation in a national membership organization and the use of an interstate clearinghouse to standardize and share professional licensing information, which is a core function of this governmental category.

The Governor’s Office oversees the operations of MSDE and sets broad policy priorities for education and public safety. The Governor would ultimately sign or veto this legislation and oversee its general implementation.

bill_summary: This bill increases the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for military retirement income from $12,500 to $20,000 for retirees who are under the age of 55, beginning in the 2026 tax year.
stakeholders: Military retirees under the age of 55
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a decrease in State general fund revenues and local income tax revenues because it increases the amount of military retirement income that can be excluded from Maryland taxable income.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering state income tax, processing returns, and implementing the specific subtraction modification defined in the bill. They will need to update tax forms and instructions to reflect the increased modification from $12,500 to $20,000.

This agency serves as the primary advocate and resource hub for Maryland's veterans. The bill directly modifies tax benefits for veterans under age 55, which is a significant part of the constituency they support through benefit navigation and outreach.

DBM oversees the state budget and estimates revenues. This bill will result in a decrease in General Fund revenues, which the agency must account for in the state's long-term fiscal planning and annual budget formulation.

As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office is responsible for signing legislation and coordinating statewide initiatives aimed at improving economic opportunity for residents, including veterans.

Synopsis: Altering from 10 business days to 14 calendar days the period of time during which a hearing must be held after the filing of a wrongful detainer action; etc.
Title: Real Property - Wrongful Detainer Actions - Time of Hearing
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill changes the required timeframe for scheduling a hearing in a wrongful detainer action from within 10 business days to within 14 calendar days after the action is filed.
stakeholders: Property owners, individuals involved in wrongful detainer legal actions, and the Maryland Judiciary.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material fiscal impact on state or local government revenues or expenditures, as it only alters the procedural timeline for scheduling court hearings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly alters the statutory timeline for judicial hearings in wrongful detainer cases, which falls under the AOC's responsibility for managing court operations, judicial scheduling, and procedural policies.

The OAG serves as the primary legal advisor for the state and manages civil appeals. Changes to the Real Property Article regarding wrongful detainer actions impact the legal framework the OAG oversees and interprets for state interests.

As the agency responsible for housing policy and community revitalization, the DHCD is concerned with laws governing the removal of individuals from real property and the broader impacts of detainer actions on community stability.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Given the 'Criminal Law - Substantive Crimes' designation of the bill, these proceedings may involve indigent individuals facing legal actions related to property occupancy or parallel criminal trespass charges where the OPD provides representation.

responsible_party: Maryland Securities Commissioner, State agencies, and local political subdivisions
stakeholders: Digital asset service providers, cryptocurrency investors, and Maryland State and local regulatory authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's exemption of digital asset staking from registration requirements likely reduces potential registration fee revenue for the State and limits the regulatory and oversight expenditures of State and local agencies concerning digital assets.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Office of Financial Regulation, which is responsible for supervising the state's financial services industry. This bill explicitly limits the regulatory authority of state agencies regarding digital assets and staking, directly impacting their oversight mandate.

The Office of the Attorney General enforces the Maryland Securities Act and protects consumers from financial fraud. Since the bill modifies definitions and registration requirements under the Maryland Securities Act, it significantly alters the OAG's legal and enforcement framework regarding digital assets.

The Department of Commerce is responsible for attracting and supporting businesses in Maryland, particularly in the technology and cybersecurity sectors. Establishing a regulatory framework for digital assets is a significant factor in economic development for the fintech industry.

As the state's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller has a vested interest in the regulation and categorization of digital assets, as these determinations can influence tax reporting, revenue collection, and fiscal forecasting.

The Governor's Office oversees the operations of all state departments and signs legislation into law. This bill represents a major shift in state policy regarding financial innovation and the regulation of emerging technology.

Synopsis: Specifying that a petition for emergency evaluation is effective for 5 days after being endorsed by a certain court; authorizing a court, on a certain motion and for good cause shown, to extend a petition for up to 5 days at a time, not to exceed a total of 30 days; requiring the court to include the date the petition expires on the petition; and requiring peace officers to comply with a certain provision of law when executing a petition.
Title: Petitions for Emergency Evaluation (Arnaud and Magruder Memorial Act)
Status: In the House - First Reading Health and Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill, known as the Arnaud and Magruder Memorial Act, establishes that a court-endorsed petition for an emergency mental health evaluation is valid for five days. It grants courts the authority to extend the petition's validity for up to five days at a time, for a maximum of 30 days, provided there is good cause. The bill also requires courts to specify the expiration date on the petition and mandates that peace officers follow legal requirements when executing these evaluations.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and State/Local Law Enforcement (Peace Officers)
stakeholders: Individuals experiencing mental health crises, law enforcement officers, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal impact is expected to be minimal. While there may be a slight increase in administrative workload for the Judiciary and law enforcement agencies due to processing extensions of petitions, these requirements can likely be handled with existing resources. No significant impact on state or local revenues is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies judicial procedures by establishing a specific five-day effective period for emergency evaluation petitions and authorizing courts to grant extensions. This impacts court forms, data entry, and judicial workload related to mental health crises.

MDH oversees behavioral health and the state's involuntary admission system. Changing the duration and extension procedures for emergency evaluation petitions directly impacts clinical intake processes and the administration of mental health services.

The bill explicitly mandates that peace officers comply with specific legal standards when executing an emergency evaluation petition. As a primary law enforcement agency with statewide jurisdiction, MSP troopers are directly responsible for the safe service and execution of these petitions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Maryland State Police. It will be responsible for advising these agencies on the implementation of new petition timelines and the legal requirements for peace officers under the Act.
The Lieutenant Governor currently leads significant statewide initiatives focused on mental health and public safety, making this procedural change relevant to their high-level policy portfolio.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and the State Police. This legislation aligns with the office's mission to coordinate statewide initiatives for public safety and mental health coordination.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Information Technology to post on its website the Statewide Information Technology Master Plan 6 months after the Governor is inaugurated in the Governor's first term; and requiring the Secretary of Information Technology to notify the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly if the plan is delayed.
