bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Information Technology to post the Statewide Information Technology Master Plan on its website within six months of the Governor's inauguration in their first term. It also mandates that the Secretary of Information Technology notify the Governor and relevant General Assembly committees if the publication of the plan is delayed.
stakeholders: Governor of Maryland, Maryland General Assembly, State agencies, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no fiscal impact on State or local finances. The Department of Information Technology currently develops the Statewide Information Technology Master Plan as part of its existing operations, and the new reporting and notification requirements can be handled using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Information Technology is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation. It is mandated to create and post the Statewide Information Technology Master Plan on its website and is responsible for notifying the Governor and the General Assembly if the plan is delayed.

The bill aligns the reporting requirement for the Statewide IT Master Plan with the Governor's inauguration and first term. Additionally, the Secretary of Information Technology is required to notify the Governor directly if the plan's publication is delayed.

This office serves as the central hub for state strategic planning and performance tracking. The Statewide Information Technology Master Plan is a key strategic document that influences the efficiency and modernization of the executive branch agencies they oversee.

This team acts as a solution incubator within the Governor's Office to modernize government services and drive data-driven initiatives. The Statewide IT Master Plan serves as the critical roadmap for the technology infrastructure required for their innovation projects.

As the state's performance and compliance watchdog, this agency would be responsible for auditing the Department of Information Technology to ensure they meet the statutory deadlines and transparency requirements established by this bill.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits a railroad train used for freight movement from being operated in Maryland unless it has at least two crew members, subject to certain exceptions. It establishes civil penalties for violations, with fines up to $10,000 for a first offense and up to $25,000 for willful violations occurring within three years of a previous violation.
stakeholders: Railroad companies, freight train operators, and railroad employees.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase State general fund revenues from civil penalties. State general fund expenditures will increase for the Maryland Department of Labor to monitor compliance and enforce the two-person crew requirement. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes mandatory crew requirements for freight railroads, which is a workplace and occupational safety matter. The Department of Labor is explicitly identified as a relevant subject for this legislation and oversees state labor standards and occupational safety (MOSH).

MDOT oversees the state's multi-modal transportation infrastructure. Railroad freight operations are a vital part of this network, and crew requirements impact the overall safety and efficiency of transportation within the state.

The PSC regulates certain transportation and utility services for safety and reliability. They typically manage railroad safety programs and would be involved in the regulatory oversight of operational requirements for freight rail.

The OAG provides legal guidance to state agencies and would play a critical role in defending the state's regulation against federal preemption challenges and interpreting the legal framework for the proposed penalties.
The Governor’s Office oversees executive branch operations, drafts the state budget influenced by potential fine revenue, and holds the authority to sign the bill into law.
DBM is responsible for the state's fiscal planning. This bill introduces high civil penalties ($10,000 to $25,000) that would impact state revenue projections and fiscal oversight.

The Judiciary, supported by the AOC, would be responsible for adjudicating cases where railroad operators are charged with violating the crew requirements and for the collection of the specified fines.

Synopsis: Classifying the theft of a firearm as a felony; establishing a penalty for a first conviction for theft of a firearm of imprisonment not exceeding 5 years or a fine not exceeding $1,000 or both; and establishing a penalty for subsequent convictions of imprisonment not exceeding 10 years or a fine not exceeding $2,500 or both.
Title: Gun Theft Felony Act of 2026
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill reclassifies the theft of a firearm as a felony offense and establishes specific penalties for convictions. A first-time conviction carries a penalty of up to 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine of up to $1,000, while subsequent convictions carry a penalty of up to 10 years imprisonment and/or a fine of up to $2,500.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Law enforcement agencies, the state court system, firearm owners, and individuals charged with firearm theft.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is primarily responsible for the management of the state’s adult correctional system. Classifying firearm theft as a felony and establishing new imprisonment penalties will directly impact its inmate population and parole/probation workloads.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD will be responsible for representing indigent defendants charged with these new felony crimes. The reclassification from misdemeanor to felony and the addition of mandatory or extended imprisonment terms increases the complexity and volume of their caseload.

The OAG handles criminal appeals for the state and provides legal counsel to state agencies. The establishment of new felony crimes and specific penalties requires their legal oversight and will likely lead to an increase in appellate work.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's central hub for public safety policy and funding, this office is heavily involved in strategies to reduce crime and violence. This bill directly aligns with their mandate to advise the Governor on criminal justice strategies.

The MSP is responsible for investigating major crimes and ensuring public safety. They will be the primary law enforcement body investigating reports of firearm theft and processing these felony arrests.

The AOC provides the infrastructure for the Maryland Judiciary. Changing the classification of firearm theft to a felony will change how these cases are processed through the court system, affecting judicial resources and records management.
DBM oversees the state budget. This bill has a notable fiscal impact due to the increased costs of incarceration and judicial processing associated with new felony convictions and longer sentences.
The Governor's Office oversees all state departments and signs or vetoes legislation. This bill is relevant as a major change to state criminal law and public safety policy.

Synopsis: Altering certain apprenticeship requirements relating to public works contracts to require certain contractors and subcontractors to employ a certain number of qualified apprentices or journeyworkers necessary to meet a certain applicable percentage for the project; altering which projects are subject to certain apprenticeship requirements; repealing certain provisions of law that authorize contractors and subcontractors to make certain payments to a certain apprenticeship program in lieu of employing certain apprentices; etc.

bill_summary: The Maryland Workforce Apprenticeship Utilization Act modifies apprenticeship requirements for public works contracts. It requires contractors and subcontractors to ensure that apprentices or journeyworkers perform a specific percentage of work on projects that meet a certain value threshold. Notably, the bill lowers the project value threshold for these requirements and repeals the provision that allowed contractors to make payments to an apprenticeship program in lieu of employing actual apprentices.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor and the Board of Public Works
stakeholders: State and local government agencies, public works contractors, subcontractors, and construction apprentices.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase state and local expenditures for public works projects due to potentially higher contract costs and increased administrative burdens. The Maryland Department of Labor will incur additional costs to oversee and enforce the updated apprenticeship utilization standards. While the exact increase in project costs is not specified, it is anticipated to affect the state's capital budget and local government procurement expenses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor oversees the state’s apprenticeship programs and workforce development initiatives. This bill directly impacts the administration of apprenticeship requirements, including the tracking of apprentices and journeyworkers on public works projects.

As the central agency for state procurement and the construction of state facilities, DGS is responsible for managing many of the public works contracts that will be subject to these new apprenticeship utilization requirements.

MDOT manages a vast multi-modal transportation network and significant infrastructure projects (highways, bridges, rail) that are classified as public works and would be subject to these apprenticeship mandates.

The Board of Public Works reviews and approves major state procurement contracts, including public works projects. Changes to the legal requirements for these contracts directly affect the Board's oversight and approval processes.
The IAC oversees and funds the construction and renovation of public school facilities, which are major public works projects impacted by apprenticeship utilization percentages.

The MSA manages large-scale construction projects for sports, entertainment, and schools. As a primary entity for state-funded construction, it must ensure contractors meet these new apprenticeship standards.
The GWDB is responsible for the state's workforce strategy and creates 'pipelines' from training to careers. This bill aligns with their mission to improve career pathways through apprenticeships.

DBM serves as the central fiscal authority and manages the statewide personnel system. It has a role in procurement policy and would likely evaluate the fiscal impact of these changes on state projects.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies on procurement law and will likely be involved in drafting regulations and ensuring compliance with the new statutory apprenticeship requirements.
As a major state entity that handles its own procurement and construction for its 12 universities, USM would need to ensure its public works contracts comply with the new apprenticeship ratios.
Morgan State is a 'primary procurement unit' for the state and manages its own campus construction projects, which are subject to public works contract regulations.
The college manages its own facilities and infrastructure projects, which would be subject to the altered apprenticeship requirements for public works contracts.
MDE funds and oversees major public works infrastructure, such as wastewater treatment plant upgrades, which would fall under the revised apprenticeship requirements.
DNR manages public lands and water infrastructure projects. Any construction contracts it issues for state parks or waterways would be impacted by the new rules.
The Treasurer sits on the Board of Public Works and oversees the management of state funds used for these contracts, ensuring fiscal compliance with procurement laws.
The Comptroller sits on the Board of Public Works and monitors state expenditures, including those related to the newly regulated public works contracts.

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations (HMOs) to provide a remittance advice that separately identifies and itemizes any interest owed to health care providers for claims that were not paid within specified timeframes.
stakeholders: Health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations (HMOs), and health care providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) may see a small increase in general fund revenues from $125 form filing fees. The bill is not expected to significantly affect state or local expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of the Maryland insurance industry, the MIA is responsible for overseeing insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs. They will be the agency charged with enforcing these new remittance advice requirements and ensuring compliance with late-paid claim interest laws.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the Maryland Insurance Administration and may be involved in enforcement actions or legal interpretations regarding the new itemization requirements for interest on late-paid claims.

The Department of Health oversees healthcare financing and the Medicaid program, which utilizes Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) that often follow standards similar to those of the HMOs and private insurers affected by this bill.

The DBM manages the health benefits for the state's workforce. Carriers providing these benefits to state employees would be required to comply with these remittance advice standards, potentially impacting the administration of state-sponsored health plans.

The MHBE administers the marketplace where many of the affected private health plans are sold. Changes to billing and remittance standards for these carriers are relevant to the Exchange's oversight and consumer assistance functions.

The MHCC monitors health system performance and cost. Standardizing how interest on late claims is itemized contributes to the transparency of healthcare spending and insurer efficiency, which aligns with the commission's planning and reporting mission.
As the executive office responsible for signing or vetoing legislation, the Governor's Office must review this bill for consistency with state healthcare policy and fiscal priorities.

Synopsis: Requiring the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to include at least three positions to conduct the duties of the Office to provide specialized case management services to assist deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals; and requiring the Office to provide specialized case management services to deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals.

bill_summary: The bill requires the Maryland Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to provide specialized case management services for individuals who are deaf, deafblind, or hard of hearing. It mandates that the Office must include at least three staff positions specifically to conduct these services.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
stakeholders: Deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $295,953 in FY 2025, which reflects the bill's October 1, 2024, effective date and the cost of hiring three case managers. Future year expenditures reflect full salaries, annual increases, and ongoing operating expenses, reaching approximately $367,314 by FY 2029. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly mandates the Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (ODHH) to hire at least three new staff members and provides a new specific requirement for the office to perform specialized case management services for its constituent population.

DBM is responsible for formulating the state budget and managing the personnel system. This bill requires the creation of at least three new positions, which will require DBM's approval for funding and position classification.

As the cross-disability policy leader for the state, this agency coordinates service delivery for individuals with disabilities. The addition of specialized case management at ODHH directly interacts with their mission to improve access and independence for Marylanders with disabilities.

ODHH is an agency within the Executive Department. The Governor’s Office oversees the operations of all state departments and initiates policies focused on child well-being and economic opportunity, which align with providing specialized case management.

The Maryland School for the Deaf provides specialized services and education to the same population up to age 21. New case management services at ODHH would likely require coordination with MSD for students transitioning into adult services.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to nearly all state agencies, including ODHH. They would likely provide counsel on the regulatory and legal frameworks for implementing new case management protocols.
The Comptroller manages the state's central payroll for all employees. The addition of at least three new positions at ODHH will impact the state's payroll administration and revenue allocation.

Synopsis: Providing that certain provisions of law pertaining to wrongful detainer actions do not apply unless certain property is posted conspicuously against trespass or loitering.
Title: Real Property - Actions for Wrongful Detainer - Required Postings
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill requires that property be conspicuously posted against trespassing or loitering as a prerequisite for the application of laws regarding wrongful detainer actions.
stakeholders: Property owners and unauthorized occupants

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Wrongful detainer actions are legal proceedings filed and adjudicated within the Maryland District Court system. As the support agency for the Judiciary, the AOC would be responsible for updating court forms, procedural guidelines, and public-facing instructional materials to reflect that conspicuous posting against trespass or loitering is now a prerequisite for such actions.

DNR manages over 500,000 acres of public state land, including parks and forests. To retain the legal authority to pursue wrongful detainer actions against unauthorized occupants or squatters on these lands, the agency must ensure its properties are conspicuously posted against trespass or loitering in accordance with this bill.

DGS is the central agency responsible for the management and security of state-owned facilities and real estate. The agency would need to implement the bill's conspicuous posting requirements across state properties under its jurisdiction to ensure it can successfully utilize wrongful detainer provisions to remove unauthorized individuals from state grounds.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and represents them in civil litigation, including real property disputes. The agency would need to advise its client agencies on the new posting prerequisites for wrongful detainer and verify compliance when initiating these actions on behalf of the state.

The SHA manages thousands of miles of state roads and extensive rights-of-way. Because these areas are frequent sites of loitering and unauthorized occupancy, the SHA would be required to update its signage and posting protocols to ensure civil wrongful detainer actions remain a viable legal remedy for clearing state property.

The MTA manages public transit hubs, rail corridors, and bus facilities. Given the operational challenges posed by unauthorized loitering at transit stations, the agency must ensure compliance with the bill's signage requirements to preserve its ability to pursue civil detainer actions against trespassers.

As the parent agency for several major land-owning units like the SHA and MTA, MDOT would oversee the coordinated implementation of new property posting policies across its multi-modal transportation network to ensure legal compliance with the revised Real Property article.

The Maryland State Police enforce trespass and motor vehicle laws on state property. While wrongful detainer is a civil process, its availability is tied to the presence of conspicuous signs against trespass or loitering, which are physical elements law enforcement typically verifies or documents during incidents on state land.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state public K-12 system and is responsible for setting statewide academic standards and ensuring local boards, such as the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, comply with state-mandated curriculum and instructional requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's central hub for public safety policy, GOCPP is relevant because the bill focuses on educating youth about the legal consequences of felony murder, which aligns with their mission to coordinate crime reduction and prevention initiatives across the state.

DJS is responsible for the rehabilitation and delinquency prevention of youth; this educational mandate serves as a preventative strategy to inform middle school students of the severe legal risks and incarceration penalties associated with serious violent crimes.

Operating within MSDE, this agency provides technical assistance and resources for school safety. Preventative education regarding the consequences of criminal behavior is a component of their mission to foster safe learning environments for students.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including MSDE. They would likely be consulted to ensure that any curriculum materials regarding the legal definition of the felony murder doctrine and Maryland's penal code are accurate.

The bill may have a fiscal impact on the state budget if MSDE is required to provide additional technical assistance or develop curriculum resources to support the Baltimore City Board, requiring oversight of state expenditures by DBM.

The GOC leads policy action to improve child well-being; instruction on the consequences of serious crime for students in high-poverty jurisdictions aligns with their 'whole-of-government' approach to improving economic mobility and long-term youth outcomes.

The Governor's Office manages executive branch operations and is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation that establishes new curriculum standards or public safety directives for Maryland's public schools.

Synopsis: Increasing from four to five the number of dealer licenses available for certain manufacturers or distributors that deal only in electric or nonfossil-fuel burning vehicles; and providing that one of the licenses may be issued only for the operation of a dealership in the City of Bowie.

stakeholders: Electric vehicle manufacturers and distributors, the City of Bowie, and potential electric vehicle purchasers in Maryland.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a division of MDOT, the MVA is directly responsible for managing driver and vehicle services, which includes the licensing and regulation of vehicle dealers in Maryland. Increasing the availability of dealer licenses for EV manufacturers directly aligns with the agency’s mission to increase renewable energy production and lower carbon emissions in the transportation sector.

The MDE leads the state’s climate change initiatives. Supporting the expansion of electric vehicle dealerships is a key component of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and meeting the state’s environmental goals.

The Department of Commerce works to attract new businesses and support the expansion of existing ones. This bill facilitates the growth of specialized vehicle manufacturers and distributors within the Maryland market, particularly in the City of Bowie.
As the state's chief executive, the Governor oversees all executive departments, including MDOT and its business regulation functions, and will be responsible for signing this legislation into law.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires the Maryland Department of Labor to adopt new energy conservation regulations by 2028. This is expected to create administrative costs for state agencies and impact construction requirements for buildings subject to energy performance standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Labor to adopt energy conservation requirements for new construction as part of the Maryland Building Performance Standards.

The new requirements apply to buildings subject to the Building Energy Performance Standards already adopted by the Department of the Environment, ensuring regulatory alignment between the two agencies.
The agency is dedicated to promoting clean, affordable energy and managing the Strategic Energy Investment Fund; it provides technical guidance and incentives related to building energy efficiency.

DGS is responsible for the design, construction, and maintenance of state-owned facilities. These new energy conservation standards will directly impact the cost and technical requirements of state construction projects.
DBM oversees the state's capital and operating budgets. Increased construction costs for state facilities due to new energy standards will have a notable fiscal impact on state budget planning.

DHCD finances the construction of affordable rental units and housing revitalization. New energy conservation requirements for large buildings will affect the development costs and standards for these projects.
The IAC manages the funding and standards for public school construction. New energy requirements for large buildings will likely apply to new school facilities, impacting project costs and design.
MSA manages large-scale public construction projects, including the Built to Learn program for schools. These standards will apply to the significant infrastructure projects they oversee.
As a major developer of academic and residential buildings across the state, USM will need to comply with these new energy conservation requirements for all future large-scale construction.
As a primary procurement unit and major developer of urban research facilities, the university must ensure new construction adheres to these updated building performance standards.
New construction projects at the college will be subject to the updated energy conservation standards, impacting future capital improvement projects.

MCEC provides financing solutions for energy efficiency upgrades and climate technologies, which will be critical for developers meeting these new standards.

stakeholders: Maryland residents eligible to vote, applicants for driver's licenses or state identification cards, and state and local election officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by $2,674,600 in FY 2025, primarily consisting of $2,422,000 for Motor Vehicle Administration information technology upgrades and $252,600 for State Board of Elections personnel and programming. Local government expenditures may also increase for local boards of elections to process additional voter registration records.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes requirements for the State Board of Elections to process transmitted voter registration information and send specific notices to applicants, making it a primary implementing agency.
The bill explicitly mandates the Motor Vehicle Administration to implement an enhanced automatic voter registration system and manage the transmission of information to the State Board of Elections.

As the agency responsible for IT infrastructure, cybersecurity, and data standards, DoIT would likely oversee the technical implementation, data security, and interoperability between the MVA and the State Board of Elections.

The Motor Vehicle Administration is a unit of MDOT. The department will be responsible for the higher-level administrative and fiscal oversight of the MVA's implementation of the new registration system.

The bill authorizes the State Board of Elections to implement automatic voter registration at other state agencies with their consent; DHS is specifically identified in the bill's subjects as a relevant agency due to its handling of benefit applications.

The bill authorizes the implementation of automatic voter registration at certain state agencies; the Health Benefit Exchange is listed in the bill's subjects as a potential participant in this expanded system.

The OAG would provide legal guidance to the State Board of Elections and MVA regarding compliance with federal and state election laws, as well as data privacy regulations involved in automatic registration.

DBM is responsible for the state's personnel and operating budget; it would be involved in managing the fiscal impact and resource allocation needed for the MVA and SBE to implement these system upgrades.

As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office oversees the departments involved (MDOT/MVA, DHS) and has ultimate responsibility for ensuring state agencies comply with legislative mandates regarding voting access.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases local government expenditures for the City of Seat Pleasant to account for employer contributions to LEOPS and the cost of providing credit for past service. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary entity responsible for managing the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). The Department of Budget and Management serves as the state’s central fiscal authority. The entry of a new participating governmental unit into a state pension system like LEOPS has fiscal implications for the state’s long-term retirement liabilities and administrative oversight.

The State Treasurer acts as the principal custodian of the state’s financial assets and sits on the board of the retirement system. The office is responsible for the prudent fiscal management of the funds that support pension systems like LEOPS.

As the state's chief financial officer and fiscal watchdog, the Comptroller monitors state revenues and expenditures. This includes overseeing the long-term fiscal health and reporting of state pension obligations.

Synopsis: Increasing the maximum period of imprisonment for a first conviction for manslaughter by vehicle or vessel from 10 years to 20 years and for a second or subsequent conviction, or having been previously convicted for certain other crimes, from 15 years to 30 years; etc.
Title: Manslaughter by Vehicle or Vessel - Increased Penalties (Jamari's Law)
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: The bill, known as Jamari's Law, increases the maximum criminal penalties for manslaughter by vehicle or vessel. Specifically, it doubles the maximum term of imprisonment for a first conviction from 10 years to 20 years. For a second or subsequent conviction, or for individuals with specific prior convictions, the maximum term of imprisonment increases from 15 years to 30 years.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals convicted of vehicular or vessel manslaughter, victims of these crimes and their families, and the state correctional system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase state general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services due to longer periods of incarceration resulting from the increased maximum sentences. No direct impact on state or local revenues is identified.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for managing the state's adult correctional system and prisons, increased maximum sentences for manslaughter by vehicle or vessel will directly lead to longer terms of incarceration and higher operational costs for the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents indigent individuals in criminal cases where incarceration is a possibility; doubling the maximum penalties for manslaughter significantly increases the complexity and stakes for their defense cases.
The judiciary is responsible for the adjudication of these criminal cases, and judges will be required to apply the updated sentencing guidelines and maximum penalties mandated by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the central hub for public safety policy and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies, making it highly relevant to legislation that alters sentencing for major crimes.
MSP is the primary agency investigating major crimes on state highways, including manslaughter by vehicle, and is involved in the enforcement and documentation of these offenses.

The bill includes increased penalties for manslaughter by 'vessel'; the DNR's Natural Resources Police are the primary law enforcement agency for Maryland's waterways and would be responsible for investigating such incidents.
The OAG handles all criminal appeals in both state and federal courts and provides legal counsel to state agencies involved in the enforcement and prosecution of these laws.
The Governor's Office oversees statewide public safety initiatives and is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation that significantly changes criminal sentencing laws.
DBM oversees the state's annual operating budget; increased prison sentences lead to long-term fiscal impacts on the state budget regarding correctional facility capacity and maintenance.
The MVA manages driver records and licensing; manslaughter convictions are critical parts of a driver's permanent record and may impact license revocations or state safety programs.

It also updates eligibility requirements for board members and requires the board to adopt and publish an ethics policy.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage licensees in Anne Arundel County, residents of Anne Arundel County, the Governor, and the Anne Arundel County Delegation to the General Assembly.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases local government expenditures for Anne Arundel County to pay for the salaries and expenses of two additional board members. There is no impact on state revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Governor to appoint members to the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County from a list of recommended individuals, directly involving the Governor's principal executive authority.

The bill requires the Board to adopt and publish a specific ethics policy. The State Ethics Commission oversees conflict-of-interest standards and ethical requirements for state-appointed board members.

The Comptroller has fiscal oversight over state revenues and historically manages components of the state's alcoholic beverage tax and regulatory framework, which connects to the function of local licensing boards.
Increasing the number of members on the Board may have fiscal impacts regarding compensation, per diems, or administrative support costs overseen by DBM.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to prepare certain literature relating to firearms and ammunition and to distribute the literature to all county health departments in the State; requiring each county health department to distribute certain literature to all establishments that sell firearms or ammunition within the county; requiring establishments that sell firearms or ammunition in the State to make certain literature visible and available and to distribute the literature to purchasers of firearms and ammunition; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to create educational literature regarding firearm safety, suicide prevention, and conflict resolution. The department must distribute this literature to county health departments, which are then responsible for providing it to local firearm and ammunition retailers. These retailers are required to prominently display the literature and provide a copy to all purchasers of firearms or ammunition.
stakeholders: Firearm and ammunition retailers, firearm and ammunition purchasers, Maryland Department of Health, and county health departments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures will increase for the Maryland Department of Health and county health departments to develop, print, and distribute the required literature. Firearm and ammunition retailers may experience minimal administrative impacts to comply with display and distribution requirements. There is no expected impact on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to prepare safety literature related to firearms and ammunition and coordinate its distribution to all 24 county health departments in the state.

As the primary agency for public safety and the regulation of firearms in Maryland, the State Police has oversight over the firearm and ammunition establishments that are required to display and distribute this literature.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the state’s hub for public safety policy and would be responsible for the strategic planning and evaluation of this firearm safety communication initiative.

The department would oversee the fiscal impact and budget allocation required for the Department of Health to create, print, and distribute the safety literature statewide.

Synopsis: Repealing the sentencing date limitation of October 1, 2021, for an individual convicted as an adult of an offense committed when the individual was a minor to file a motion to reduce the duration of the sentence.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the October 1, 2021, sentencing date limitation for individuals convicted as adults for offenses committed when they were minors. By removing this date restriction, any individual convicted as an adult for a crime committed as a minor may file a motion to reduce their sentence after serving at least 20 years, regardless of their sentencing date.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Office of the Public Defender, and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals convicted as adults for crimes committed while they were minors, the Maryland Judiciary, the Office of the Public Defender, State's Attorneys, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary and the Office of the Public Defender may increase minimally to process and represent additional motions for sentence reductions. Conversely, State general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services may decrease minimally if individuals are released from incarceration earlier than originally scheduled. Local government workloads for State's Attorneys may also increase minimally to respond to these motions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the eligibility for filing motions to reduce sentences in the circuit courts, which will directly impact court workloads, case management, and the scheduling of hearings overseen by the Judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency managing Maryland's adult correctional system, any legislation that facilitates the reduction of sentences for incarcerated individuals directly impacts prison population management and release coordination.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals in criminal cases. The OAG represents the State in criminal appeals and provides legal advice to the state on criminal procedure. They may be involved in responding to these motions or handling subsequent appeals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the central hub for public safety policy and sentencing data. This bill alters sentencing outcomes for specific populations, which aligns with their role in advising the Governor on criminal justice strategies.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase Carroll County expenditures due to more frequent and higher-cost workers' compensation claims, as the county is self-insured and must pay for additional disability benefits and medical costs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency dedicated to advocating for and promoting the welfare of individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing, ODHH will likely play a key role in the Advisory Council and in ensuring the program's resources are accessible and effective.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards

The Maryland Department of Health is often involved in early childhood health services, including hearing screenings and early intervention programs that intersect with language acquisition tracking.
The establishment of a new State Coordinator position and a tracking program within MSDE will require fiscal oversight, budget allocation, and personnel management by DBM.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is projected to result in a significant increase in State General Fund revenues and local income tax revenues by preventing federal tax deductions from reducing Maryland taxable income. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's chief tax collector and fiscal watchdog, the Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for implementing and administering changes to the Maryland income tax code, including the decoupling from federal depreciation and business interest expense deductions.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the Comptroller and represents the state in complex litigation regarding tax law interpretations and challenges to income tax modifications.

Changes to tax deductions for business interest and depreciation affect the corporate tax environment and the economic competitiveness of Maryland for private investment, which falls under the Department's mandate for business expansion.
The Governor's Office oversees the operations of all state departments and is responsible for drafting the state budget, which is impacted by the revenue changes resulting from tax code decoupling.

The Treasurer is a principal custodian of state funds and sits on the Board of Public Works; they monitor fiscal health and credit ratings, which are influenced by major shifts in the state's tax revenue streams.

The Department of Health is responsible for the regulatory oversight of health-related occupations, including funeral services, making it the primary agency involved in this policy area.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement that the Governor include in the annual budget bill a $350,000 appropriation to the State's Consumer Health Information Hub; requiring the Hub to carry out certain duties to the extent funding is available; and repealing the termination date for certain provisions of law related to consumer health information and the State's Consumer Health Information Hub.
Title: Consumer Health Information - Termination Date and Mandatory Funding for the State's Consumer Health Information Hub - Repeal
Status: In the House - First Reading Health
bill_summary: This bill repeals the requirement for the Governor to include a $350,000 mandated annual appropriation for the State's Consumer Health Information Hub in the budget bill. Additionally, the bill removes the sunset provision for the Hub, effectively making its operations permanent, and specifies that the Hub is only required to carry out its duties to the extent that funding is available.
stakeholders: Maryland health care consumers and the State's Consumer Health Information Hub at the University of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in an annual decrease in State general fund expenditures of $350,000 beginning in fiscal 2025 due to the repeal of the mandated appropriation. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances, although the Hub's operations will be contingent on available alternate funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals a mandatory annual appropriation of $350,000 that the Governor must include in the annual budget bill. As the agency responsible for formulating and overseeing the state’s annual operating budget, DBM is directly impacted by changes to mandated spending requirements.

The bill concerns the State's Consumer Health Information Hub and public health information. The Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for protecting and promoting public health and coordinating health service initiatives across the state.

The State’s Consumer Health Information Hub is located at the University of Maryland, College Park (a constituent institution of USM). Repealing the mandatory funding and changing the Hub's duties to be contingent on available funding directly impacts the operations and financial resources of the university.

The Governor's Office is responsible for drafting the annual budget and enforcing state laws. This bill specifically modifies the Governor's statutory requirements regarding the content of the annual budget bill and the mandate to fund a specific public health entity.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is responsible for health system planning and maintaining consumer transparency through public data reporting. The Hub’s mission to provide consumer health information directly aligns with the Commission’s duties to empower consumers with health quality and cost data.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a developer of artificial intelligence from making, or knowingly causing artificial intelligence to make, certain representations or statements relating to behavioral health care subject to a civil penalty not exceeding $1,000,000; requiring a developer artificial intelligence sold, leased, given, or otherwise provided to consumers in the State to include a certain notice or protocols; authorizing the Attorney General to bring an action for an alleged violation of the Act; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits artificial intelligence developers from making false or misleading statements regarding behavioral health care and requires them to implement specific notices or protocols for AI products provided to consumers. The Attorney General is authorized to enforce these requirements, with violators facing civil penalties of up to $1,000,000.
stakeholders: Artificial intelligence developers and Maryland consumers seeking or receiving behavioral health care services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues may increase due to the establishment of civil penalties of up to $1,000,000 for violations. State expenditures may increase for the Attorney General to investigate and bring enforcement actions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions for violations of the act. As the state's primary consumer protection authority, the OAG would lead the investigation and prosecution of AI developers making false representations regarding behavioral health.

The bill focuses on behavioral health care, which falls directly under the jurisdiction of the Department of Health. The MDH manages behavioral health services and oversees the professional boards (such as social workers and therapists) that would be impacted by AI tools making health-related claims.

The MHCC is responsible for health information technology standards and planning. The regulation of AI as it relates to health care claims and consumer disclosure protocols falls within its mandate to improve transparency and quality in health information systems.

As the state's central authority for IT policy and strategy, the Department of Information Technology is relevant to the implementation of standards and protocols for artificial intelligence development and digital consumer notices.

The bill establishes significant civil penalties and regulatory requirements for AI developers and technology businesses. This affects the state's commercial landscape and the technology sector that the Department of Commerce is tasked with supporting and attracting.

Synopsis: Requiring, to address a funding disparity, that the Governor include at least $5,000,000 to the University of Maryland Eastern Shore in the annual budget bill each fiscal year until a total amount of $321,181,312 is appropriated; and authorizing the University of Maryland Eastern Shore to use funds made available by the Act for development of infrastructure and academic programs, investment in faculty, scholarships, and certain other institutional needs.

bill_summary: The Land-Grant Equity and Accountability Act addresses historical funding disparities at the University of Maryland Eastern Shore (UMES) by requiring the Governor to include a minimum of $5,000,000 in the annual state budget for the university. These appropriations must continue until a cumulative total of $321,181,312 has been reached. UMES is authorized to use these funds for infrastructure development, academic programs, scholarships, faculty investment, and other institutional needs.
responsible_party: Governor of Maryland and the University of Maryland Eastern Shore
stakeholders: Students, faculty, and staff of the University of Maryland Eastern Shore and the Eastern Shore community
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $5,000,000 annually until the total mandate of $321,181,312 is fulfilled. No direct impact on local revenues or expenditures is described in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Governor to include specific funding for UMES in the annual budget bill and addresses a state-level funding disparity policy.
DBM is responsible for formulating the state budget and would be the primary agency ensuring the mandated $5 million annual appropriation is included in the Governor's budget.
The University of Maryland Eastern Shore is a member institution of the University System of Maryland, which provides financial stewardship and strategic oversight for its universities.
MHEC coordinates policy and academic growth for the state's higher education institutions and would oversee the academic programs and scholarships funded by this Act.
The Board of Public Works must approve major state expenditures and contracts, which would include the infrastructure development projects authorized by this funding.
As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller monitors state revenue and oversees fiscal accountability for large appropriations.
The State Treasurer manages the state's banking and investment of public funds, including the multi-year funding stream established by this legislation.
The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor for state agencies and the University System, potentially advising on the implementation of equity-based funding mandates.
The OLA is responsible for auditing state agencies, including the University System, and would likely review the use of these specific funds to ensure compliance with the Act.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from knowingly and willfully causing another to ingest an abortion-inducing drug when the person knows or believes that the other person is pregnant and without consent, through fraud or coercion, or by force or threat of force.
Title: Criminal Law - Causing Ingestion of an Abortion-Inducing Drug - Prohibition (Women's Freedom From Coercion Act)
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary and Health
bill_summary: This bill prohibits a person from knowingly and willfully causing another person to ingest an abortion-inducing drug without their consent. The prohibition applies when the person knows or believes the other individual is pregnant and utilizes fraud, coercion, force, or the threat of force to cause the ingestion.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Office of the State's Attorney
stakeholders: Pregnant individuals, law enforcement agencies, and the state judicial system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal fiscal impact. State and local expenditures may increase minimally due to costs associated with incarceration and supervision of individuals convicted under the new prohibition. State revenues may increase minimally from fines imposed in District Court cases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the chief legal office for the state, the OAG is responsible for upholding the rule of law, advising the legislature on criminal law implementation, and managing all criminal appeals resulting from convictions under this new statute.

The Maryland State Police are the primary statewide law enforcement agency responsible for investigating major crimes, including criminal acts involving force, coercion, and the unauthorized administration of drugs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD is constitutionally and statutorily mandated to provide legal representation to indigent residents facing incarceration for criminal charges, which would include defendants charged under this new Act.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is responsible for the management of the state's correctional facilities and the supervision of individuals on parole or probation, directly impacting their operations should this law lead to new convictions and sentences.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's hub for public safety policy, GOCPP advises on criminal justice strategies and manages the data and grant funding that support law enforcement efforts and victim services related to this crime.
The AOC provides the administrative and technological infrastructure for the Maryland Judiciary, which will be responsible for adjudicating criminal cases brought under this new prohibition.

DHS oversees child and adult protective services; instances of forced or coerced drug ingestion in domestic or vulnerable person scenarios would likely require intervention from their welfare divisions.
DJS is responsible for the rehabilitation and supervision of any youth involved in the juvenile justice system who may be referred for committing this offense.
MDH regulates healthcare and monitors the legal supply chain of drugs through the Office of Controlled Substances Administration, which overlaps with the bill's focus on abortion-inducing drugs.
The Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation and overseeing the executive agencies that will implement and enforce this new criminal law.
DBM coordinates the state's budget and will monitor the fiscal impact of new criminal enforcement, judicial proceedings, and correctional requirements necessitated by the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and managed care organizations to provide coverage for services provided in any setting by certain certified peer recovery specialists; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to convene a certain workgroup on the certification process of peer recovery specialists.
Title: Certified Peer Recovery Specialists - Coverage Under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance and Workgroup on Certification
Status: In the House - First Reading Health
bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and certain private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and managed care organizations to provide insurance coverage for services rendered by certified peer recovery specialists in any setting. It also directs the Maryland Department of Health to form a workgroup to study and make recommendations regarding the certification process for peer recovery specialists.
stakeholders: Certified peer recovery specialists, individuals receiving substance use or mental health recovery services, the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, health insurance carriers, and managed care organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase State expenditures (both general and federal funds) to cover Medicaid reimbursements for peer recovery services beginning in fiscal 2025. Private insurance carriers may experience increased claims costs, which could lead to higher premiums. Local government expenditures for employee health insurance plans may also increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Department of Health. Additionally, the Department is specifically required to convene and lead the Workgroup on Peer Recovery Specialist Certification.

The Maryland Insurance Administration is responsible for regulating the private insurance market, including the insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations that the bill mandates to provide coverage for peer recovery specialist services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the creation of a new Workgroup on Peer Recovery Specialist Certification to study and make recommendations on the certification process and fees.

As the manager of the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, the Department of Budget and Management would be affected by mandates on health insurers that increase the cost or scope of the state's health plans.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange administers the Maryland Health Connection marketplace; mandates on insurance coverage affect the qualified health plans and dental plans offered on the exchange and their associated costs.

The Commission is responsible for health system planning and quality reporting; it may be involved in assessing the cost impact and efficacy of the expanded coverage requirements for peer recovery services.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and would be involved in the final approval of this legislation and its budgetary implications for Medicaid and the state's healthcare policy.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration regarding the implementation and enforcement of new coverage mandates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates statewide initiatives for substance abuse policy and public safety; peer recovery specialists are a key component of the state's strategy to address the opioid crisis and recidivism.

Synopsis: Altering, for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2029, the distribution of proceeds from video lottery terminals by requiring $200,000 of local impact grants distributed to Cecil County to be used for purses offered for certain races held at the Fair Hill Natural Resources Management Area.

bill_summary: This bill mandates that for fiscal years 2027 through 2029, $200,000 of the video lottery terminal local impact grants allocated to Cecil County must be used specifically for horse racing purses for races held at the Fair Hill Natural Resources Management Area.
stakeholders: Cecil County government, horse racing industry participants, and the Fair Hill Natural Resources Management Area.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill reallocates $200,000 of Cecil County's local impact grants annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2029 to be used for racing purses. There is no net change in total state or local revenues or expenditures, as the bill redirects a portion of existing grant funding rather than authorizing new spending.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is responsible for regulating the state's commercial gaming industry, including video lottery terminals (VLTs), and ensuring the proper distribution of gaming proceeds to various funds and local impact grants as modified by this bill.
The Fair Hill Natural Resources Management Area is a state-owned property managed by the DNR. The bill specifically allocates funding for horse racing purses at this location.
As the state's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller oversees the collection of state revenues and the distribution of funds, including gaming proceeds and local impact grants.
The Treasurer's Office is the principal custodian of state funds and manages the banking services and investment of public funds, including the distribution of grant money to counties.
DBM oversees the state's operating budget and ensures that taxpayer resources are allocated effectively. This bill mandates a specific allocation of grant funds over a three-year fiscal period.
The MDA promotes and protects Maryland's agricultural industry, which includes supporting the horse racing industry and equine-related economic development.

Synopsis: Expanding eligibility for a certain property tax credit in Washington County for certain disabled veterans to include certain members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service.
Title: Washington County - Property Tax Credit for Disabled Veterans - Eligibility
Status: In the House - First Reading Ways and Means
bill_summary: This bill expands the eligibility for a property tax credit in Washington County for disabled veterans to include former members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the Public Health Service (PHS).
stakeholders: Disabled veterans and former members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service in Washington County
fiscal_impact_summary: The expansion of the tax credit eligibility results in an indeterminate but likely minimal decrease in Washington County property tax revenues beginning in fiscal 2025. State finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the definition of eligibility for a property tax credit provided to disabled veterans, expanding it to include certain uniformed service members in NOAA and the Public Health Service. This aligns with the agency's primary mission as an advocate for veterans and their benefits.

Since the tax credit is specifically targeted at individuals with disabilities (disabled veterans), the Department of Disabilities is relevant due to its role in cross-disability policy leadership and advocacy for the financial independence and rights of Marylanders with disabilities.

As an independent administrative agency that adjudicates tax controversies, the Maryland Tax Court is relevant because it serves as the venue for appeals regarding tax determinations, including eligibility for property tax credits.

The PTAAB is responsible for hearing appeals related to the rejection of property tax exemptions and credits, such as the Homeowners' and Renters' Tax Credit Programs, making it a relevant entity for disputes arising from this local credit.

The OAG acts as the legal advisor to state agencies and the General Assembly. It would be involved in reviewing the legal definitions of veterans and service members to ensure the bill complies with broader state and federal legal standards.
As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation passed by the General Assembly, including local tax credit expansion bills.

The Comptroller acts as the state's fiscal watchdog and financial reporter. While property taxes are primarily managed locally, the Comptroller provides economic forecasting and monitors tax policy impacts on the state's overall fiscal health.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Wicomico County and the governing body of a municipal corporation in Wicomico County to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on certain real property owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc.

Status: In the House - First Reading Ways and Means

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Wicomico County and any municipal corporation within the county to grant a property tax credit against the local property tax for real property owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc.
responsible_party: Wicomico County Government and municipal corporations in Wicomico County
stakeholders: Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc., Wicomico County, and municipal governments within Wicomico County
fiscal_impact_summary: Wicomico County and municipal property tax revenues decrease beginning in fiscal 2025 to the extent the tax credit is granted. The magnitude of the revenue loss depends on the assessed value of the property owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc. and the specific amount of the credit authorized by local governing bodies. There is no impact on State revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the chief executive office, the Governor is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation passed by the General Assembly, including local property tax authorizations.
The Comptroller acts as the state's fiscal watchdog and monitors changes to tax law and revenue structures, including local property tax credits.
The OAG reviews legislation for legal sufficiency and constitutional compliance, providing counsel to the General Assembly on the implementation of new tax laws.
Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc. is a nonprofit dedicated to affordable housing and community revitalization, aligning directly with this department's mission and programs.
The department coordinates state land use and sustainable growth efforts; supporting local community development nonprofits via tax credits facilitates neighborhood revitalization goals.
Wicomico County is one of the 18 rural counties served by the Council, which advocates for policies that improve economic sustainability and the quality of life in rural communities.
This office partners with nonprofits and community organizations to address local needs such as housing and poverty, making the financial health of local housing NGOs relevant to its mission.

The office works to eliminate childhood poverty and improve family well-being; access to stable, affordable housing provided by organizations like Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services is a critical component of this mission.
The team focuses on data-driven solutions for economic mobility and childhood poverty; housing stability programs supported by this credit are foundational to long-term economic opportunity.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain on-site interview following a report of suspected child abuse to be with the child's parent or guardian rather than the child's caretaker; and requiring a local department of social services or a law enforcement agency to provide a certain notice to a parent or legal guardian of a child at a certain time during an investigation of suspected child abuse or neglect.
Title: Family Law - Child Abuse and Neglect Investigations ("Know Before They Knock" Family Right to Notice Act)
Status: In the House - First Reading Judiciary
bill_summary: This bill, known as the 'Know Before They Knock' Family Right to Notice Act, requires local departments of social services or law enforcement agencies to provide parents or legal guardians with a written notice of their rights and available resources at the start of a child abuse or neglect investigation. It also specifies that certain on-site interviews following a report of suspected abuse must be conducted with the child's parent or guardian rather than a caretaker.
responsible_party: Local departments of social services and law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Parents, legal guardians, children, social workers, and law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal fiscal impact. Local departments of social services and law enforcement agencies may incur minor administrative costs to develop and distribute the required written notices, which can likely be absorbed within existing resources. There is no significant impact on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services oversees the local departments of social services that are primarily responsible for investigating reports of suspected child abuse and neglect. This bill directly dictates the procedures and notice requirements these departments must follow during on-site interviews and investigations.

The bill explicitly names law enforcement agencies as entities that must provide specific notices to parents or legal guardians during investigations of suspected child abuse or neglect. As a primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police will be directly impacted by these procedural mandates.

The bill changes the protocol for on-site interviews, which often take place in public schools or child care facilities regulated by the Department of Education. Requiring interviews with parents/guardians rather than school-based caretakers significantly alters the investigative process within these educational environments.

As the agency responsible for aligning the efforts of state departments to improve child well-being and coordinate policy action for families, the Governor's Office for Children has a direct interest in legislation that impacts family rights and child welfare investigation protocols.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the legal advisor to the Department of Human Services and the Maryland State Police. It would be responsible for providing guidance on the implementation of these new notice requirements and defending the agencies in potential litigation regarding procedural compliance.

Child abuse and neglect investigations frequently result in Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) cases in the judicial system. The Administrative Office of the Courts must ensure the judiciary is prepared for the legal implications of these new investigative procedural rights for families.

The bill imposes new administrative duties on state agencies, specifically regarding the timing and delivery of legal notices. This may have a fiscal impact on agency operations, staffing needs, and training budgets, which are managed and overseen by DBM.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the state’s hub for criminal justice policy and victim services. Because child abuse is both a criminal matter and a child welfare issue, the office's policy development and grant management for victim support may be impacted by these changes in investigative procedures.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested findings of child abuse and neglect. If an investigation fails to follow the statutory notice requirements established by this bill, it could become a central procedural issue in administrative appeals filed by parents or guardians.

The Governor's Office oversees the operations of all state departments, including those tasked with child protective services. The Governor would be responsible for signing this bill into law and ensuring the relevant executive agencies comply with the new statutory mandates.

Synopsis: Requiring the Patuxent Institution and each State and local correctional facility to maintain records on instances of items damaged or destroyed due to visible leakage of menstrual discharge under certain circumstances; prohibiting the Patuxent Institution and each State and local correctional facility from subjecting female incarcerated individuals to disciplinary measures for items damaged or destroyed without malicious intent due to visible leakage of menstrual discharge; etc.
Title: Correctional Services - Incarcerated Individuals - Menstrual Hygiene
Status: In the House - First Reading Government, Labor, and Elections
bill_summary: This bill requires State and local correctional facilities, including the Patuxent Institution, to develop and implement a menstrual hygiene policy that provides products to incarcerated individuals at no cost. It prohibits disciplinary action against individuals for items damaged by menstrual leakage without malicious intent and requires facilities to maintain records of such occurrences.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and local correctional facilities
stakeholders: Female incarcerated individuals in State and local correctional facilities, correctional administrators, and staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures may increase minimally to provide additional menstrual hygiene products and to cover administrative costs associated with record-keeping. No impact on state or local revenues is expected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for managing Maryland’s adult correctional system and the Patuxent Institution, DPSCS is the lead implementer of this bill. It will be required to update disciplinary protocols and establish record-keeping systems for damaged items related to menstrual hygiene.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to nearly all state agencies, including DPSCS. It would provide legal guidance on the implementation of these new correctional standards and handle any civil appeals or legal challenges regarding disciplinary measures.

DBM is responsible for the state's annual budget and fiscal accountability. This bill may have a fiscal impact related to the administrative costs of record-keeping and the replacement of state property (linens and uniforms) destroyed by leakage.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the state’s central hub for public safety policy and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies. This bill’s focus on correctional services and inmate treatment falls within its oversight of statewide justice policy.

MCCR investigates complaints of discrimination and ensures equal opportunity. Prohibiting disciplinary measures for gender-specific biological functions (menstruation) within state facilities is relevant to the commission’s mission to ensure equitable treatment for all residents.

The Governor's Office oversees all executive departments and signs or vetoes legislation. It is responsible for ensuring that correctional policies implemented by DPSCS align with the Governor’s broader initiatives for public safety and humane treatment.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain persons to bring an action when the owner of a property that includes a cemetery proposes the sale, transfer, or alternate use of all or part of a certain cemetery; and requiring a court to take certain actions under certain circumstances.
