bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance carriers to notify the Maryland Insurance Commissioner and affected enrollees when a material change occurs in their provider network, specifically involving a health system's departure. It mandates health systems to comply with notice requirements for contract terminations and establishes a special enrollment period for enrollees whose access to a health system is impacted by such changes.
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, health systems, and insured Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange are expected to implement the bill using existing resources. There is no significant impact on state or local revenues, though minor administrative costs may be incurred to oversee the new notification requirements and special enrollment periods.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is the primary regulator for the state's insurance industry. The bill explicitly alters notification requirements that carriers must provide to the Insurance Commissioner regarding material changes to provider panels and oversees carrier compliance with notice of contract terminations.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) administers Maryland Health Connection. Material changes to provider networks often trigger Special Enrollment Periods (SEPs), which the Exchange must manage to ensure residents can transition to new plans if their providers leave a network.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the legal advisor to the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Department of Health. Its Consumer Protection Division also has an interest in ensuring enrollees receive timely and accurate notifications regarding changes to their healthcare access.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) oversees health systems and public health services. Significant contract terminations between carriers and health systems can disrupt patient care coordination and impact the accessibility of services across the state.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) manages the state's central payroll and the health benefits program for over 100,000 state employees. Material changes to the networks of carriers providing state employee benefits directly impact the health coverage options for the state's workforce.

Synopsis: Authorizing a licensed certified social worker-clinical to provide evaluation services for workers' compensation claims related to permanent impairments involving a behavioral or mental disorder; and requiring a licensed certified social worker-clinical to meet certain requirements to perform the evaluation services.
Title: Workers' Compensation - Evaluation of Permanent Impairments - Licensed Social Worker-Clinical
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Finance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes licensed certified social workers-clinical (LCSW-C) to perform evaluations of permanent impairments for workers' compensation claims involving behavioral or mental disorders, provided they meet certain requirements.
stakeholders: Licensed certified social workers-clinical (LCSW-C), workers' compensation claimants with mental or behavioral health impairments, employers, and workers' compensation insurers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect state or local finances. While it expands the pool of authorized professionals who can conduct specific impairment evaluations, it does not mandate additional state expenditures or generate new state revenue.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission is the primary regulator and adjudicator of the Workers' Compensation Act. This bill directly modifies the administrative rules for evidence by expanding the types of healthcare providers allowed to perform impairment evaluations for behavioral or mental disorders in their proceedings.

As the largest writer of workers' compensation insurance in Maryland and the insurer for state employees, this agency will be directly responsible for processing and paying for evaluations performed by licensed social workers-clinical under the new law.

The Treasurer's Office manages the State Insurance Trust Fund, which provides workers' compensation coverage for all state employees. Authorizing new providers to conduct impairment evaluations could affect the fiscal management and risk assessment of state employee claims.

The SIF evaluates permanent impairments to determine liability in cases involving pre-existing disabilities. Expanding the pool of eligible evaluators to include LCSW-Cs will directly impact their investigation and evaluation of complex behavioral health claims.

The MIA regulates the private insurance market in Maryland, including workers' compensation insurers. They oversee the financial impact of changes in claims processing and medical evaluation standards on insurance rates and carrier solvency.

The Maryland Department of Health houses the professional boards responsible for the licensing and regulation of Licensed Certified Social Workers-Clinical (LCSW-Cs). The bill establishes specific professional requirements that these clinicians must meet to perform the evaluations.
DBM oversees the state's personnel system and the annual budget. They are relevant due to the potential fiscal impact on workers' compensation expenditures for the state workforce.

bill_summary: This bill allows three specific offices within the Baltimore City Mayor's Office—Neighborhood Safety and Engagement, Children and Family Success, and African American Male Engagement—to access and use confidential juvenile police and court records for the purpose of providing services to the child who is the subject of the record or the child's family.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Neighborhood Safety and Engagement, the Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Children and Family Success, and the Baltimore City Mayor's Office of African American Male Engagement
stakeholders: Juveniles and families in Baltimore City involved in the juvenile justice system, Baltimore City government offices, and Maryland state agencies managing juvenile records.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no significant fiscal impact on State or local revenues or expenditures, as the administrative responsibilities for providing record access can be managed with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly addresses the confidentiality and authorized access of juvenile police and court records, which are central to the department's mandate of managing youth involved in the juvenile justice system and their rehabilitative records.
The bill impacts the confidentiality laws surrounding court records, which the AOC is responsible for managing and maintaining as the central administrative arm of the Maryland Judiciary.

The bill concerns access to juvenile police records; as a primary statewide law enforcement agency, the MSP generates and maintains these records and must adhere to legal standards for their dissemination.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's central hub for public safety policy and youth-involved justice programs, this agency is relevant to legislation expanding local government access to data for crime prevention and neighborhood safety initiatives.

The bill grants record access to the Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Children and Family Success, aligning with the Governor's Office for Children's mission to coordinate whole-of-government approaches to child well-being and economic mobility.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS), which is the primary repository for criminal records in Maryland, and would be involved if the access granted by this bill involves CJIS data protocols.
The OAG serves as the primary legal advisor to state agencies and would oversee the legal implications of modifying state laws regarding record confidentiality and inter-jurisdictional data sharing.

Synopsis: Establishing the Ibogaine Clinical Research Grant Program to provide grants to certain research institutions to conduct certain clinical drug development trials on the use of ibogaine; and including the Program as an authorized use of funding from the Opioid Restitution Fund.
Title: Public Health - Ibogaine Clinical Research Grant Program - Establishment (Veterans Mental Health Innovations Act)
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Finance
bill_summary: This bill establishes the Ibogaine Clinical Research Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health to provide grants to research institutions for clinical drug development trials on the use of ibogaine in treating post-traumatic stress disorder, traumatic brain injury, and substance use disorders, specifically targeting the needs of veterans. The program is authorized to receive funding from the Opioid Restitution Fund.
stakeholders: Veterans, research institutions, and individuals suffering from PTSD, traumatic brain injury, or substance use disorders.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $32,583 in FY 2025 for a part-time administrator. Special fund expenditures from the Opioid Restitution Fund are estimated to increase by between $500,000 and $1,000,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2029 to provide research grants. There is no impact on local revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for public health and substance use disorder services. It would most likely be the state entity tasked with establishing the Ibogaine Clinical Research Grant Program and overseeing the clinical drug development trials.

The bill is titled the 'Veterans Mental Health Innovations Act' and focuses on research that could provide mental health treatments for veterans. The agency acts as an advocate and resource hub for veterans' healthcare needs.

DBM oversees the state's operating budget and the allocation of funds. This bill specifically adds the grant program as an authorized use of the Opioid Restitution Fund, requiring fiscal oversight and coordination.

The grant program is designed to fund clinical trials at research institutions. Universities within the System, such as the University of Maryland, Baltimore, are primary candidates to conduct this medical and clinical research.

The Governor's Office oversees all state departments and leads statewide initiatives. This bill creates a new public health program and directs the use of opioid settlement funds, which are high-priority executive policy areas.
As a public urban research university, Morgan State would be an eligible research institution to apply for and receive grants under this clinical research program.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like the Department of Health and has a significant role in managing the legal aspects and implementation of the Opioid Restitution Fund.
The Comptroller serves as the state's fiscal watchdog and would be involved in the accounting and disbursement of grants from the Opioid Restitution Fund.
The Treasurer's Office manages the state's banking and investment of funds, including the Opioid Restitution Fund from which these grants would be distributed.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits video streaming services from broadcasting commercial advertisements at a volume louder than the main video content being viewed. It establishes that compliance with federal loudness regulations constitutes compliance with this state law and classifies violations as unfair or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Maryland consumers and video streaming service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes that a violation is subject to the enforcement and penalty provisions of the Maryland Consumer Protection Act. While the provided text does not specify exact dollar amounts, such provisions typically result in potential civil penalties credited to the State's general fund and administrative costs for the Office of the Attorney General to handle complaints and enforcement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly states that a violation of the act is subject to enforcement under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division is the primary state entity responsible for enforcing these laws, investigating complaints regarding unfair or deceptive trade practices, and ensuring businesses comply with advertising standards.

As the chief executive office, the Governor is responsible for signing or vetoing this legislation and oversees the general enforcement of state laws. The office also coordinates statewide initiatives that improve public safety and consumer welfare.

Enforcement actions initiated by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General may result in contested cases. The Office of Administrative Hearings would provide the impartial Administrative Law Judges necessary to adjudicate these disputes between the state and video streaming services.

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland public senior higher education institutions and community colleges to report annually on student contraception access to the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC). It further mandates that community colleges provide students with access to all methods of over-the-counter contraception and requires MHEC to submit a consolidated annual report to the General Assembly.
stakeholders: Students at public senior higher education institutions and community colleges in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases state and local expenditures because the Maryland Higher Education Commission must collect and process annual reports, and community colleges are required to provide access to over-the-counter contraception methods. The fiscal impact on community colleges varies depending on how access is provided, such as through vending machines or campus health centers. No direct impact on state revenues is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary agency responsible for receiving annual reports from higher education institutions and community colleges regarding contraception access, and it must compile these into a yearly report for the General Assembly.

As the umbrella organization for the state's public senior higher education institutions, USM's member universities are directly required to submit reports to MHEC and potentially modify student access to contraception.
As a public senior higher education institution, Morgan State is directly mandated by the bill to submit annual reports on contraception access to MHEC.
As a public senior higher education institution, St. Mary's College is directly mandated by the bill to submit annual reports on contraception access to MHEC.
MDH oversees public health and may be consulted on the types and standards of over-the-counter contraception that community colleges are required to provide under this legislation.
DBM oversees the fiscal performance and budget allocations for the state-funded higher education institutions and MHEC, which will incur operational and reporting costs under the bill.
The OAG acts as legal counsel for the Maryland Higher Education Commission and the state's public universities, advising them on compliance with the new reporting and access mandates.

Synopsis: Altering the annual salary of the Sheriff of Frederick County to be $175,000 for calendar year 2027; and altering the annual salary of the Sheriff of Frederick County to be 82.5% of the State's Attorney for Frederick County's annual salary including any increments and salary adjustments authorized under certain provisions of law for calendar year 2028 and each subsequent calendar year.

Status: In the Senate - First Reading Judicial Proceedings
bill_summary: This bill establishes the annual salary of the Sheriff of Frederick County at $175,000 for calendar year 2027. Beginning in calendar year 2028 and for each subsequent year, the salary will be adjusted to 82.5% of the Frederick County State's Attorney's annual salary, including any authorized increments and adjustments.
stakeholders: The Sheriff of Frederick County and the residents of Frederick County
fiscal_impact_summary: Frederick County expenditures will increase starting in fiscal 2027 to cover the increased salary and associated fringe benefits for the Sheriff. The exact fiscal impact in 2028 and subsequent years will depend on salary adjustments made for the Frederick County State's Attorney.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the Sheriff is a member of the state retirement and pension system, altering their annual salary directly impacts pensionable earnings, employer/employee contributions, and future benefit calculations managed by the agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office serves as the state's central hub for public safety policy and advises on criminal justice strategies; changes to the compensation structure of a lead county law enforcement official fall within its policy interest.

Sheriffs perform essential functions for the judiciary, including providing court security and serving legal process. Compensation for these officers is relevant to the AOC’s role in supporting the efficient operation of the court system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS coordinates closely with local sheriffs on public safety, prisoner transport, and offender management; the statutory compensation of these key local partners is relevant to the agency's broad mission.
The Governor’s Office is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation passed by the General Assembly, including statutory changes to the salaries of local constitutional officers.

The OAG provides legal counsel on legislation and constitutional matters; linking the Sheriff's salary to that of the State's Attorney (another constitutional officer) involves legal frameworks the OAG may be called upon to review.

The Sheriff is an elected constitutional officer; changes to the compensation or terms of the office are relevant to the agency that manages the certification and oversight of elections for such positions.
As the state's central fiscal authority, DBM evaluates the fiscal impact of legislation on both state and local governments and oversees personnel-related fiscal reporting.

The Maryland State Police is the primary statewide law enforcement partner to county sheriffs; adjustments to the compensation of lead local law enforcement peers are of secondary interest to the agency.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the requirement that private home detention monitoring agencies must notify the designated law enforcement agency when a person violates a condition of their home detention monitoring under specific circumstances.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Private home detention monitoring agencies, law enforcement agencies, and individuals subject to home detention monitoring.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal fiscal impact on state and local operations. It primarily removes an administrative reporting requirement for private monitoring agencies, which may result in a negligible reduction in administrative workload for law enforcement agencies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary agency responsible for managing pretrial detention and community supervision. In Maryland, this department also oversees the licensing and regulation of private home detention monitoring agencies, making it the central regulatory body for the entities affected by this bill.

The bill repeals the requirement for private monitoring agencies to notify law enforcement of certain violations. As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the MSP is directly impacted by changes in communication protocols regarding potential criminal activity or violations of court-ordered monitoring.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the state's hub for public safety policy and funding. A change in the notification process for home detention violations affects statewide criminal justice strategies and public safety protocols which fall under its advisory and policy mission.

The judiciary often orders home detention as a condition of pretrial release or sentencing. Changes to how violations are reported impact the administration of court orders and the information available to judges regarding a defendant's compliance with those orders.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents indigent individuals who are frequently placed on home detention. Repealing notification requirements for certain violations could impact the legal status and defense of their clients during violation of probation or pretrial hearings.

The OAG serves as the primary legal advisor to state agencies, including DPSCS. They would be responsible for providing counsel on the implementation of these changes and managing any related civil or criminal appeals involving home detention regulation.

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Youth Delinquency Prevention Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to provide grants to local governments and community-based organizations for programs and services aimed at reducing youth delinquency and improving outcomes for at-risk youth.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
stakeholders: Local governments, community-based non-profit organizations, and youth at risk of or involved in the juvenile justice system.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2026 due to a mandated appropriation to the fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy increase by at least $500,000 annually as funds are received and distributed via grants. Local government revenues and expenditures increase to the extent that they apply for and receive grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for the management, supervision, and rehabilitation of youth involved in the juvenile justice system, DJS is a central stakeholder in delinquency prevention efforts and would likely be a primary beneficiary or partner in the programs supported by this fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency serves as the state’s central hub for public safety funding and grant administration. It would likely be the agency tasked with managing the Youth Delinquency Prevention Fund and distributing grants to local governments or nonprofits.

DBM is responsible for the state's annual operating budget and fiscal accountability. The establishment of a new state fund requires DBM oversight to ensure proper allocation and management of taxpayer resources.

The GOC leads a 'whole-of-government' approach to youth well-being and childhood poverty. Delinquency prevention is a key component of their mission to improve long-term economic and social outcomes for vulnerable children.

The State Treasurer's Office is the principal custodian of state financial assets and manages the investment of public funds. Any new state fund would be established under its financial oversight and banking management.

As the state's chief financial officer and fiscal watchdog, the Comptroller oversees the collection of revenues and the reporting of state financial health, including the tracking of specific state-administered funds.

The Governor’s Office oversees all state departments and signs or vetoes legislation. Enhancing public safety and addressing childhood poverty are top executive priorities that would be impacted by the creation of this fund.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies. They would likely assist in drafting the regulations for the new fund and ensuring its administration complies with state and federal law.

The agency's mission involves stimulating private investment and job creation. Supporting workforce events and job fairs aligns with their economic development goals.

Title: Public Health - Food and Milk Product Labeling - Requirements
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Finance

Synopsis: Requiring a unit of State and local government and a person that receives funding from the State operating or capital budget to report on or before October 15 each year to the Comptroller certain information regarding the use of the funds; requiring a certain individual or corporation that receives payments from a unit of State and local government for providing goods or services to the unit to include certain information on the individual's or corporation's income tax return or declaration; etc.
Title: Recipients of State and Local Government Funding - Reporting (Buy Maryland Reporting Requirements)
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Budget and Taxation

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland State and local government units, as well as any person or entity receiving funding from the State operating or capital budget, to submit an annual report to the Comptroller by October 15 regarding the usage of those funds. Additionally, individuals or corporations that receive payments from government units for goods or services are required to include information about those payments on their income tax returns or declarations.
stakeholders: State and local government units, individuals and entities receiving State budget funding, and contractors providing goods or services to Maryland government entities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for collecting the reports mandated by this bill and administering the changes to income tax returns and declarations required for corporations and individuals receiving state funds.

DBM serves as the state's central fiscal authority and oversees the operating budget; as the bill requires reporting on the use of these funds, DBM is critical to the bill's fiscal accountability and budget management goals.

DGS is the central procurement and logistics agency for the state; the bill's focus on reporting payments for goods and services directly impacts DGS's management of state contracts and business oversight.

The BPW reviews and approves major state expenditures and procurement contracts; this bill establishes reporting requirements for the specific funds and recipients the Board oversees, enhancing their role as a fiscal watchdog.

DoIT manages the state's strategic IT infrastructure and will likely be responsible for the digital systems and cybersecurity standards necessary to facilitate the annual electronic reporting of funding usage.

OLA is responsible for auditing state agencies for fiscal compliance; it will be tasked with verifying the accuracy of the new funding reports and ensuring adherence to the legal mandates created by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the monitor of state procurement participation goals, this office is directly impacted by requirements to track and report on the recipients of state funds, particularly to ensure transparency in local business opportunities.

The bill's 'Buy Maryland' focus aligns with the Department's mission to stimulate the local economy and support Maryland businesses; the reported data will provide critical insights into domestic spending.
As one of the state's largest agencies by budget and procurement volume, MDOT will be significantly impacted by the requirement to report on its extensive use of state operating and capital funds.

The Governor's Office oversees all state departments and the budget process; it will be responsible for ensuring that all executive branch units comply with the new annual reporting mandates by the October deadline.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the Comptroller and nearly all state agencies; it will provide legal counsel on the implementation of the bill's reporting requirements and regulatory compliance.

The Treasurer is the custodian of state funds and sits on the Board of Public Works; the office is relevant to the oversight and management of the public funds subject to the bill's new reporting requirements.

Synopsis: Requiring that a court determine custody before awarding child support under certain circumstances; and establishing a conclusive presumption that the application of the child support guidelines would be unjust or inappropriate if the parents mutually assert that the agreement is in the best interest of the child.
Title: Family Law - Child Support - Determination of Custody and Agreements Between Parents
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Judicial Proceedings
bill_summary: This bill requires a court to determine child custody before awarding child support in certain circumstances. It also establishes a conclusive presumption that the standard child support guidelines are unjust or inappropriate if parents mutually agree to a child support amount and assert that the agreement is in the best interest of the child.
stakeholders: Parents and children involved in custody and child support legal proceedings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services (DHS) manages the Child Support Administration (CSA), which is directly responsible for the implementation of child support guidelines and the collection and distribution of payments. This bill's changes to child support determination and parent agreements directly impact their core functions.

The Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC) oversees judicial policies and court resources. Since this bill mandates specific court procedures for determining custody before awarding child support and introduces a new conclusive presumption for judges to apply, it significantly impacts judicial operations and family law proceedings.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) serves as the primary legal advisor to state agencies, including DHS. They would be responsible for interpreting the legal implications of the bill's changes and defending state policies related to the Child Support Administration.

The Governor's Office for Children leads the state's 'whole-of-government' approach to child well-being and reducing childhood poverty. Changes to child support laws are critical to the financial stability of children and families, which is a central part of their mission.

The Governor's Office oversees all state departments and spearheads initiatives aimed at child well-being and economic opportunity. As the bill addresses child support and custody—key factors in family stability—it falls under their broad policy oversight and executive mandate.

Synopsis: Requiring certain facilities to inform individuals of certain rights relating to the participation of a family member or other authorized individual in the individual's plan of treatment; requiring facilities to recognize certain documents as an individual's formal request to allow a certain individual to participate in a certain plan; limiting the reasons for which a treating provider is authorized to withhold information on an individual's plan of treatment from certain third parties; etc.
Title: Mental Health - Treatment Plans for Individuals in Facilities - Participation of Family Members or Other Individuals
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Finance
bill_summary: This bill requires mental health facilities to notify patients upon admission of their right to involve family members or other authorized individuals in their treatment planning. Facilities must recognize documents such as advance directives as formal requests for this participation and are restricted from withholding treatment plan information from authorized third parties except under specific clinical or safety circumstances.
stakeholders: Individuals receiving mental health treatment in facilities, family members of patients, authorized patient representatives, and mental health facility administrators.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has a minimal impact on State expenditures, primarily involving costs for the Maryland Department of Health to update regulations and forms. There is no significant impact on local government finances or state revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency responsible for behavioral health services and the licensing and regulatory oversight of healthcare facilities. This bill directly impacts the operational procedures and patient rights within facilities that MDH oversees and regulates.

The Department of Disabilities serves as a cross-disability policy leader and advocates for the rights, choice, and independence of individuals with disabilities, including those with mental health conditions. Ensuring patient participation in treatment planning is a core policy interest for the agency.

The Maryland Department of Aging advocates for older adults and manages the Long-Term Care Ombudsman program. This bill is relevant as it affects the rights of older adults in facilities regarding the participation of family members in their mental health treatment plans.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal advisor to state agencies, including MDH. It would be responsible for interpreting the legal requirements for recognizing formal documents and ensuring that facility policies comply with state and federal law.

DHS oversees adult and child welfare services, including protective services for vulnerable individuals. The agency often works with individuals in facilities and coordinates with family members or guardians who would be authorized to participate in treatment plans.

DJS is responsible for the rehabilitation and treatment of youth in secure and community-based facilities. To the extent that 'certain facilities' includes juvenile facilities, DJS would need to update its intake and treatment protocols to allow for family participation as specified.

The OAH is responsible for resolving contested cases for the Department of Health. If an individual or authorized family member challenges a facility's failure to recognize their right to participate in a treatment plan, the OAH may be the forum for adjudication.

The Governor's Office oversees the operations of all state departments and leads statewide initiatives related to public health and mental health. This bill aligns with the office's mission to improve public well-being and oversee agency compliance.

The Commission on Civil Rights enforces anti-discrimination laws in public accommodations and state programs. Withholding information or excluding authorized individuals from treatment plans could potentially involve issues related to equal access and civil rights.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition against a surrogate authorizing treatment for a mental disorder for a person who has been certified to be incapable of making an informed decision.
Title: Health Care Decisions Act - Surrogate Decision Making - Mental Disorders
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Finance
bill_summary: This bill repeals the prohibition that previously prevented a surrogate decision-maker from authorizing treatment for a mental disorder for an individual certified as incapable of making an informed decision, thereby allowing surrogates to provide consent for such care.
stakeholders: Surrogate decision-makers, patients with mental disorders who are incapable of making informed decisions, and healthcare providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no material impact on state or local government revenues or expenditures, as it modifies legal protocols for surrogate decision-making.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for behavioral health and medical regulation, the Department of Health is responsible for the oversight and implementation of the Health Care Decisions Act in clinical settings, especially regarding treatment for mental disorders.

The OAG provides the legal interpretation and guidance for the Health Care Decisions Act, advising state agencies and medical practitioners on the lawful exercise of surrogate decision-making authority.

Older adults frequently rely on surrogate decision-makers or public guardianship; this bill directly impacts the scope of treatment authorization available for seniors with mental health conditions or cognitive decline.

This bill significantly impacts individuals with disabilities who may lack the capacity to make informed medical decisions, altering the policy for how their mental health treatment is authorized by surrogates.
The Judiciary manages guardianship proceedings and provides public resources through court help centers that will be affected by changes to the legal standards for surrogate healthcare authorization.
DHS manages adult protective services and cases involving vulnerable residents whose mental health care is often coordinated through surrogate or representative decision-makers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents indigent clients in mental health and involuntary commitment proceedings where the authority of a surrogate to override individual autonomy for treatment is a critical legal issue.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive agencies implementing the law and holds the constitutional authority to sign or veto legislation affecting patient rights and surrogate responsibilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department manages healthcare for incarcerated individuals, and changes to surrogate decision-making laws impact the protocols for treating inmates with mental disorders who lack decision-making capacity.
DJS provides mental health services to youth in the juvenile justice system and must align its treatment authorization protocols with state laws regarding surrogate decision-making.

Synopsis: Requiring certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide individuals with salpingectomy coverage for ovarian cancer prevention; and prohibiting the insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from imposing a copayment, coinsurance, or deductible requirement on the salpingectomy coverage.
Title: Health Insurance - Ovarian Cancer Prevention With Salpingectomy - Required Coverage and Prohibited Cost Sharing
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Finance

Synopsis: Establishing the Suitland Development Authority in Prince George's County; requiring the Authority to support and develop a certain neighborhood revitalization plan in coordination with certain residents; authorizing the Authority to modify certain boundaries, subject to a certain vote; requiring the Authority to take certain actions regarding the finances of the Authority; and exempting the Authority from certain taxation or assessments under certain circumstances.
Title: Economic Development - Prince George's County Suitland Development Authority - Established
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Finance

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Suitland Development Authority in Prince George's County to support and develop a neighborhood revitalization plan for the Suitland area. The Authority is required to coordinate with residents, manage its own finances, and is granted tax-exempt status for its operations and properties.
stakeholders: Residents and business owners in Suitland, Prince George's County, and the Prince George's County government.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Authority is exempt from state and local taxes, which may impact county revenue. Prince George's County will likely experience increased expenditures to support the Authority's revitalization activities and administrative functions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill focuses on neighborhood revitalization and community development in the Suitland area, which aligns directly with DHCD's primary mission to revitalize neighborhoods and expand access to sustainable housing.
As the state's primary economic development agency, Commerce is relevant to the establishment of a new development authority intended to stimulate investment and job creation.
The bill involves a neighborhood revitalization plan and boundary modifications, falling under the Department of Planning's role in coordinating sustainable growth and land use.
The bill includes exemptions from certain taxes and assessments for the new Authority, which falls under the Comptroller's purview as the state's tax collector and fiscal watchdog.
The Treasurer's Office oversees the fiscal management of public instrumentalities and safeguards state financial assets, making it relevant to the Authority's financial requirements.
The Governor's Office oversees the creation of state-authorized entities and enforces the laws governing state departments and agencies that will interact with this new Authority.
The BPW reviews and approves significant state expenditures and the acquisition or sale of property, which may be relevant if the Authority receives state funding or deals with state assets.
The OAG serves as the legal advisor for state agencies and would likely provide counsel regarding the legal establishment and regulatory compliance of the new Authority.
The bill requires the Authority to take specific financial and auditing actions; OLA is the agency responsible for auditing state-authorized entities to ensure fiscal compliance.
MEDCO is a quasi-public agency that performs similar economic development functions and may serve as a partner or model for the newly established Suitland Development Authority.
The synopsis mentions ethics as a subject; the commission would be responsible for ensuring the Authority's board and employees comply with the Maryland Public Ethics Law.
The Office of Appointments would be responsible for recruiting and vetting candidates if the Governor is tasked with appointing members to the Authority's board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Economic development and neighborhood revitalization projects often involve procurement goals for small, minority, and women-owned businesses, which this office oversees.

Synopsis: Reestablishing the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland with an altered membership and mandate.
Title: Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland - Reestablishment
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Education, Energy, and the Environment

Synopsis: Repealing provisions of law related to the Baltimore City Public School Board Community Panel; and altering the process for appointments to the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners to require that appointed members and members appointed to fill a vacancy of an appointed or elected member are subject to confirmation by the Senate of Maryland.
Title: Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners - Appointment Process - Alterations
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Education, Energy, and the Environment

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: The bill repeals the Baltimore City Public School Board Community Panel and requires that all Mayoral appointments to the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, including those made to fill vacancies for both elected and appointed members, must be confirmed by the Maryland Senate.
responsible_party: Mayor of Baltimore and the Maryland Senate
stakeholders: Baltimore City Public School System, the Mayor of Baltimore, the Maryland Senate, and Baltimore City residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no fiscal impact on State or local government revenues or expenditures as it only modifies administrative procedures for board appointments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's chief executive, the Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing this legislation and oversees the state's executive appointment process, which this bill directly alters.
The OAG serves as the primary legal advisor to the state and will oversee the legal and constitutional implications of altering board appointment processes and Senate confirmation requirements.
DBM acts as the state's central fiscal authority and would manage any potential fiscal impacts or administrative cost changes associated with the board's restructuring and appointment procedures.

MSDE oversees Maryland's public K-12 education system, including the Baltimore City Public School System. Changes to local school board governance directly impact their regulatory and policy oversight.

The GOC leads whole-of-government efforts for child well-being. Changes to the leadership of the state's largest school system affect their mission to reduce childhood poverty and improve educational outcomes.
This office is primarily responsible for recruiting and vetting candidates for state-regulated boards. The bill directly changes the appointment and confirmation process they manage.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Baltimore City Public School Board Community Panel, which falls under this designation of specialized advisory bodies created to address public concerns.
The IAC coordinates capital funding and infrastructure for local schools; changes in the governance of the Baltimore City board may affect ongoing capital improvement project coordination.
The MSA manages significant school modernization programs in Baltimore City, such as 'Built to Learn.' Restructuring the school board impacts their primary local partner in these projects.
Because the bill addresses the process for filling vacancies of both appointed and elected members, the SBE is relevant to the oversight of the hybrid board's electoral integrity.
This unit focuses on economic mobility and childhood poverty in Baltimore; school board governance is a critical component of their data-driven strategy for the city's residents.

The PERB oversees collective bargaining and labor relations for public school employees. Changes to the Board of School Commissioners alter the primary leadership body with whom they interact on labor disputes.

Synopsis: Altering the duties of the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council; establishing the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program in the Maryland Department of Health to lead the State's public health efforts relating to brain health and dementia; requiring the Director of Dementia Services and Brain Health to administer the Program; requiring the Program, rather than the Director, to perform certain duties and staff the Council; etc.
Title: Health - Dementia Services and Brain Health Program and Clinical Toolkit
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Finance

Synopsis: Requiring the Public Service Commission to authorize certain rate consolidations involving two or more water systems or sewage disposal systems; requiring the Commission to allow water companies, sewage disposal companies, and water and sewage disposal companies to aggregate certain revenues and costs for certain purposes; authorizing the Commission to order gradual adjustments to certain rates charged to a system over a certain time period; etc.
Title: Water Companies, Sewage Disposal Companies, and Water and Sewage Disposal Companies - Rate Consolidation and Limited-Income Mechanisms
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Education, Energy, and the Environment
